title: Strong Coupling In A Three-mode Superconducting-spin Hybrid Quantum System
authors: Yingqiu Mao, Han-Yu Ren, Zi-Yi Liu, Yi-Zheng Zhen, Tao Rong, Tao Jiang, Zhuo Chen, Zhe-Heng Yuan, Wen-Hua Qin, Xiaoran Zhang, Xiaobing Liu, Ming Gong, Kae Nemoto, William J. Munro, And Johannes Majer
abstract:
Author(s): Yingqiu Mao, Han-Yu Ren, Zi-Yi Liu, Yi-Zheng Zhen, Tao Rong, Tao Jiang, Zhuo Chen, Zhe-Heng Yuan, Wen-Hua Qin, Xiaoran Zhang, Xiaobing Liu, Ming Gong, Kae Nemoto, William J. Munro, and Johannes Majer

We demonstrate strong coupling in a solid-state hybrid quantum system comprising a fixed-frequency coplanar-waveguide resonator, a superconducting transmon qubit, and an ensemble of nitrogen-vacancy centers in diamond. Frequency-domain spectroscopy reveals a characteristic three-mode avoided crossin…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023343] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates strong coupling in a three-mode hybrid system of a superconducting transmon qubit, a coplanar-waveguide resonator, and an NV center ensemble.
motivation: Hybrid quantum systems combining superconducting qubits with spin ensembles are promising for quantum information processing, but achieving strong coupling in multi-mode configurations is challenging.
method: The authors fabricate a device with a fixed-frequency coplanar-waveguide resonator, a transmon qubit, and an NV center ensemble, and perform frequency-domain spectroscopy to observe avoided crossings.
result: They observe characteristic three-mode avoided crossings, indicating strong coupling between all three components, and extract coupling strengths and system parameters.
conclusion: This work demonstrates a viable platform for hybrid quantum systems with strong coupling, enabling future applications in quantum memory and transduction.

title: Reassessing The Boundary Between Classical And Nonclassical For Individual Quantum Processes
authors: Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, And Robert W. Spekkens
abstract:
Author(s): Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, and Robert W. Spekkens

Researchers have proposed a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, recovering many standard signatures of quantumness while revealing that many phenomena long thought to be classical actually possess hidden, intrinsically quantum properties that could power future technologies.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021050] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, revealing hidden quantum properties in phenomena previously thought classical.
motivation: To resolve ambiguities in defining quantumness for individual processes and to uncover nonclassical features that could enable new technologies.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework based on process matrices and operational probabilistic theories, introducing a criterion that separates classical and nonclassical processes.
result: The unified rule recovers standard quantum signatures and identifies intrinsically quantum properties in many processes previously considered classical.
conclusion: The boundary between classical and quantum is broader than previously thought, with implications for quantum information processing and foundational studies.

title: Fast Thermalization With Quantum Algorithms
authors: Anirban Chowdhury
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 03 July 2026;
tldr: A quantum algorithm efficiently prepares thermal equilibrium states, advancing quantum simulation.
motivation: Preparing thermal states is crucial for quantum simulation but computationally hard; this work provides an efficient algorithm for an important class of thermal states.
method: The algorithm leverages quantum signal processing and Hamiltonian simulation to prepare Gibbs states with provable efficiency.
result: The algorithm achieves polynomial scaling in system size and inverse temperature, outperforming classical methods.
conclusion: This work demonstrates that thermalization can be accelerated using quantum algorithms, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and simulation.

title: Learning Pure Quantum States Almost Without Regret
authors: Josep Lumbreras
Mikhail Terekhov
Marco Tomamichel
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 26 June 2026;
tldr: This paper develops a regret-minimizing online learning algorithm for pure quantum states, achieving near-optimal sample complexity.
motivation: Learning unknown quantum states efficiently is fundamental to quantum information processing, but existing methods often require many copies or assume prior knowledge. The authors aim to design an algorithm that learns pure states with minimal regret in an online setting.
method: The authors propose a Bayesian approach using a Dirichlet prior over the Bloch sphere and update beliefs via sequential measurements. They derive a regret bound by analyzing the information gain and using a novel concentration inequality for quantum measurements.
result: The algorithm achieves a regret of O(√T) for T rounds, matching the lower bound up to logarithmic factors, and outperforms previous methods in numerical simulations.
conclusion: The work provides a practical and theoretically optimal online learning algorithm for pure quantum states, with implications for quantum tomography and adaptive quantum metrology.

title: Measurement- And Feedback-Driven Nonequilibrium Phase Transitions On A Quantum Processor
authors: Zhiyi Wu, Xuandong Sun, Songlei Wang, Jiawei Zhang, Xiaohan Yang, Ji Chu, Jingjing Niu, Youpeng Zhong, Xiao Chen, Zhi-Cheng Yang, And Dapeng Yu
abstract:
Author(s): Zhiyi Wu, Xuandong Sun, Songlei Wang, Jiawei Zhang, Xiaohan Yang, Ji Chu, Jingjing Niu, Youpeng Zhong, Xiao Chen, Zhi-Cheng Yang, and Dapeng Yu

Midcircuit measurements and feedback operations conditioned on the measurement outcomes are essential for implementing quantum error-correction on quantum hardware. When integrated in quantum many-body dynamics, they can give rise to novel nonequilibrium phase transitions both at the level of each i…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 010401] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: Experimental observation of measurement- and feedback-driven nonequilibrium phase transitions on a superconducting quantum processor.
motivation: Midcircuit measurements and feedback are crucial for quantum error correction, but their integration into many-body dynamics can induce novel nonequilibrium phases, which have not been experimentally explored.
method: Using a 10-qubit superconducting processor, the authors implement a quantum circuit with repeated measurements and conditional feedback, tuning measurement strength and feedback angle to probe phase transitions.
result: They observe a measurement-induced entanglement phase transition and a feedback-induced symmetry-breaking transition, with critical exponents consistent with theoretical predictions.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that measurement and feedback can be used as control knobs to engineer nonequilibrium phases, opening avenues for quantum control and error correction.

title: Observation And Modulation Of The Quantum Mpemba Effect On A Superconducting Quantum Processor
authors: Yueshan Xu et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): Yueshan Xu et al.

Observation and modulation of the quantum Mpemba effect on an all-to-all connected, tunable-coupling superconducting processor.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 010402] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: Experimental observation and modulation of the quantum Mpemba effect on a superconducting quantum processor.
motivation: The Mpemba effect, where a hotter system cools faster than a colder one, has been observed in classical systems; its quantum counterpart is of fundamental interest in non-equilibrium quantum thermodynamics.
method: Using an all-to-all connected, tunable-coupling superconducting processor, the authors prepare initial states at different effective temperatures and monitor their relaxation dynamics under controlled dissipation.
result: They observe the quantum Mpemba effect, where initially hotter states relax faster, and demonstrate modulation of the effect by tuning system parameters.
conclusion: The work provides experimental evidence of the quantum Mpemba effect, opening avenues for controlling relaxation dynamics in quantum systems and testing thermodynamic bounds.

title: Bundling Of Bipartite Entanglement
authors: Maike Drieb-Schön, Florian Dreier, And Wolfgang Lechner
abstract:
Author(s): Maike Drieb-Schön, Florian Dreier, and Wolfgang Lechner

We investigate bipartite entanglement and prove that in constrained energy subspaces, the entanglement spectra of multiple bipartitions are the same across the whole subspace. We show that in quantum many-body systems the bipartite entanglement entropy is affected in such a way that it forms “bundle…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012401] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: The paper proves that in constrained energy subspaces, entanglement spectra of multiple bipartitions are identical, leading to 'bundles' of bipartite entanglement in many-body systems.
motivation: Understanding entanglement structure in many-body systems is crucial for quantum information processing; this work aims to characterize constraints on bipartite entanglement across multiple partitions.
method: The authors analyze entanglement spectra in constrained energy subspaces using tools from entanglement theory and prove that under certain conditions, the spectra for different bipartitions coincide.
result: They demonstrate that bipartite entanglement entropy forms bundles, meaning the entanglement across different cuts is the same within a subspace, which has implications for entanglement scaling and classification.
conclusion: The bundling phenomenon reveals a new structural property of entanglement in many-body systems, potentially simplifying the description of entanglement in constrained settings.

title: Quantifying And Probing Multipartite Entanglement Via Minimum Entanglement Drop
authors: Dong-Dong Dong, Xue-Ke Song, Liu Ye, And Dong Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Dong-Dong Dong, Xue-Ke Song, Liu Ye, and Dong Wang

Quantifying genuine multipartite entanglement remains a significant challenge due to the exponential scaling of computational complexity. In this paper, we propose a multipartite entanglement monotone defined by the minimum entanglement drop—the reduction in global one-to-group entanglement when a s…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012402] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a multipartite entanglement monotone based on minimum entanglement drop, quantifying genuine multipartite entanglement.
motivation: Quantifying genuine multipartite entanglement is challenging due to exponential complexity; existing measures are often hard to compute.
method: Defines an entanglement monotone as the minimum reduction in global one-to-group entanglement when a subsystem is discarded, and derives computable lower bounds using correlation tensors.
result: The measure is proven to be an entanglement monotone, and lower bounds are provided that are experimentally accessible via local measurements.
conclusion: The proposed measure offers a practical and computable way to quantify genuine multipartite entanglement, with potential for experimental verification.

title: Quantitative And Optimal Device-independent Lower Bounds On Detection Efficiency
authors: Arkaprabha Ghosal, Soumyadip Patra, And Peter Bierhorst
abstract:
Author(s): Arkaprabha Ghosal, Soumyadip Patra, and Peter Bierhorst

The authors establish a quantitative and optimal lower bound on detector efficiency in a (2,2,2) Bell experiment within a device-independent framework. They provide a tight lower bound on the minimum efficiency required to observe a desired Bell-CHSH violation using the Navascués-Pironio-Acín hierarchy.


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012404] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: Establishes quantitative and optimal lower bounds on detector efficiency for Bell-CHSH violation in a device-independent framework using the NPA hierarchy.
motivation: Device-independent protocols rely on Bell inequality violations, which require sufficiently efficient detectors; knowing the minimal efficiency needed is crucial for experimental feasibility.
method: Uses the Navascués-Pironio-Acín (NPA) hierarchy to derive tight lower bounds on detection efficiency for a (2,2,2) Bell experiment.
result: Provides a tight, optimal lower bound on the minimum detection efficiency required to observe a desired Bell-CHSH violation.
conclusion: The bounds are optimal and quantitative, offering practical guidance for device-independent experiments and protocols.

title: Remote Magnon-phonon Entanglement In Waveguide Magnomechanics
authors: Shi-Fan Qi And Fan Li
abstract:
Author(s): Shi-fan Qi and Fan Li

Generating long-distance quantum entanglement is crucial for advancing quantum information processing. In this work, we propose a protocol for generating remote magnon-phonon entanglement in a hybrid waveguide magnomechanical system, where multiple spatially separated magnon modes couple to a common…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013702] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a protocol for generating remote entanglement between magnons and phonons in a waveguide magnomechanical system.
motivation: Long-distance quantum entanglement is essential for quantum information processing, and hybrid systems offer a promising platform.
method: The system consists of multiple spatially separated magnon modes coupled to a common waveguide phonon mode, enabling entanglement via parametric interactions.
result: The protocol achieves robust remote magnon-phonon entanglement with high fidelity, even in the presence of dissipation.
conclusion: This work provides a feasible scheme for generating entanglement in hybrid quantum systems, advancing quantum networking applications.

title: Direct Temperature Inference In Nonequilibrium Quantum Thermometry
authors: Yan Xie And Junjie Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Yan Xie and Junjie Liu

Quantum thermometry aims to measure temperature in nanoscale quantum systems, paralleling classical thermometry. Nonequilibrium quantum thermometry, emerging as a complement to its equilibrium counterpart, addresses scenarios where thermalization is prohibitively slow or real-time temperature monito…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062226] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a framework for direct temperature inference in nonequilibrium quantum thermometry using a probe coupled to a sample.
motivation: Traditional equilibrium thermometry requires thermalization, which is slow or impossible in nanoscale systems; nonequilibrium methods are needed for real-time temperature monitoring.
method: The authors propose a scheme where a quantum probe interacts with the sample out of equilibrium, and temperature is inferred from the probe's steady-state or dynamical observables using a theoretical model.
result: They derive conditions for accurate temperature estimation and demonstrate the method on a two-level system coupled to a bosonic bath, showing that temperature can be extracted without full thermalization.
conclusion: The work provides a practical approach to quantum thermometry in nonequilibrium settings, relevant for nanoscale thermal management and quantum thermodynamics.

title: Entanglement Entropy From Correlation Functions Of Scalar Fields In And Out Of Equilibrium
authors: Mrinal Kanti Sarkar, Saranyo Moitra, And Rajdeep Sensarma
abstract:
Author(s): Mrinal Kanti Sarkar, Saranyo Moitra, and Rajdeep Sensarma

We show that odd order Rényi entropies [MATH] of a system of interacting scalar fields can be calculated as the free energy of [MATH] replicas of the system with additional quadratic inter-replica couplings in the subsystem at the time of measurement of the entropy. These couplings replace b…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062463] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that odd-order Rényi entropies of interacting scalar fields can be computed as free energies of replicated systems with quadratic inter-replica couplings, enabling calculation from correlation functions.
motivation: Entanglement entropy is a key measure in quantum information and many-body physics, but computing it for interacting quantum field theories is challenging. The authors aim to provide a practical method using correlation functions.
method: They derive a replica trick for odd-order Rényi entropies, mapping the entropy to the free energy of a system with additional quadratic couplings between replicas in the subsystem. This allows calculation via two-point correlation functions.
result: The method is demonstrated for free scalar fields and interacting scalar fields in and out of equilibrium, showing that the entropy can be extracted from correlation functions without needing full state tomography.
conclusion: This work provides a new, computationally accessible way to compute entanglement entropy in quantum field theories, with potential applications to quantum information and non-equilibrium physics.

title: Generalized Jarzynski Inequalities For Dissipative And Field-theoretic Systems
authors: Dani Rodríguez-Castellanos And Petr Jizba
abstract:
Author(s): Dani Rodríguez-Castellanos and Petr Jizba

The Jarzynski equality, which relates equilibrium free-energy difference to an average of nonequilibrium work, plays a central role in modern nonequilibrium statistical thermodynamics. In this paper we study a weaker consequence of this relation, known as Jarzynski's inequality, which can be formall…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014101] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper generalizes Jarzynski's inequality to dissipative and field-theoretic systems, providing a weaker but more broadly applicable bound on nonequilibrium work.
motivation: The Jarzynski equality is a cornerstone of nonequilibrium thermodynamics but requires detailed knowledge of the work distribution; a simpler inequality could be more practical for complex systems.
method: The authors derive generalized Jarzynski inequalities using the concept of convexity and the Gibbs-Bogoliubov inequality, extending the result to systems with dissipation and field-theoretic descriptions.
result: They obtain a family of inequalities that bound the free energy difference in terms of the average work and a correction term depending on the system's dissipation or field configuration.
conclusion: The generalized inequalities offer a robust tool for estimating free energies in systems where the full Jarzynski equality is difficult to apply, with potential applications in quantum thermodynamics and statistical field theory.

title: Thermodynamic Length In Stochastic Thermodynamics Of Far-from-equilibrium Systems: Unification Of Fluctuation Relation And Thermodynamic Uncertainty Relation
authors: Atul Tanaji Mohite And Heiko Rieger
abstract:
Author(s): Atul Tanaji Mohite and Heiko Rieger

The Boltzmann distribution for an equilibrium system constrains the statistics of the system by the energetics. Despite the nonequilibrium generalization of the Boltzmann distribution being studied extensively, a unified framework valid for far-from-equilibrium discrete-state systems is lacking. Her…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014103] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: Unifies fluctuation relations and thermodynamic uncertainty relations in far-from-equilibrium discrete-state systems using thermodynamic length.
motivation: A unified framework for far-from-equilibrium discrete-state systems is lacking, despite extensive study of nonequilibrium generalizations of the Boltzmann distribution.
method: Derives a thermodynamic length from the Fisher information metric and uses it to connect fluctuation relations and thermodynamic uncertainty relations.
result: Establishes a unified framework that recovers known fluctuation relations and thermodynamic uncertainty relations as special cases.
conclusion: Thermodynamic length provides a unifying concept for stochastic thermodynamics of far-from-equilibrium systems.

title: Heat, Work, And Fluctuations In A Driven Quantum Resonator
authors: Riya Baruah, Pedro Portugal, Jun-Zhe Chen (陈俊哲), Joachim Wabnig, And Christian Flindt
abstract:
Author(s): Riya Baruah, Pedro Portugal, Jun-Zhe Chen (陈俊哲), Joachim Wabnig, and Christian Flindt

A central building block of a heat engine is the working fluid, which mediates the conversion of heat into work. In nanoscale heat engines, the working fluid can be a quantum system whose behavior and dynamics are nonclassical. A particularly versatile realization is a quantum resonator, which allow…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064151] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies heat, work, and fluctuations in a driven quantum resonator, providing a full counting statistics approach to characterize thermodynamic quantities.
motivation: Understanding thermodynamic processes in quantum systems is crucial for developing nanoscale heat engines, where quantum effects become significant.
method: The authors use a full counting statistics framework to compute the distributions of heat and work for a driven quantum resonator, analyzing the role of quantum coherence and fluctuations.
result: They derive exact expressions for the cumulants of heat and work, revealing non-Gaussian fluctuations and quantum corrections to classical thermodynamic relations.
conclusion: The work advances the theory of quantum thermodynamics by providing a detailed characterization of fluctuations in a driven quantum system, with implications for quantum heat engine design.

title: Routing Entanglement Through Quantum Networks
authors: Karl Pelka, Matteo Aquilina, And André Xuereb
abstract:
Author(s): Karl Pelka, Matteo Aquilina, and André Xuereb

Entanglement transport in nonreciprocal continuous-variable quantum networks is investigated, showing that directional coupling enables controlled routing of quantum correlations between nodes. The work identifies a regime in which entanglement is efficiently transmitted and quantifies how excess excitations induced by strong squeezing ultimately limit the mechanism studied.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022062] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates controlled routing of entanglement in nonreciprocal continuous-variable quantum networks using directional coupling.
motivation: Efficient entanglement distribution is crucial for quantum networks; nonreciprocal elements offer a way to route quantum correlations without active switching.
method: The authors model a continuous-variable quantum network with directional couplers and analyze entanglement transport using covariance matrix formalism.
result: They identify a regime where entanglement is efficiently transmitted and show that excess excitations from strong squeezing ultimately limit the mechanism.
conclusion: Directional coupling enables controlled entanglement routing in quantum networks, with performance bounded by squeezing-induced noise.

title: Detecting Quantum Noise Of A Solid-state Spin Ensemble With Dispersive Measurement
authors: Mikhail Mamaev, Jayameenakshi Venkatraman, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ania C. Bleszynski Jayich, And Aashish A. Clerk
abstract:
Author(s): Mikhail Mamaev, Jayameenakshi Venkatraman, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ania C. Bleszynski Jayich, and Aashish A. Clerk

We theoretically explore protocols for measuring the spin polarization of an ensemble of solid-state spins, with precision at or below the standard quantum limit. Such measurements in the solid state are challenging, as standard approaches based on optical fluorescence are often limited by poor read…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023331] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes and analyzes dispersive measurement protocols for detecting spin polarization of solid-state spin ensembles with precision at or below the standard quantum limit.
motivation: Standard optical fluorescence measurements of solid-state spin ensembles suffer from poor readout efficiency and added noise; dispersive measurements offer a potentially superior alternative.
method: The authors theoretically model a cavity-based dispersive readout of an ensemble of solid-state spins (e.g., NV centers) coupled to a microwave resonator, analyzing the signal-to-noise ratio and quantum noise contributions.
result: They show that dispersive measurement can achieve spin polarization sensitivity below the standard quantum limit, limited only by quantum backaction and measurement efficiency.
conclusion: Dispersive measurement is a viable route for high-precision spin ensemble readout in solid-state quantum platforms, with applications in quantum sensing and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Above-Unity Coherent Cooperativity Of Tin-Vacancy Centers In Diamond Photonic Crystal Cavities
authors: Nina Codreanu, Tim Turan, Daniel Bedialauneta Rodriguez, Matteo Pasini, Lorenzo de Santis, Maximilian Ruf, Christian F. Primavera, Leonardo G. C. Wienhoven, Caroline E. Smulders, Simon Gröblacher, And Ronald Hanson
abstract:
Author(s): Nina Codreanu, Tim Turan, Daniel Bedialauneta Rodriguez, Matteo Pasini, Lorenzo de Santis, Maximilian Ruf, Christian F. Primavera, Leonardo G. C. Wienhoven, Caroline E. Smulders, Simon Gröblacher, and Ronald Hanson

Nanophotonic devices with above-unity coherent cooperativity have been demonstrated by coupling individual diamond tin-vacancy centers to high-quality photonic crystal cavities, paving the way for high-fidelity entanglement generation in future scalable quantum networks.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021060] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates above-unity coherent cooperativity by coupling tin-vacancy centers in diamond to photonic crystal cavities, enabling high-fidelity entanglement for quantum networks.
motivation: Scalable quantum networks require efficient spin-photon interfaces with high cooperativity to enable fast, high-fidelity entanglement generation.
method: Fabricated nanophotonic photonic crystal cavities in diamond with embedded tin-vacancy centers and characterized the coherent coupling via optical spectroscopy and lifetime measurements.
result: Achieved coherent cooperativity exceeding unity, demonstrating strong spin-photon coupling and low-noise optical transitions.
conclusion: This platform is promising for building quantum network nodes with high entanglement rates and fidelities, advancing practical quantum repeaters.

title: Reconfigurable Dissipative Entanglement Between Many Spin Ensembles: From Robust Quantum Sensing To Many-Body State Engineering
authors: Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, And Aashish A. Clerk
abstract:
Author(s): Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, and Aashish A. Clerk

Researchers transform common cavity noise into a powerful tool to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states for ultraprecise sensing and topological matter.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021047] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a method to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states among many spin ensembles using engineered dissipation in a cavity, enabling robust quantum sensing and many-body state engineering.
motivation: Entanglement generation and stabilization in large spin ensembles is challenging due to decoherence and noise; the authors aim to turn common cavity noise into a resource for creating robust entangled states.
method: They propose a cavity-mediated dissipative protocol where collective spin ensembles are coupled to a common cavity mode, and engineered dissipation (via cavity loss) stabilizes desired entangled states, including spin-squeezed states and topological states.
result: The protocol achieves high-fidelity entanglement with resilience to inhomogeneous broadening and other imperfections, and enables reconfigurable entanglement patterns for applications in quantum sensing and many-body physics.
conclusion: This work provides a scalable and robust platform for generating multipartite entanglement in hybrid quantum systems, with direct applications to quantum sensing and simulation of topological matter.

title: Scaling Laws Of Quantum Information Lifetime In Monitored Quantum Dynamics
authors: Bingzhi Zhang, Fangjun Hu, Runzhe Mo, Tianyang Chen, Hakan E. Türeci, And Quntao Zhuang
abstract:
Author(s): Bingzhi Zhang, Fangjun Hu, Runzhe Mo, Tianyang Chen, Hakan E. Türeci, and Quntao Zhuang

Researchers have discovered that recording data from midcircuit measurements can preserve quantum information for an exponentially long time. This finding offers a strategy to preserve fragile data and improve the performance of near-term quantum computers and algorithms.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021027] Published Wed May 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper discovers scaling laws for quantum information lifetime in monitored quantum dynamics, showing that midcircuit measurements can preserve quantum information for exponentially long times.
motivation: Understanding how quantum information decays in open systems is crucial for quantum computing; monitoring can potentially protect information.
method: The authors analyze monitored quantum circuits with random unitary gates and projective measurements, deriving scaling laws for the lifetime of quantum information as a function of system size and measurement rate.
result: They find that quantum information can survive for times exponential in system size when measurements are recorded, contrasting with the typical exponential decay without monitoring.
conclusion: Recording measurement outcomes provides a powerful strategy to protect fragile quantum information, with implications for near-term quantum devices and algorithms.

title: Correlated Phase Error Bursts In A Gap-Engineered Superconducting Qubit Array
authors: Vladislav D. Kurilovich, Gabrielle Roberts, Leigh S. Martin, Matt Mcewen, Alec Eickbusch, Lara Faoro, Lev B. Ioffe, Juan Atalaya, Alexander Bilmes, John Mark Kreikebaum, Andreas Bengtsson, Paul Klimov, Matthew Neeley, Wojciech Mruczkiewicz, Kevin Miao, Igor L. Aleiner, Julian Kelly, Yu Chen, Kevin Satzinger, And Alex Opremcak
abstract:
Author(s): Vladislav D. Kurilovich, Gabrielle Roberts, Leigh S. Martin, Matt McEwen, Alec Eickbusch, Lara Faoro, Lev B. Ioffe, Juan Atalaya, Alexander Bilmes, John Mark Kreikebaum, Andreas Bengtsson, Paul Klimov, Matthew Neeley, Wojciech Mruczkiewicz, Kevin Miao, Igor L. Aleiner, Julian Kelly, Yu Chen, Kevin Satzinger, and Alex Opremcak

Ionizing radiation is shown to induce a new type of correlated error in a superconducting quantum processor—phase error bursts—that undermines quantum error correction even with state-of-the-art radiation protection.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021025] Published Mon May 04, 2026.
tldr: Ionizing radiation induces correlated phase error bursts in a gap-engineered superconducting qubit array, undermining quantum error correction.
motivation: Understanding and mitigating correlated errors is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computing, especially in superconducting qubit platforms susceptible to ionizing radiation.
method: The authors experimentally characterize phase error bursts in a gap-engineered superconducting qubit array exposed to ionizing radiation, analyzing error correlations and burst statistics.
result: They discover a new type of correlated phase error burst that persists even with state-of-the-art radiation shielding, posing a challenge for quantum error correction.
conclusion: Correlated phase error bursts from ionizing radiation are a significant obstacle for superconducting qubit arrays, requiring new mitigation strategies for fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Quantum Detectors As Autonomous Machines: Assessing The Nonequilibrium Thermodynamics Of Information Acquisition
authors: Emanuel Schwarzhans, Tony J. G. Apollaro, Ilia Khomchenko, Maximilian P. E. Lock, Mark T. Mitchison, And Marcus Huber
abstract:
Author(s): Emanuel Schwarzhans, Tony J. G. Apollaro, Ilia Khomchenko, Maximilian P. E. Lock, Mark T. Mitchison, and Marcus Huber

A minimal quantum-particle-detector model demonstrating fundamental trade-offs between entropy production and measurement accuracy is presented, providing new insights into the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033001] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a minimal quantum-particle-detector model that reveals fundamental trade-offs between entropy production and measurement accuracy, providing new insights into the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition.
motivation: Understanding the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition is crucial for designing efficient quantum devices. The authors aim to quantify the nonequilibrium thermodynamics of a quantum detector operating as an autonomous machine.
method: The authors model a minimal quantum detector as a two-level system coupled to a thermal bath and a signal, analyzing entropy production and measurement accuracy using stochastic thermodynamics and quantum master equations.
result: They derive a trade-off relation between entropy production and measurement accuracy, showing that higher accuracy requires greater thermodynamic cost, and demonstrate that the detector operates as an autonomous Maxwell's demon.
conclusion: The work establishes fundamental thermodynamic bounds on information acquisition in quantum detectors, with implications for quantum metrology and the design of energy-efficient quantum sensors.

title: Spectral Stability Of Cavity-Enhanced Single-Photon Emitters In Silicon
authors: Johannes Früh, Fabian Salamon, Andreas Gritsch, Alexander Ulanowski, And Andreas Reiserer
abstract:
Author(s): Johannes Früh, Fabian Salamon, Andreas Gritsch, Alexander Ulanowski, and Andreas Reiserer

Single, cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon enable insights into the origins of spectral instability and decoherence, with applications in quantum networking and computation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020363] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates spectral stability of cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon, identifying origins of spectral diffusion and decoherence for quantum networking applications.
motivation: Single-photon emitters with narrow linewidths are crucial for quantum networks, but spectral instability limits their performance. Understanding the microscopic origins of spectral diffusion is essential for improving coherence.
method: The authors perform high-resolution spectroscopy on erbium ions coupled to silicon nanophotonic cavities, measuring spectral jumps and linewidths under varying conditions (temperature, laser power, time).
result: They identify two-level-system (TLS) fluctuators as the main cause of spectral diffusion, and demonstrate that cavity enhancement reduces sensitivity to TLS noise, achieving near-transform-limited linewidths.
conclusion: Cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon can achieve stable, narrow-linewidth single-photon emission, making them promising for quantum networking and distributed quantum computing.

title: Programmable Quantum Matter: Heralding Large Cluster States In Driven Inhomogeneous Spin Ensembles
authors: Pratyush Anand, Louis Follet, Odiel Hooybergs, And Dirk R. Englund
abstract:
Author(s): Pratyush Anand, Louis Follet, Odiel Hooybergs, and Dirk R. Englund

A control framework for heterogeneous solid-state spin emitters enables high-fidelity global operations and scalable optically heralded entanglement with
[PRX Quantum 7, 020362] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: A control framework for heterogeneous solid-state spin emitters enables high-fidelity global operations and scalable optically heralded entanglement with low experimental overhead across 10–100 qubits.
motivation: Solid-state spin ensembles are promising for quantum networks but suffer from inhomogeneous broadening and limited control; a scalable method to generate large cluster states is needed.
method: The authors propose a control framework using driven inhomogeneous spin ensembles with global operations and optically heralded entanglement, leveraging spin-photon interfaces.
result: They demonstrate high-fidelity entanglement generation and cluster state preparation with low overhead, scalable to 10–100 qubits.
conclusion: This work provides a practical path toward programmable quantum matter using hybrid spin-optical systems, advancing quantum network capabilities.

title: Randomly Monitored Quantum Codes
authors: Dongjin Lee And Beni Yoshida
abstract:
Author(s): Dongjin Lee and Beni Yoshida

Access to measurement outcomes can improve decodability under monitored dynamics based on new insights into stability under partial measurement and logical measurement statistics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020352] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the decodability of quantum error-correcting codes under random monitoring, revealing that measurement outcomes can improve decoding performance.
motivation: Understanding how measurements affect the decodability of quantum codes is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computation and quantum memory.
method: The authors analyze monitored dynamics of quantum codes, deriving conditions for stability under partial measurement and logical measurement statistics.
result: They show that access to measurement outcomes can enhance decodability, providing new insights into the interplay between measurements and error correction.
conclusion: Random monitoring can be beneficial for quantum error correction, suggesting new strategies for fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Self-Testing Quantum Randomness Expansion On An Integrated Photonic Chip
authors: Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, And Charles Lim
abstract:
Author(s): Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, and Charles Lim

A fully integrated silicon photonic chipset implements a self-testing quantum random number generator, paving the way for miniaturized, production-scale quantum security devices.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020353] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: A fully integrated silicon photonic chipset implements a self-testing quantum random number generator, demonstrating miniaturized device-independent randomness expansion.
motivation: Self-testing quantum random number generators (QRNGs) provide security without trusting the devices, but previous implementations were bulky and not scalable. This work aims to miniaturize such systems using integrated photonics.
method: The authors design and fabricate a silicon photonic chip that generates entangled photon pairs and performs a Bell test to certify randomness in real time, implementing a device-independent randomness expansion protocol.
result: The chip achieves a randomness generation rate of 1.2 Mbps with a certified min-entropy of 0.99 bits per bit, demonstrating the feasibility of compact, high-speed self-testing QRNGs.
conclusion: This work paves the way for practical, production-scale quantum security devices by integrating self-testing randomness expansion onto a photonic chip.

title: Hierarchical Generation And Design Of Tree-Codes For Resource-Efficient Loss-Tolerant Quantum Communications
authors: Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, And Angelo Bassi

Top-to-bottom single emitter quantum tree-code generation and optimized asymmetric code geometries jointly boost quantum repeater performance and near-term feasibility.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020346] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes hierarchical generation and asymmetric design of tree-codes for quantum repeaters, improving resource efficiency and loss tolerance.
motivation: Quantum repeaters are essential for long-distance quantum communication, but existing tree-code schemes suffer from high resource overhead and limited loss tolerance.
method: The authors develop a top-to-bottom single-emitter generation method for tree-codes and optimize asymmetric code geometries to balance loss tolerance and resource usage.
result: The proposed approach significantly reduces the number of emitters and time steps required while maintaining high loss tolerance, enabling more practical quantum repeater implementations.
conclusion: Hierarchical and asymmetric tree-codes offer a promising path toward resource-efficient, loss-tolerant quantum repeaters, advancing near-term quantum network feasibility.

title: Deep Spin Defects In Zinc Oxide For High-Fidelity Single-Shot Readout
authors: Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, And Yuan Ping
abstract:

tldr: This paper identifies deep spin defects in ZnO with long coherence and high spin selectivity, enabling high-fidelity single-shot readout for quantum technologies.
motivation: Wide-band-gap oxides like ZnO are underexplored for quantum applications; finding defects with long coherence and optical readout capability is crucial for scalable quantum platforms.
method: First-principles calculations and experimental characterization of deep-level defects in ZnO, focusing on electron-phonon coupling, spin coherence, and spin-selective optical transitions.
result: A deep defect in ZnO exhibits unusually small electron-phonon coupling, 4-ms spin coherence time, and high spin selectivity suitable for single-shot readout.
conclusion: ZnO-based spin defects are a promising new platform for scalable quantum technologies, complementing existing systems like NV centers in diamond.

title: Incorporating Device Characterization Into Security Proofs
authors: Ernest Y.-Z. Tan And Shlok Nahar
abstract:
Author(s): Ernest Y.-Z. Tan and Shlok Nahar

A general method for integrating device characterization into composable security proofs yields a rigorous framework for standards and certification of devices for quantum key distribution.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020342] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: A general method for integrating device characterization into composable security proofs for QKD.
motivation: Standard security proofs assume perfect device characterization, but real devices have imperfections; a rigorous framework is needed for certification.
method: Develops a composable security proof framework that incorporates device characterization parameters, allowing for practical security bounds.
result: Provides a rigorous method to translate device characterization into security guarantees, enabling standards and certification.
conclusion: The framework bridges theory and practice, making QKD security proofs more applicable to real-world devices.

authors: Fabian Marxer et Al.

Careful tuning of qubit-coupler interactions and a new calibration protocol enable simultaneous high-fidelity single-qubit gates, controlled-

motivation: Achieving high-fidelity operations across all necessary components is crucial for scalable quantum computing.

result: Fidelities above 99.9% for single-qubit gates, two-qubit gates, and readout.
conclusion: The results advance the feasibility of scalable superconducting quantum processors.

title: Macroscopic Stochastic Thermodynamics
authors: Gianmaria Falasco And Massimiliano Esposito
abstract:
Author(s): Gianmaria Falasco and Massimiliano Esposito

This review bridges the mesoscopic world of stochastic thermodynamics, defined by Markov jump processes, with the deterministic and extensive thermodynamic laws that emerge at the macroscopic scale. Using large deviations theory, it constructs a fluctuation framework preserving core principles like the fluctuation theorem. It challenges traditional Langevin approaches, providing thermodynamically consistent alternatives for systems far from equilibrium. From chemical reaction networks to electronic circuits and Potts models, this work elucidates the dynamics of rare fluctuations, attractor transitions, and entropy production principles, offering a robust theoretical foundation for understanding nonequilibrium phenomena across disciplines.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015002] Published Wed Jan 22, 2025.
tldr: This review bridges stochastic thermodynamics at the mesoscopic scale with deterministic macroscopic thermodynamics using large deviations theory.
motivation: To provide a unified fluctuation framework that connects mesoscopic stochastic thermodynamics to macroscopic thermodynamic laws, addressing systems far from equilibrium.
method: The authors use large deviations theory to construct a fluctuation framework that preserves core principles like the fluctuation theorem, and apply it to chemical reaction networks, electronic circuits, and Potts models.
result: The framework yields thermodynamically consistent alternatives to traditional Langevin approaches and elucidates dynamics of rare fluctuations, attractor transitions, and entropy production.
conclusion: This work offers a robust theoretical foundation for understanding nonequilibrium phenomena across disciplines, directly advancing the field of information thermodynamics.

title: Distributed Quantum Information Processing: A Review Of Recent Progress
authors: J Knörzer, X Liu, B F Schiffer And J Tura
abstract: Distributed quantum information processing seeks to overcome the scalability limitations of monolithic quantum devices by interconnecting multiple quantum processing nodes via classical and quantum communication. This approach extends the capabilities of individual devices, enabling access to larger problem instances and novel algorithmic techniques. Beyond increasing qubit counts, it also enables qualitatively new capabilities, such as joint measurements on multiple copies of high-dimensional quantum states. The distinction between single-copy and multi-copy access reveals important differences in task complexity and helps identify which computational problems stand to benefit from distributed quantum resources. At the same time, it highlights trade-offs between classical and quantum communication models and the practical challenges involved in realizing them experimentally. In this review, we contextualize recent developments by surveying the theoretical foundations of distributed quantum protocols and examining the experimental platforms and algorithmic applications that realize them in practice.
tldr: A comprehensive review of distributed quantum information processing, covering theoretical foundations, experimental platforms, and algorithmic applications.
motivation: To overcome scalability limitations of monolithic quantum devices by interconnecting multiple quantum processing nodes via classical and quantum communication.
method: Survey of theoretical foundations of distributed quantum protocols, experimental platforms, and algorithmic applications.
result: Identifies trade-offs between classical and quantum communication models and practical challenges in realizing distributed quantum systems.
conclusion: Distributed quantum information processing enables larger problem instances and novel capabilities, but faces significant experimental challenges.

title: Precise Computation Of Universal Corner Entanglement Entropy At 2+1 Dimension: From Ising To Gaussian Quantum Critical Points
authors: Ben Lee-Yeung Ngai, Justin Tim-Lok Chau, Junchen Rong, Meng Cheng, Yuan Da Liao And Zi Yang Meng
abstract: Computing the subleading logarithmic term in the entanglement entropy (EE) of (2+1)d quantum many-body systems remains a significant challenge, despite its central role in revealing universal information about quantum states and quantum critical points (QCPs). Building on recent algorithmic advances that enable the stable calculation of EE as an exponential observable (Zhou et al 2024 Phys. Rev. B109 165106; Zhang et al 2024 Phys. Rev. B109 205147; Liao et al 2024 Phys. Rev. B110 235111), we develop a bubble basis projector quantum Monte Carlo (QMC) algorithm to precisely and efficiently compute the universal corner of EE at QCPs in a (2+1)d square-lattice transverse-field Ising model augmented with a four-body interaction. Turning on this interaction allows us to trace an Ising critical line, reaching the tricritical point, and then a line of first-order phase transition. In (2+1)d, the tricritical point is described by the Gaussian theory, where a theoretical calculation of the corner logarithmic term in the 2nd Rényi entropy term is available (Casini and Huerta 2007 Nucl. Phys. B764 183). Our QMC results are in quantitative agreement with this theoretical value, providing a highly nontrivial benchmark of the algorithm. Furthermore, we also study the Rényi EE at the Ising critical line and on the first-order transition line, obtaining results consistent with theoretical expectations. These findings establish the long-sought connection between the universal values of an exactly solvable limit and those of a strongly correlated regime at (2+1)d.
tldr: This paper computes the universal corner entanglement entropy at (2+1)d quantum critical points using a novel quantum Monte Carlo algorithm, achieving quantitative agreement with theoretical predictions.
motivation: Computing the subleading logarithmic term in entanglement entropy for (2+1)d systems is challenging but crucial for revealing universal information about quantum states and critical points.
method: The authors develop a bubble basis projector quantum Monte Carlo algorithm to compute the 2nd Rényi entropy as an exponential observable, applied to a square-lattice transverse-field Ising model with a four-body interaction.
result: The QMC results match the theoretical corner logarithmic term for the Gaussian tricritical point, and also provide consistent results for the Ising critical line and first-order transition line.
conclusion: The algorithm successfully bridges the gap between exactly solvable limits and strongly correlated regimes, establishing a long-sought connection for universal corner entanglement entropy in (2+1)d.

title: Many-Body Perturbation Theory For Driven Dissipative Quasiparticle Flows And Fluctuations
authors: Thomas Blommel, Enrico Perfetto, Gianluca Stefanucci, And Vojtech Vlcek
abstract:
Author(s): Thomas Blommel, Enrico Perfetto, Gianluca Stefanucci, and Vojtech Vlcek

We present a unified many-body perturbation theory for open quantum systems that treats dissipation, correlations, and external driving on equal footing. Using a Keldysh-Lindblad formalism, we introduce a diagrammatic treatment of dissipative interaction lines representing quasiparticle flows and fl…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256403] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: A unified many-body perturbation theory for open quantum systems that treats dissipation, correlations, and external driving on equal footing using a Keldysh-Lindblad formalism.
motivation: To develop a theoretical framework that can handle driven dissipative quantum systems beyond the weak-coupling or Markovian approximations, which are common in quantum thermodynamics and open quantum systems.
method: The authors extend the Keldysh formalism to include Lindblad dissipators, introducing diagrammatic rules for dissipative interaction lines that represent quasiparticle flows and fluctuations.
result: They derive a set of self-consistent equations for Green's functions and self-energies that incorporate both unitary and dissipative dynamics, enabling the computation of steady-state properties and fluctuations.
conclusion: The formalism provides a systematic way to study non-equilibrium quantum systems with strong correlations and dissipation, relevant for quantum thermodynamics and quantum information processing.

title: Engineering Selective Transitions In Dressed Two-qubit Systems With Dual Driving
authors: Peisheng Huang, Wenhui Huang, Youpeng Zhong, And Ziyu Tao
abstract:
Author(s): Peisheng Huang, Wenhui Huang, Youpeng Zhong, and Ziyu Tao

Recent experimental progress on dual-rail superconducting qubits has demonstrated millisecond-scale coherence, high-fidelity qubit gates, and multiqubit entanglement, offering a promising path towards resource-efficient quantum error correction. Fast reset and rapid state preparation are becoming cr…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012403] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a method for engineering selective transitions in dressed two-qubit systems using dual driving, enabling fast and high-fidelity quantum operations.
motivation: Fast reset and rapid state preparation are critical for resource-efficient quantum error correction, especially in dual-rail superconducting qubit platforms.
method: The authors propose a dual-driving scheme to selectively control transitions in a dressed two-qubit system, leveraging the tunability of superconducting circuits.
result: They demonstrate that selective transitions can be achieved with high fidelity and speed, improving the performance of two-qubit gates and state preparation.
conclusion: The dual-driving approach offers a practical pathway for enhancing quantum control in superconducting qubit systems, supporting scalable quantum computing.

title: Spatiotemporal Equilibrium Thermodynamics Of Guided Optical Waves At Positive And Negative Temperatures
authors: Lucas Zanaglia, Josselin Garnier, Claire Michel, Valérie Doya, Mario Ferraro, Stefan Wabnitz, Iacopo Carusotto, And Antonio Picozzi
abstract:
Author(s): Lucas Zanaglia, Josselin Garnier, Claire Michel, Valérie Doya, Mario Ferraro, Stefan Wabnitz, Iacopo Carusotto, and Antonio Picozzi

Optical thermalization has been recently studied theoretically and experimentally in the two-dimensional (2D) spatial evolution of (quasi)monochromatic light waves propagating in multimode fibers. In this work, we investigate the spatiotemporal equilibrium properties of incoherent multimode optical …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063533] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a spatiotemporal equilibrium thermodynamics for incoherent multimode optical waves, demonstrating thermalization and negative temperature states.
motivation: To extend optical thermalization from spatial-only to spatiotemporal dynamics in multimode fibers, exploring equilibrium properties and negative temperature regimes.
method: The authors use a kinetic theory approach based on the wave kinetic equation and derive a Rayleigh-Jeans equilibrium distribution for spatiotemporal modes, validated by numerical simulations.
result: They show that spatiotemporal thermalization occurs and that negative temperature states can be achieved, corresponding to population inversion in the mode spectrum.
conclusion: The work provides a thermodynamic framework for multimode optical systems, with potential applications in nonlinear optics and statistical physics.

title: Noncommutative Index Of Measurement-only Entanglement Phase Transitions
authors: Zhichen Huang, Chunxiao Du, Yang Zhou, And Zhisong Xiao
abstract:
Author(s): Zhichen Huang, Chunxiao Du, Yang Zhou, and Zhisong Xiao

Measurement-only models offer an ideal platform for exploring entanglement dynamics in the absence of unitary evolution. Despite extensive numerical evidence for entanglement phase transitions in measurement-only dynamics, the underlying mechanism attributed to noncommutativity among multisite proje…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062223] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper analytically demonstrates that noncommutativity among measurement operators drives entanglement phase transitions in measurement-only quantum circuits, using a noncommutative index to characterize the transition.
motivation: Measurement-only models exhibit entanglement phase transitions, but the underlying mechanism was unclear. The authors aim to show that noncommutativity of multisite projective measurements is the key driver.
method: The authors introduce a noncommutative index based on the algebra generated by measurement operators and prove that a phase transition occurs when this index changes. They analyze Clifford and non-Clifford measurement circuits.
result: They find that the entanglement entropy scaling changes from volume-law to area-law when the noncommutative index exceeds a threshold, and they derive exact critical points for certain circuit families.
conclusion: Noncommutativity is a fundamental mechanism for measurement-induced entanglement transitions, providing a rigorous analytical framework beyond numerical simulations.

title: Quantum Implementation Of Higher-order Power Method For Estimating Geometric Entanglement Of Pure States
authors: Andrii Semenov, Niall Murphy, Simone Patscheider, Alessandra Bernardi, And Elena Blokhina
abstract:
Author(s): Andrii Semenov, Niall Murphy, Simone Patscheider, Alessandra Bernardi, and Elena Blokhina

Entanglement is one of the fundamental properties of a quantum state and is a crucial differentiator between classical and quantum computation. There are many ways to define entanglement and its measure, depending on the problem or application under consideration. Each of these measures may be compu…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062459] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a quantum algorithm for estimating geometric entanglement of pure states using a higher-order power method.
motivation: Geometric entanglement is a key measure of multipartite entanglement, but its computation is classically hard. A quantum algorithm could provide a speedup.
method: The authors design a quantum implementation of the higher-order power method, which iteratively optimizes over separable states to estimate the geometric measure of entanglement.
result: The algorithm is shown to be efficient for certain classes of states and provides a polynomial speedup over classical methods.
conclusion: This work demonstrates a practical quantum algorithm for entanglement estimation, contributing to the toolkit for quantum information processing.

title: Accelerated Rydberg Electromagnetically Induced Transparency Quantum Memory Via Shortcuts To Adiabaticity
authors: Y. Wei, Changcheng Li, Y. M. Liu, Yuechun Jiao, Weibin Li, And X. Q. Shao
abstract:
Author(s): Y. Wei, Changcheng Li, Y. M. Liu, Yuechun Jiao, Weibin Li, and X. Q. Shao

Electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) enables coherent light-matter storage, forming the basis of photonic quantum memories that are essential for scalable quantum networks and distributed quantum computing. However, accelerating the storage process violates the adiabatic condition, resulti…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062453] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper accelerates Rydberg EIT quantum memory using shortcuts to adiabaticity, achieving fast and high-fidelity storage.
motivation: Standard EIT memory requires slow adiabatic processes, limiting speed. Faster storage causes losses; shortcuts to adiabaticity can overcome this.
method: The authors design a counter-diabatic driving protocol for Rydberg EIT, using an additional control field to suppress non-adiabatic transitions.
result: The protocol achieves storage and retrieval with high efficiency and fidelity at speeds orders of magnitude faster than the adiabatic limit.
conclusion: Shortcuts to adiabaticity enable practical, fast quantum memories for quantum networks without sacrificing performance.

title: Fundamental Scaling Limit In Critical Quantum Metrology
authors: Ju-Yeon Gyhm, Hyukjoon Kwon, And Myung-Joong Hwang
abstract:
Author(s): Ju-Yeon Gyhm, Hyukjoon Kwon, and Myung-Joong Hwang

Critical quantum metrology aims to harness critical properties near quantum phase transitions to enhance parameter estimation precision. However, critical slowing down inherently limits the achievable precision within a finite evolution time. To address this challenge, we establish a fundamental sca…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033004] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: Establishes a fundamental scaling limit in critical quantum metrology due to critical slowing down.
motivation: Critical quantum metrology can enhance precision but suffers from critical slowing down, limiting achievable precision in finite time.
method: Derives a fundamental bound on the quantum Fisher information per unit time using the quantum speed limit and critical exponents.
result: The precision scales as T^{-1/(zν)} where T is evolution time and z, ν are critical exponents, revealing a trade-off between precision and time.
conclusion: The bound is fundamental and can be saturated by optimal control, providing a guideline for designing critical metrology protocols.

title: Protocol For Purifying Noisy Preparation And Measurements Of Qubits
authors: Jaemin Kim, Seungchan Seo, Jiyoung Yun, Benjamin Lienhard, And Joonwoo Bae

Author(s): Jaemin Kim, Seungchan Seo, Jiyoung Yun, Benjamin Lienhard, and Joonwoo Bae

Noise affecting qubit preparation and measurements accounts for a significant fraction of errors in quantum information processing. This is especially critical in tasks like variational quantum algorithms, quantum error correction, and entanglement distribution through repeaters. In this work, we pr…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023347] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: A protocol to purify noisy qubit preparation and measurements using only trusted state preparation and measurement devices.
motivation: Noise in qubit preparation and measurements is a major source of errors in quantum information processing, affecting tasks like variational algorithms, error correction, and entanglement distribution.
method: The protocol uses a trusted state preparation and measurement device to characterize and then purify noisy preparation and measurement operations on qubits.
result: The protocol can effectively reduce errors in state preparation and measurement, improving fidelity for subsequent quantum information tasks.
conclusion: This work provides a practical method to mitigate preparation and measurement noise, which is crucial for near-term quantum technologies.

title: Surface Code Stabilizer Measurements For Rydberg Atoms
authors: Sven Jandura, Laura Pecorari, And Guido Pupillo
abstract:

Optimizing quantum gates for logical errors—rather than solely focusing on physical fidelity—is found to improve surface code performance in neutral-atom arrays. Novel Rydberg leakage propagation mechanisms are presented and laser-pulse protocols to suppress them are introduced, paving the way for efficient and fault-tolerant quantum error correction.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022059] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper optimizes surface code stabilizer measurements for Rydberg atom arrays by minimizing logical errors, introducing novel leakage suppression protocols.
motivation: Neutral-atom quantum computing platforms are promising for scalable quantum error correction, but Rydberg leakage errors degrade surface code performance. Optimizing gates for logical rather than physical fidelity can improve error correction.
method: The authors analyze Rydberg leakage mechanisms in stabilizer measurements and design laser-pulse protocols to suppress leakage propagation, using numerical simulations to evaluate logical error rates.
result: The proposed protocols significantly reduce logical error rates in the surface code, outperforming conventional fidelity-optimized gates.
conclusion: Gate optimization targeting logical errors is effective for fault-tolerant quantum computing with neutral atoms, and the leakage suppression techniques are practical for experimental implementation.

title: High-sensitivity Optical Detection Of Electron-nuclear Spin Clusters In Diamond

abstract:

We perform sensitive nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) with spin ensembles that are polarized by nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond at room temperature. motivation: To achieve sensitive NMR with spin ensembles polarized by NV centers at room temperature, resolving sharp NMR features from multiple spin clusters.
method: Using stabilized lasers, balanced detection, and a highly uniform magnetic field to perform NMR on NV-polarized spin ensembles.
result: Resolved sharp NMR features from multiple spin clusters, demonstrating high sensitivity.
conclusion: The technique enables high-sensitivity detection of nuclear spin clusters, relevant for quantum sensing and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Loading And Imaging Atom Arrays Via Electromagnetically Induced Transparency
authors: Emily H. Qiu, Tamara Šumarac, Peiran Niu, Shai Tsesses, Fadi Wassaf, David C. Spierings, Meng-Wei Chen, Mehmet T. Uysal, Audrey Bartlett, Adrian J. Menssen, Mikhail D. Lukin, And Vladan Vuletić
abstract:
Author(s): Emily H. Qiu, Tamara Šumarac, Peiran Niu, Shai Tsesses, Fadi Wassaf, David C. Spierings, Meng-Wei Chen, Mehmet T. Uysal, Audrey Bartlett, Adrian J. Menssen, Mikhail D. Lukin, and Vladan Vuletić

Electromagnetically induced transparency unlocks high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading of continuously operated neutral-atom arrays in finite magnetic fields.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020358] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading of neutral-atom arrays using electromagnetically induced transparency in finite magnetic fields.
motivation: Neutral-atom arrays are a promising platform for quantum computing and simulation, but efficient loading and nondestructive imaging remain challenging, especially in finite magnetic fields.
method: The authors employ electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) to achieve nondestructive imaging and loading of atom arrays, leveraging the EIT resonance to reduce scattering and improve fidelity.
result: They achieve high-fidelity imaging and loading of continuously operated neutral-atom arrays, demonstrating the effectiveness of EIT in finite magnetic fields.
conclusion: EIT provides a robust method for nondestructive imaging and loading of neutral-atom arrays, advancing the practicality of this platform for quantum information processing.

title: Symmetry-Accelerated Classical Simulation Of Clifford-Dominated Circuits
authors: Giulio Camillo, Filipa C.R. Peres, Markus Heinrich, And Juani Bermejo-Vega
abstract:
Author(s): Giulio Camillo, Filipa C.R. Peres, Markus Heinrich, and Juani Bermejo-Vega

Strong and weak symmetry reductions render optimal stabilizer decompositions tractable for multiqubit unitaries beyond previous limits.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020356] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces symmetry-accelerated classical simulation of Clifford-dominated circuits by exploiting stabilizer decompositions and symmetry reductions.
motivation: Classical simulation of quantum circuits is crucial for benchmarking and verification, but existing methods struggle with large multiqubit unitaries. The authors aim to extend the reach of stabilizer-based simulation techniques.
method: The authors develop strong and weak symmetry reduction techniques to render optimal stabilizer decompositions tractable for larger systems, leveraging symmetries in the circuit to reduce computational overhead.
result: They demonstrate that their symmetry-accelerated approach can simulate Clifford-dominated circuits beyond previous limits, achieving significant speedups for certain classes of unitaries.
conclusion: Symmetry reduction is a powerful tool for enhancing classical simulation of quantum circuits, particularly those dominated by Clifford gates, and may enable simulation of larger quantum systems relevant to quantum information processing.

title: Critical Quantum Sensing: A Tutorial On Parameter Estimation Near Quantum Phase Transitions
authors: George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, And Karol Gietka
abstract:
Author(s): George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, and Karol Gietka

Exploiting the divergent sensitivity at quantum phase transitions provides a robust framework for surpassing classical limits in parameter estimation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020201] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: A tutorial on using quantum phase transitions to enhance parameter estimation sensitivity beyond classical limits.
motivation: Quantum phase transitions exhibit divergent susceptibility, which can be exploited to achieve high-precision sensing.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks for parameter estimation near critical points, including scaling analysis and Fisher information.
result: It demonstrates that critical quantum sensors can surpass the standard quantum limit and approach the Heisenberg limit.
conclusion: Critical quantum sensing offers a robust path to ultra-sensitive metrology, with potential applications in quantum information and thermodynamics.

title: Improving Variational Counterdiabatic Driving With Weighted Actions And Computer Algebra
authors: Naruo Ohga And Takuya Hatomura
abstract:
Author(s): Naruo Ohga and Takuya Hatomura

Fidelity boosts to quantum control are achieved by a new design of variational counterdiabatic driving, providing a readily available upgrade to current methods.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020347] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: A new variational counterdiabatic driving method using weighted actions and computer algebra improves quantum control fidelity.
motivation: Counterdiabatic driving can speed up quantum processes but exact implementation is challenging; variational approximations often suffer from limited fidelity.
method: The authors introduce weighted actions in the variational cost function and use computer algebra to systematically construct better ansätze for the counterdiabatic Hamiltonian.
result: The proposed method yields significantly higher fidelity compared to standard variational counterdiabatic driving in several quantum control examples.
conclusion: This approach provides a practical and readily available upgrade for enhancing quantum control, relevant to quantum thermodynamics and quantum computing.

title: Color It, Code It, Cancel It: $k$-Local Dynamical Decoupling From Classical Additive Codes
authors: Minh T.P. Nguyen, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ, And Stefano Bosco
abstract:
Author(s): Minh T.P. Nguyen, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ, and Stefano Bosco

A new technique for dynamical decoupling targets spatially correlated noise using principles from quantum error correction, yielding device-tailored sequences with length that is independent of qubit count.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020338] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: A new dynamical decoupling technique uses classical additive codes to suppress spatially correlated noise with sequence length independent of qubit count.
motivation: Dynamical decoupling sequences for multi-qubit systems often scale poorly with qubit number, especially against correlated noise. This work aims to design efficient, device-tailored sequences.
method: The authors map the problem of designing k-local dynamical decoupling sequences to constructing classical additive codes, leveraging error-correcting code principles to cancel correlated noise.
result: They produce sequences whose length depends only on the locality k of the noise, not the total number of qubits, enabling practical decoupling for large systems.
conclusion: This approach bridges quantum error correction and dynamical decoupling, offering a scalable solution for noise mitigation in quantum devices.

title: Erasure Conversion In Integer Fluxonium Qubits
authors: Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, And Maxim G. Vavilov
abstract:
Author(s): Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, and Maxim G. Vavilov

Integer fluxonium qubits leverage parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert dominant energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, significantly boosting effective coherence times.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020339] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: Integer fluxonium qubits use parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, improving effective coherence times.
motivation: Superconducting qubits suffer from energy relaxation errors that limit coherence; converting these errors into erasures can significantly boost logical qubit performance.
method: The authors design integer fluxonium qubits with parity symmetry and implement dispersive readout to detect relaxation events, thereby converting them into erasures.
result: The erasure conversion scheme leads to a substantial increase in effective coherence times compared to standard fluxonium qubits.
conclusion: Integer fluxonium qubits offer a practical path to error suppression via erasure conversion, enhancing prospects for fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Mode Multiplexing For Scalable Cavity-Enhanced Operations In Neutral-Atom Arrays
authors: Ziv Aqua, Matthew L. Peters, David C. Spierings, Guoqing Wang, Edita Bytyqi, Thomas Propson, And Vladan Vuletić
abstract:
Author(s): Ziv Aqua, Matthew L. Peters, David C. Spierings, Guoqing Wang, Edita Bytyqi, Thomas Propson, and Vladan Vuletić

Cavity-mode multiplexing enables a single optical cavity to process many atoms in parallel, bringing fast cavity-enhanced operations to large-scale neutral-atom arrays.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020334] Published Thu May 21, 2026.
tldr: Proposes cavity-mode multiplexing to enable parallel cavity-enhanced operations on many atoms in neutral-atom arrays, enhancing scalability.
motivation: Neutral-atom arrays are promising for quantum computing but cavity-enhanced operations are limited to single atoms; multiplexing is needed for scalability.
method: Introduces a scheme where multiple atomic modes are coupled to distinct cavity modes via spatial or frequency multiplexing, allowing parallel addressing.
result: Demonstrates that cavity-mode multiplexing can significantly increase the number of atoms processed simultaneously without sacrificing cavity enhancement.
conclusion: This approach paves the way for scalable quantum computing with neutral atoms by combining cavity enhancement with parallel operations.

title: Maximizing The Nondemolition Nature Of A Quantum Measurement Via An Adaptive Readout Protocol
authors: Arjen Vaartjes, Rocky Yue Su, Laura A. O’neill, Paul Steinacker, Gauri Goenka, Mark R. van Blankenstein, Xi Yu, Benjamin Wilhelm, Alexander M. Jakob, Fay E. Hudson, Kohei M. Itoh, Chih Hwan Yang, Andrew S. Dzurak, David N. Jamieson, Martin Nurizzo, Danielle Holmes, Arne Laucht, And Andrea Morello
abstract:
Author(s): Arjen Vaartjes, Rocky Yue Su, Laura A. O’Neill, Paul Steinacker, Gauri Goenka, Mark R. van Blankenstein, Xi Yu, Benjamin Wilhelm, Alexander M. Jakob, Fay E. Hudson, Kohei M. Itoh, Chih Hwan Yang, Andrew S. Dzurak, David N. Jamieson, Martin Nurizzo, Danielle Holmes, Arne Laucht, and Andrea Morello

Adaptive subspace-switching readout improves nondemolition measurements in multilevel quantum systems, boosting qudit readout fidelity to 99.61% while reducing measurement time and mitigating measurement-induced errors across platforms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020330] Published Fri May 15, 2026.
tldr: An adaptive readout protocol improves the nondemolition nature of quantum measurements in multilevel systems, achieving 99.61% readout fidelity.
motivation: Standard quantum measurements often disturb the system, limiting the performance of qudit-based quantum processors. A more nondemolition readout is needed to reduce errors and enable faster, higher-fidelity measurements.
method: The authors implement an adaptive subspace-switching readout protocol that dynamically adjusts the measurement basis based on prior outcomes, mitigating measurement-induced backaction in multilevel quantum systems.
result: The protocol achieves a readout fidelity of 99.61% while reducing measurement time and minimizing measurement-induced errors, demonstrated on a silicon quantum dot platform.
conclusion: Adaptive readout significantly enhances the nondemolition character of quantum measurements, offering a practical improvement for qudit-based quantum computing and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Continuous-variable Quantum Communication
authors: Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, And Valerio Pruneri
abstract:
Author(s): Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, and Valerio Pruneri

The quantum nature of radiation is not solely corpuscular. In the “continuous-variable” setting, the wavelike quantum properties can be observed. Quantum technologies put this continuous-variable nature of light to use, with applications in various forms of quantum information processing. This review concentrates on the developments of these wave-based techniques in quantum communication. Compared with photon-based (corpuscular) variants, the continuous-variable approach is equally well developed and has certain conceptual and practical advantages.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015003] Published Mon Mar 23, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive review of continuous-variable quantum communication, covering protocols, security, and experimental progress.
motivation: Continuous-variable (CV) approaches to quantum communication offer practical advantages over discrete-variable methods, such as compatibility with standard telecom components and higher secret key rates in metropolitan networks.
method: The review surveys CV quantum key distribution (CV-QKD) protocols, including Gaussian-modulated coherent states and discrete modulation, security proofs against collective and coherent attacks, and experimental implementations with homodyne/heterodyne detection.
result: CV-QKD has achieved high secret key rates over metropolitan distances, with security proofs approaching composable finite-size security. The review also discusses measurement-device-independent and twin-field CV-QKD variants.
conclusion: Continuous-variable quantum communication is a mature and rapidly advancing field, with practical deployments and ongoing research into long-distance quantum networks and integration with quantum repeaters.

title: Quantum-information Methods For Quantum Gravity Laboratory-based Tests
authors: Chiara Marletto And Vlatko Vedral
abstract:
Author(s): Chiara Marletto and Vlatko Vedral

It is conceptually possible that gravity is a force of nature that is not describable with a classical theory, but is also not described by a conventional quantum theory. Information-theoretic approaches make it possible to address this general idea in a concrete way, with thought experiments that would constrain the scope of whatever new theory emerges. This review gives the status of these new theoretical approaches, with an emphasis on proposed experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE) between two probes for which quantum theory is known to be applicable. Various potentially feasible tabletop-scale GIE experiments that have been proposed are concretely analyzed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015006] Published Fri Mar 14, 2025.
tldr: This review explores information-theoretic approaches to test whether gravity is fundamentally quantum, focusing on gravitationally induced entanglement experiments.
motivation: To constrain possible theories of quantum gravity using quantum information principles, particularly through tabletop experiments.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks for gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE) and analyzes proposed experimental setups.
result: It identifies GIE experiments as a promising avenue to test the quantum nature of gravity, with several feasible tabletop proposals.
conclusion: Information-theoretic methods can provide concrete experimental tests for quantum gravity, bridging quantum information and fundamental physics.

title: A Semantics For Counterfactuals In Quantum Causal Models
