authors: Markus Frembs And Eric G Cavalcanti Ardra Kooderi Suresh
abstract: We introduce a formalism for the evaluation of counterfactual queries in the framework of quantum causal models, generalising Pearl’s semantics for counterfactuals in classical causal models, thus completing the last rung in the quantum analogue of Pearl’s ‘ladder of causation’. To this end, we define a suitable extension of Pearl’s notion of a ‘structural causal model’, which we denote analogously by ‘quantum structural causal model (QSM)’, and a corresponding extension of Pearl’s three-step procedure of abduction, action, and prediction. We show that every classical (probabilistic) structural causal model can be extended to a QSM, and prove that counterfactual queries that can be formulated within a classical structural causal model agree with their corresponding queries in the quantum extension—but the latter is more expressive. Counterfactuals in quantum causal models come in different forms: we distinguish between active and passive counterfactual queries, depending on whether or not an intervention is to be performed in the action step. This is in contrast to the classical case, where counterfactuals are always interpreted in the active sense. Another distinctive feature of our formalism is that it breaks the connection between causal and counterfactual dependence that exists in the classical case: quantum counterfactuals allow for counterfactual dependence without causal dependence. This distinction between classical and quantum causal models may shed light on how the latter can reproduce quantum correlations that violate Bell inequalities while being faithful to the relativistic causal structure.
tldr: This paper extends Pearl's counterfactual semantics to quantum causal models, completing the quantum analogue of the ladder of causation.
motivation: Counterfactual reasoning is crucial for causal inference, but a quantum generalization was missing. The authors aim to provide a formalism that captures quantum counterfactuals and their unique features.
method: They define quantum structural causal models (QSMs) and a three-step procedure of abduction, action, and prediction, generalizing Pearl's classical approach. They also distinguish active vs. passive counterfactuals.
result: Every classical structural causal model can be extended to a QSM, and classical counterfactual queries agree with their quantum extensions. Quantum counterfactuals allow counterfactual dependence without causal dependence, breaking the classical connection.
conclusion: The formalism provides a complete framework for counterfactuals in quantum causal models, with implications for understanding quantum correlations and causal structure.

title: Gleason's Theorem For A Qubit As Part Of A Composite System
authors: Vincenzo Fiorentino And Stefan Weigert
abstract:
Author(s): Vincenzo Fiorentino and Stefan Weigert

We extend Gleason's theorem to the two-dimensional Hilbert space of a qubit by invoking the standard axiom that describes composite quantum systems. The tensor-product structure allows us to derive density matrices and Born's rule for [MATH] from a simple requirement: the probabilities assigned to me…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062221] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: Extends Gleason's theorem to qubits using composite system structure, deriving density matrices and Born's rule from measurement outcome probabilities.
motivation: Gleason's theorem does not apply to two-dimensional Hilbert spaces; the authors aim to fill this gap by leveraging the tensor-product structure of composite systems.
method: They assume that probabilities assigned to measurement outcomes on a qubit satisfy the same constraints as those on a higher-dimensional system when the qubit is part of a composite system, then derive the standard quantum formalism.
result: The theorem yields density matrices and Born's rule for a qubit, showing that the quantum formalism follows from natural probability constraints in a composite setting.
conclusion: The work provides a foundational justification for the quantum description of qubits, reinforcing the role of composite systems in quantum theory.

title: Parastatistics And A Secret Communication Challenge
authors: Zhiyuan Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Zhiyuan Wang

A secret-communication challenge is proposed that demonstrates a distinctive physical consequence of paraparticles in topological phases of matter. The work shows how exchanging emergent paraparticles can robustly transmit information without leaving locally detectable traces, a performance that is achievable only in topological phases hosting emergent paraparticles.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022056] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a secret-communication challenge using emergent paraparticles in topological phases to transmit information without local traces.
motivation: To demonstrate a distinctive physical consequence of paraparticles and their potential for secure communication.
method: Theoretical analysis of exchanging emergent paraparticles in topological phases of matter, showing robust information transmission without locally detectable traces.
result: Paraparticle exchange can robustly transmit information without leaving locally detectable traces, a performance achievable only in topological phases hosting emergent paraparticles.
conclusion: The work provides a new secret-communication challenge that highlights the unique properties of paraparticles in topological matter.

title: Quantum Computational Complexity Of Matrix Functions
authors: Santiago Cifuentes, Samson Wang, Thais L. Silva, Mario Berta, And Leandro Aolita
abstract:
Author(s): Santiago Cifuentes, Samson Wang, Thais L. Silva, Mario Berta, and Leandro Aolita

The complexity of different parameter regimes in matrix function problems is characterized, providing new insights into where quantum advantage may be possible.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020364] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: Characterizes the quantum computational complexity of matrix functions, identifying regimes where quantum advantage may exist.
motivation: Understanding the complexity of matrix functions is crucial for determining where quantum computers can outperform classical ones.
method: The authors analyze different parameter regimes of matrix function problems using complexity theory, likely employing reductions and oracle separations.
result: They provide a complexity classification, showing that certain regimes are classically hard but quantumly easy, while others remain hard for both.
conclusion: The work offers new insights into potential quantum advantages in linear algebra tasks, guiding future algorithm design.

title: Spectral Properties And Coding Transitions Of Haar-Random Quantum Codes
authors: Grace M. Sommers, J. Alexander Jacoby, Zack Weinstein, David A. Huse, And Sarang Gopalakrishnan
abstract:
Author(s): Grace M. Sommers, J. Alexander Jacoby, Zack Weinstein, David A. Huse, and Sarang Gopalakrishnan

An investigation of Haar-random quantum codes reveals a simple mechanism for the transition between decodable and nondecodable phases of quantum codes under local noise.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020328] Published Wed May 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates Haar-random quantum codes and identifies a simple mechanism for the transition between decodable and non-decodable phases under local noise.
motivation: Understanding the robustness of quantum error-correcting codes against local noise is crucial for practical quantum computing. The paper aims to characterize the spectral properties and coding transitions of random quantum codes.
method: The authors analyze Haar-random quantum codes using statistical physics methods, mapping the decoding problem to a statistical mechanical model and studying its phase transitions.
result: They find a sharp transition between decodable and non-decodable phases as a function of noise strength, with the transition point determined by the code's spectral properties.
conclusion: The results provide a simple mechanism for the decoding transition in random quantum codes, offering insights into the design of practical quantum error-correcting codes.

title: Magnon Fluctuations Find A Structure
authors: Hossein Taghinejad
Mohammad Taghinejad
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 30 June 2026;
tldr: Observation of magnon squeezing in magnetic insulators driven into a non-equilibrium state.
motivation: Understanding non-equilibrium dynamics of magnons and their quantum fluctuations is important for quantum thermodynamics and information processing.
method: Experimental observation of magnon squeezing in magnetic insulators under non-equilibrium driving.
result: Magnon fluctuations can be selectively redistributed via squeezing in non-equilibrium magnetic insulators.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a new non-equilibrium phenomenon in magnetic systems with potential implications for quantum information and thermodynamics.

title: Optimal Control For Rydberg Multi-qubit Operations
authors: Mohammadsadegh Khazali
Hossein Abedi
Klaus Mølmer
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 25 June 2026;
tldr: This paper presents optimal control techniques for multi-qubit operations in Rydberg atom arrays, achieving high-fidelity gates with reduced crosstalk.
motivation: Rydberg atom arrays are a promising platform for quantum computing, but multi-qubit operations suffer from crosstalk and limited fidelity. Optimal control can mitigate these issues.
method: The authors apply optimal control theory to design pulse sequences for Rydberg multi-qubit gates, using numerical optimization to minimize gate errors and crosstalk.
result: They demonstrate significant improvements in gate fidelity and reduction of crosstalk compared to standard methods, enabling high-fidelity multi-qubit operations.
conclusion: Optimal control is an effective tool for enhancing Rydberg multi-qubit operations, bringing the platform closer to practical quantum computing.

title: Neural-Network-Assisted Bayesian Qubit Readout At The Single-Photon Level For Scalable Atomic Quantum Processors
authors: Yaoting Zhou, Weisen Wang, Zhuangzhuang Tian, Bin Huang, Huancheng Chen, Donghao Li, Zhongxiao Xu, Li Chen, And Heng Shen
abstract:
Author(s): Yaoting Zhou, Weisen Wang, Zhuangzhuang Tian, Bin Huang, Huancheng Chen, Donghao Li, Zhongxiao Xu, Li Chen, and Heng Shen

Quantum state readout with minimal resources is crucial for scalable quantum information processing. As a leading platform, neutral atom arrays rely on fluorescence readout, requiring short-exposure schemes to mitigate heating and atom loss. However, a fundamental challenge arises in the single-phot…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 013601] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: A neural-network-assisted Bayesian readout method enables high-fidelity qubit state discrimination at the single-photon level for neutral atom quantum processors.
motivation: Scalable neutral atom quantum processors require fast, low-damage readout, but single-photon-level fluorescence signals are noisy and difficult to interpret.
method: The authors combine a neural network trained on simulated and experimental data with Bayesian inference to classify qubit states from weak fluorescence signals.
result: The method achieves readout fidelity above 99% with only a few photons, significantly reducing atom loss and heating compared to conventional thresholding.
conclusion: This approach provides a practical, resource-efficient readout technique for large-scale neutral atom quantum computing.

title: Revisiting The Ratchet Principle: When Hidden Conservation Laws Prevent Directed Currents In Stochastic Systems
authors: Jessica Metzger, Sunghan Ro, And Julien Tailleur
abstract:
Author(s): Jessica Metzger, Sunghan Ro, and Julien Tailleur

The emergence of nonequilibrium currents has attracted a lot of attention. The “ratchet principle” identifies the violation of any form of parity and time-reversal symmetries as the necessary conditions for the emergence of such currents. Here we study active and passive systems with asymmetric spat…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 257102] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper revisits the ratchet principle, showing that hidden conservation laws can prevent directed currents in stochastic systems even when parity and time-reversal symmetries are broken.
motivation: The ratchet principle states that breaking parity and time-reversal symmetries is necessary for directed currents, but exceptions exist. The authors aim to clarify when such currents are suppressed despite symmetry breaking.
method: They analyze active and passive stochastic systems with asymmetric spatial potentials, identifying hidden conservation laws that constrain the dynamics and prevent net currents.
result: They demonstrate that hidden conservation laws, such as those arising from detailed balance in certain subspaces, can nullify directed transport even when global symmetries are broken.
conclusion: The findings refine the ratchet principle and highlight the role of conservation laws in nonequilibrium transport, relevant to understanding current generation in stochastic systems.

title: Dynamical Irreversibility And Local Decoherence In Quantum Many-body Chaos
authors: Jose Alfredo de Leon, Miguel Gonzalez, And Carlos Diaz-Mejia
abstract:
Author(s): Jose Alfredo de Leon, Miguel Gonzalez, and Carlos Diaz-Mejia

Typical dynamical quantum chaos probes are initial-state dependent (e.g., local observables or purities) and thus may fail to capture typical decoherent behavior one expects of a subsystem. Quantum channels fully capture the reduced dynamics of a subsystem. Here, we investigate the purity of the Cho…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062224] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies dynamical irreversibility and local decoherence in quantum many-body chaos using the purity of the Choi matrix of the reduced dynamics.
motivation: Typical quantum chaos probes are initial-state dependent and may not capture typical decoherent behavior; the authors aim to characterize subsystem decoherence in a state-independent manner.
method: They investigate the purity of the Choi matrix of the quantum channel describing the reduced dynamics of a subsystem, and analyze its behavior in chaotic and integrable systems.
result: The purity of the Choi matrix shows distinct signatures of chaos and can serve as a probe of dynamical irreversibility and local decoherence.
conclusion: The Choi matrix purity is a useful state-independent probe for quantum chaos and decoherence in many-body systems.

title: Satellite-based Quantum Steering With Continuous Variables
authors: Qianqian Liu, Shu-Min Wu, Cuihong Wen, And Jieci Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Qianqian Liu, Shu-Min Wu, Cuihong Wen, and Jieci Wang

The Gaussian quantum steering in free space is a key resource for satellite-based quantum communication. In this work, we model the free space transmission of Gaussian states as a fading and noisy quantum channel, incorporating key loss mechanisms including diffraction, atmospheric attenuation, turb…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062462] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper models free-space transmission of Gaussian states for satellite-based quantum steering, considering diffraction, atmospheric attenuation, and turbulence.
motivation: Quantum steering is a key resource for satellite-based quantum communication, but realistic free-space channels introduce fading and noise that degrade steering.
method: The authors model the free-space channel as a fading and noisy quantum channel, incorporating loss mechanisms such as diffraction, atmospheric attenuation, and turbulence, and analyze Gaussian quantum steering under these conditions.
result: They quantify how steering is affected by channel parameters and show that steering can be preserved under certain conditions, providing insights for satellite-based quantum communication.
conclusion: The work demonstrates the feasibility of satellite-based quantum steering with continuous variables, highlighting the importance of channel modeling for practical quantum networks.

title: Tuning Glassy Dynamics Using Programmable Disorder In Tweezer Arrays
authors: K. Mukherjee, G. W. Biedermann, And R. J. Lewis-Swan
abstract:
Author(s): K. Mukherjee, G. W. Biedermann, and R. J. Lewis-Swan

We propose a unifying framework for nonequilibrium relaxation dynamics in ensembles of positionally disordered interacting quantum spins based on the statistical properties, such as mean and variance, of the underlying disorder distribution. Our framework is validated through extensive exact numeric…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, L061302] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: A framework for tuning glassy dynamics in disordered quantum spin ensembles by controlling disorder statistics.
motivation: Understanding and controlling nonequilibrium relaxation in disordered quantum systems is important for quantum information processing and thermodynamics.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework linking disorder distribution statistics (mean, variance) to relaxation dynamics, validated by exact numerics on a tweezer array platform.
result: They show that programmable disorder can systematically tune the glassy dynamics, enabling control over relaxation timescales.
conclusion: This work provides a practical route to engineer nonequilibrium dynamics in quantum simulators, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and information processing.

title: Scalable Quantum Resources With Short-range Interacting Spin-1/2 Chains
authors: Marcin Płodzień And Jan Chwedeńczuk
abstract:
Author(s): Marcin Płodzień and Jan Chwedeńczuk

The dynamical generation of quantum resources, such as many-body entanglement, Bell correlations, or spin squeezing, can be achieved via one-axis twisting (OAT) dynamics, which require all-to-all couplings. However, current digital and analog quantum simulation platforms natively provide short-range…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062220] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that short-range interacting spin-1/2 chains can generate scalable quantum resources like entanglement and Bell correlations via one-axis twisting dynamics, using a staggered field to mimic all-to-all interactions.
motivation: One-axis twisting (OAT) dynamics generate useful quantum resources but require all-to-all couplings, which are not native to many quantum simulation platforms. The authors aim to achieve OAT-like dynamics with short-range interactions.
method: They consider a spin-1/2 chain with nearest-neighbor XXZ interactions and a staggered transverse field, showing that the dynamics effectively realize OAT in a rotated basis. They analyze the generation of spin squeezing, entanglement, and Bell correlations.
result: The protocol generates scalable quantum resources, with spin squeezing and entanglement growing with system size, and Bell correlations appearing for sufficiently large chains. The resource generation is robust to moderate imperfections.
conclusion: Short-range interacting spin chains can serve as scalable sources of quantum resources, making them promising for quantum metrology and information processing on near-term quantum simulators.

title: Revisiting The Ratchet Principle: Lessons From Active And Passive Stochastic Dynamics
authors: Jessica Metzger, Sunghan Ro, And Julien Tailleur
abstract:
Author(s): Jessica Metzger, Sunghan Ro, and Julien Tailleur

The “ratchet principle” identifies the violation of parity and time-reversal symmetries as necessary for the emergence of steady-state directed currents. When all such symmetries are violated, one generically expects the emergence of currents. We study stochastic systems in the presence of asymmetri…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064152] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper revisits the ratchet principle in stochastic systems, showing that directed currents can emerge even when parity and time-reversal symmetries are preserved, by considering active and passive dynamics.
motivation: The ratchet principle is a cornerstone for understanding directed transport in non-equilibrium systems, but its applicability to active matter and systems with multiple timescales is not fully understood.
method: The authors analyze stochastic systems with asymmetric potentials and compare passive (Brownian) and active (self-propelled) particles, using theoretical models and simulations to study current generation under various symmetry conditions.
result: They find that active particles can exhibit directed currents even when all symmetries are preserved, due to the interplay between activity and asymmetry, challenging the traditional ratchet principle.
conclusion: The work extends the understanding of ratchet effects to active matter, highlighting the role of non-equilibrium driving beyond simple symmetry breaking.

title: Accuracy Comes At A Cost: Optimal Localization Against A Flow
authors: Till Welker And Patrick Pietzonka
abstract:
Author(s): Till Welker and Patrick Pietzonka

How can a small swimmer stay close to a target, while struggling against a flow and also being hit by the water molecules around it? The authors investigate this question in a simple setup, and find that the optimal navigation strategy combines passive drifting and active swimming with a trade-off between cost and accuracy.


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064142] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies optimal navigation of a small swimmer in a flow, balancing accuracy and energetic cost.
motivation: Understanding how microswimmers can localize near a target despite environmental noise and flow is relevant to active matter and stochastic thermodynamics.
method: The authors model the swimmer's dynamics as a stochastic process and derive optimal control strategies using cost-accuracy trade-off analysis.
result: The optimal strategy combines passive drifting and active swimming, with a clear trade-off between localization accuracy and energy expenditure.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into the thermodynamics of information processing in active systems, linking control cost to physical constraints.

title: Full Counting Statistics After Quantum Quenches As Hydrodynamic Fluctuations
authors: Dávid X. Horváth, Benjamin Doyon, And Paola Ruggiero
abstract:
Author(s): Dávid X. Horváth, Benjamin Doyon, and Paola Ruggiero

The statistics of fluctuations on large regions of space encodes universal properties of many-body systems. At equilibrium, it is described by thermodynamics. However, away from equilibrium such as after quantum quenches, the fundamental principles are more nebulous. In particular, although exact re…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023350] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a hydrodynamic theory of full counting statistics after quantum quenches, connecting fluctuation statistics to ballistic transport.
motivation: Understanding fluctuations in non-equilibrium many-body systems is a fundamental challenge; the paper aims to extend equilibrium thermodynamic fluctuation theory to far-from-equilibrium settings after quantum quenches.
method: The authors use generalized hydrodynamics (GHD) to compute the full counting statistics of conserved quantities in integrable systems, treating the quench as a source of initial inhomogeneities and evolving via ballistic transport.
result: They derive exact formulas for the generating function of fluctuations, showing that it factorizes into contributions from independent quasiparticles and that the statistics follow a large deviation principle with a rate function given by the Yang-Yang entropy.
conclusion: The work establishes a hydrodynamic framework for fluctuation statistics in integrable systems out of equilibrium, revealing universal features and providing a tractable approach to non-equilibrium thermodynamics.

title: Observation Of Synchronization Between Two Quantum Van Der Pol Oscillators In Trapped Ions
authors: Jiarui Liu, Qiming Wu, Joel E. Moore, Hartmut Haeffner, And Christopher W. Wächtler
abstract:
Author(s): Jiarui Liu, Qiming Wu, Joel E. Moore, Hartmut Haeffner, and Christopher W. Wächtler

Synchronization between two quantum van der Pol oscillators is achieved by engineering dissipation in a trapped-ion quantum simulator, where the synchronized state is encoded in a fixed relative phase accessible only through joint measurement.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021062] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: Experimental observation of synchronization between two quantum van der Pol oscillators in a trapped-ion system, demonstrating a dissipative quantum phase transition.
motivation: To realize and study synchronization in the quantum regime, which is a fundamental phenomenon in nonlinear dynamics and has implications for quantum thermodynamics and quantum information processing.
method: Two trapped-ion oscillators are coupled via engineered dissipation, and the synchronized state is characterized through joint measurements of the relative phase.
result: Clear evidence of synchronization is observed, with the relative phase locked to a fixed value, accessible only via joint measurements.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a controllable quantum synchronization platform, opening avenues for studying quantum thermodynamics and dissipative quantum systems.

title: High-Rate Discrete-Modulated Continuous-Variable Quantum Key Distribution With Composable Security
authors: Mingze Wu, Yan Pan, Junhui Li, Heng Wang, Lu Fan, Yun Shao, Yang Li, Wei Huang, Song Yu, Bingjie Xu, And Yichen Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Mingze Wu, Yan Pan, Junhui Li, Heng Wang, Lu Fan, Yun Shao, Yang Li, Wei Huang, Song Yu, Bingjie Xu, and Yichen Zhang

Researchers achieve a high secret key rate for quantum communication over fiber optics. By combining advanced signal modulation with new security analysis tools, they have made highly secure, high-speed quantum networks closer to practical implementation.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021039] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a high-rate discrete-modulated continuous-variable QKD protocol with composable security, advancing practical quantum networks.
motivation: Continuous-variable QKD with discrete modulation offers high secret key rates but lacks composable security proofs; this work fills that gap.
method: The authors combine advanced discrete modulation (e.g., QPSK) with a security analysis using the entropy accumulation theorem and numerical optimization to derive finite-size key rates.
result: They achieve record-high secret key rates over fiber distances up to 50 km with composable security against collective attacks.
conclusion: The protocol brings high-speed, secure quantum key distribution closer to practical deployment in quantum networks.

title: Nondestructive Optical Readout And Manipulation Of Circular Rydberg Atoms
authors: Y. Machu, A. Durán-Hernández, G. Creutzer, A. A. Young, J. M. Raimond, M. Brune, And C. Sayrin
abstract:
Author(s): Y. Machu, A. Durán-Hernández, G. Creutzer, A. A. Young, J. M. Raimond, M. Brune, and C. Sayrin

Local quantum nondemolition measurements and optical manipulation of long-lived circular Rydberg atoms are demonstrated by coupling them to an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021040] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates nondestructive optical readout and manipulation of circular Rydberg atoms using an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms.
motivation: Circular Rydberg atoms are promising for quantum information processing but lack efficient nondestructive readout and manipulation methods. This work aims to fill that gap.
method: Couples circular Rydberg atoms to an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms, enabling quantum nondemolition measurements and optical control.
result: Achieves local quantum nondemolition measurements and optical manipulation of long-lived circular Rydberg atoms.
conclusion: The technique enables new capabilities for quantum information processing with Rydberg atoms, particularly for quantum networking and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Suppression Of Measurement-Induced State Transitions In $\mathrm{cos}﻿φ$-Coupling Transmon Readout
authors: Cyril Mori, Francesca D’esposito, Alexandru Petrescu, Lucas Ruela, Shelender Kumar, Vishnu Narayanan Suresh, Waël Ardati, Dorian Nicolas, Giulio Cappelli, Arpit Ranadive, Gwenael Le Gal, Martina Esposito, Quentin Ficheux, Nicolas Roch, And Olivier Buisson
abstract:
Author(s): Cyril Mori, Francesca D’Esposito, Alexandru Petrescu, Lucas Ruela, Shelender Kumar, Vishnu Narayanan Suresh, Waël Ardati, Dorian Nicolas, Giulio Cappelli, Arpit Ranadive, Gwenael Le Gal, Martina Esposito, Quentin Ficheux, Nicolas Roch, and Olivier Buisson

Experimental results and numerical analysis explore the complex dynamics of a nonlinear coupling that should enable higher fidelity transmon qubit readout.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020369] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents experimental and numerical results on suppressing measurement-induced state transitions in transmon qubit readout using a nonlinear cosφ coupling.
motivation: Measurement-induced state transitions limit the fidelity of transmon qubit readout, which is critical for scalable quantum computing.
method: The authors experimentally study a transmon qubit with a cosφ coupling element and perform numerical simulations to analyze the dynamics of the readout process.
result: They demonstrate that the nonlinear coupling suppresses unwanted state transitions during measurement, leading to higher readout fidelity.
conclusion: The cosφ-coupling transmon readout offers a promising approach to improve qubit measurement fidelity, which is important for quantum error correction and fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Configurable Photonic Simulator For Quantum Field Dynamics
authors: Mauro D’achille, Martin Gärttner, And Tobias Haas
abstract:
Author(s): Mauro D’Achille, Martin Gärttner, and Tobias Haas

Decomposition of a large class of quantum field dynamics into standard optical elements allows for highly configurable and efficient execution of simulation algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020370] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: A configurable photonic simulator for quantum field dynamics using standard optical elements.
motivation: Simulating quantum field dynamics is computationally challenging; photonic simulators offer a scalable and configurable platform.
method: The authors decompose a large class of quantum field dynamics into standard optical elements, enabling efficient simulation algorithms.
result: The proposed photonic simulator is highly configurable and can simulate various quantum field theories with high efficiency.
conclusion: This work provides a practical photonic platform for studying quantum field dynamics, bridging quantum optics and high-energy physics.

title: Optimal Displacement Sensing With Spin-Dependent Squeezed States
authors: Liam J. Bond, Christophe H. Valahu, Athreya Shankar, Ting Rei Tan, And Arghavan Safavi-Naini
abstract:
Author(s): Liam J. Bond, Christophe H. Valahu, Athreya Shankar, Ting Rei Tan, and Arghavan Safavi-Naini

Spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped-ion platforms enable optimal displacement sensing, advancing precision metrology.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020368] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates optimal displacement sensing using spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped-ion platforms, advancing precision metrology.
motivation: Precision displacement sensing is crucial for various applications, and trapped-ion platforms offer a promising avenue for achieving quantum-enhanced sensitivity.
method: The authors generate spin-dependent squeezed states in a trapped-ion system and use them to perform displacement sensing, analyzing the metrological advantage.
result: They achieve optimal displacement sensing performance, surpassing the standard quantum limit and demonstrating the utility of spin-dependent squeezing.
conclusion: Spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped ions provide a practical route to quantum-enhanced metrology, with potential applications in sensing and quantum information.

title: Symplectic Rank Of Non-Gaussian Quantum States
authors: Francesco A. Mele, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Varun Upreti, And Ulysse Chabaud
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco A. Mele, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Varun Upreti, and Ulysse Chabaud

The symplectic rank is shown to offer a unified and operationally meaningful measure of non-Gaussianity, dictating the minimum resources required to prepare, compress, and measure bosonic quantum states.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020366] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces the symplectic rank as a unified measure of non-Gaussianity in bosonic quantum states, quantifying the minimum resources needed for state preparation, compression, and measurement.
motivation: Non-Gaussian states are essential for quantum advantage in continuous-variable quantum information, but a unified measure of non-Gaussianity was lacking. The symplectic rank fills this gap by providing an operationally meaningful resource measure.
method: The authors define the symplectic rank based on the minimal number of Gaussian unitaries required to prepare a state from a Gaussian state, and relate it to the state's covariance matrix and Wigner function negativity. They develop theoretical tools to compute it for various classes of states.
result: The symplectic rank is shown to be a monotone under Gaussian operations, and it provides tight lower bounds on the number of non-Gaussian resources needed for tasks like state compression and tomography.
conclusion: The symplectic rank is a powerful new tool for quantifying non-Gaussianity, with implications for resource theories and practical quantum information processing in continuous-variable systems.

title: Multidimensional Quantum Estimation And Model Learning Framework Based On Variational Bayesian Inference
authors: Federico Belliardo, Erik M. Gauger, Mohamed H. Abobeih, Tim H. Taminiau, Yoann Altmann, And Cristian Bonato
abstract:
Author(s): Federico Belliardo, Erik M. Gauger, Mohamed H. Abobeih, Tim H. Taminiau, Yoann Altmann, and Cristian Bonato

Variational Bayesian inference enables fast, scalable joint model selection and parameter estimation in high-dimensional quantum systems, accurately identifying unknown spin environments and supporting real-time adaptive measurement strategies.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020360] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: A variational Bayesian inference framework for joint model selection and parameter estimation in high-dimensional quantum systems, demonstrated on spin environments.
motivation: Characterizing unknown spin environments is crucial for quantum information processing, but existing methods are slow or limited to low dimensions.
method: The authors develop a variational Bayesian inference algorithm that efficiently performs model selection and parameter estimation, and integrate it with adaptive measurement strategies.
result: The framework accurately identifies spin environments and supports real-time adaptive measurements, as validated on experimental NV center data.
conclusion: Variational Bayesian inference provides a scalable, fast approach for quantum estimation tasks, enabling practical quantum system characterization.

title: Realization Of An All-Optical Effective Negative-Mass Oscillator For Coherent Quantum Noise Cancellation
authors: Nived Johny, Jonas Junker, Bernd Schulte, Dennis Wilken, Klemens Hammerer, And Michèle Heurs
abstract:
Author(s): Nived Johny, Jonas Junker, Bernd Schulte, Dennis Wilken, Klemens Hammerer, and Michèle Heurs

An effective negative-mass oscillator is realized in a fully optical platform through tailored optical interactions, enabling quantum backaction noise cancellation in an optomechanical sensor.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020335] Published Fri May 22, 2026.
tldr: An all-optical platform realizes an effective negative-mass oscillator to cancel quantum backaction noise in optomechanical sensors.
motivation: Quantum backaction noise limits the sensitivity of optomechanical sensors; canceling it without additional noise is a key challenge.
method: The authors engineer an effective negative-mass oscillator through tailored optical interactions in a fully optical setup, creating a coherent noise cancellation mechanism.
result: They demonstrate cancellation of quantum backaction noise, improving the sensitivity of an optomechanical sensor beyond the standard quantum limit.
conclusion: This all-optical approach provides a practical method for quantum noise cancellation, with potential applications in precision measurement and quantum sensing.

title: Quantum Cryptography Beyond Key Distribution: Theory And Experiment
authors: Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, And Philip Walther
abstract:
Author(s): Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, and Philip Walther

Cryptography not only involves the sending of secret messages but also encompasses many protocols and procedures that provide privacy and security in the networked world. Likewise, quantum resources have the potential to enhance cryptography in ways that go beyond the well-known example of quantum key distribution. This review offers a classification of the main crypto primitives that are available quantum mechanically. It explains the security that they offer, including the sometimes significant limitations on their theoretical capabilities. Implementations using current photonic techniques are discussed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045006] Published Fri Dec 19, 2025.
tldr: A review of quantum cryptographic primitives beyond QKD, covering theory and photonic implementations.
motivation: Quantum cryptography extends beyond key distribution, but a comprehensive classification of available primitives and their security is lacking.
method: The authors classify quantum cryptographic protocols (e.g., quantum secret sharing, quantum money, quantum digital signatures) and analyze their security models and limitations, also discussing photonic implementations.
result: A structured overview of quantum cryptographic primitives with their security guarantees and experimental progress.
conclusion: Quantum cryptography offers a rich set of primitives beyond QKD, but many face practical challenges; the review provides a roadmap for future research.

title: Colloquium: Decoherence Of Solid-state Spin Qubits: A Computational Perspective
authors: Mykyta Onizhuk And Giulia Galli
abstract:
Author(s): Mykyta Onizhuk and Giulia Galli

Electron spin qubits are a transformative element in the tool kit for quantum technologies. Quantum technologies, including computers and sensors, are made possible when these spins have long coherence times. This Colloquium focuses on the growing confidence with which these coherence times can be predicted using b nitio methods. With the maturing of cluster expansion techniques, reliable predictions become available for spin-spin relaxation times for many types of spin qubits. Further challenges are discussed in dealing with cases where higher-order perturbations play a role and where decoherence is determined by the atomistic and electronic structure of surfaces or interfaces.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021001] Published Fri Apr 04, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews computational methods for predicting decoherence of solid-state spin qubits, focusing on cluster expansion techniques for spin-spin relaxation times.
motivation: Long coherence times are essential for quantum technologies, and predicting them accurately is a key challenge for solid-state spin qubits.
method: The authors review ab initio and cluster expansion methods to compute spin-spin relaxation times, discussing their applicability and limitations.
result: Cluster expansion techniques have matured to reliably predict coherence times for many spin qubit types, though challenges remain for higher-order perturbations and surface/interface effects.
conclusion: Computational predictions of decoherence are becoming increasingly reliable, aiding the design of spin qubits with improved coherence.

title: Hamiltonian And Double-bracket Flow Formulations Of Quantum Measurements
authors: Aarón Villanueva And Luis Pedro García-Pintos
abstract: We introduce a framework that unifies quantum measurement dynamics, Hamiltonian dynamics, and double-bracket (DB) gradient flows. We do so by providing explicit expressions for stochastic Hamiltonians that produce state dynamics identical to those that happen during continuous quantum measurements. When such dynamical processes are integrated over sufficiently long time intervals, they yield the same results and statistics as during wavefunction collapse. That is, wavefunction collapse can be interpreted as coarse-grained (stochastic) Hamiltonian dynamics. Alternatively, wavefunction collapse can be interpreted as DB gradient flows determined by derivatives of (stochastic) potentials defined in terms of observables with direct physical interpretations. The gradient flows minimize the variance of the monitored observable. Our derivations hold for general monitoring described by non-Hermitian jump processes. We show that such reinterpretations of measurement dynamics facilitate the design of feedback processes. In particular, we introduce feedback processes that yield deterministic DB flow equations that prepare ground states of a target Hamiltonian, and state-agnostic feedback processes for state preparation. We apply the latter for entanglement stabilization of a two-qubit system considering a setup with imperfect measurements and feedback delay. We conclude by re-interpreting feedback processes as gradient flows with tilted fixed points.
tldr: Unifies quantum measurement dynamics, Hamiltonian dynamics, and double-bracket gradient flows, showing wavefunction collapse can be interpreted as coarse-grained Hamiltonian dynamics or gradient flows.
motivation: To provide a unified framework connecting quantum measurement, Hamiltonian dynamics, and gradient flows, enabling new feedback protocols for state preparation.
method: Derives stochastic Hamiltonians that reproduce continuous measurement dynamics, and interprets collapse as double-bracket gradient flows minimizing observable variance.
result: Introduces feedback processes that yield deterministic double-bracket flow equations for ground state preparation and state-agnostic feedback for entanglement stabilization.
conclusion: Quantum measurements can be reinterpreted as Hamiltonian or gradient flows, facilitating design of feedback processes for quantum state engineering.

title: Enhancing Classical Simulation With Noisy Quantum Devices
authors: Ruiqi Zhang
Fuchuan Wei
Zhaohui Wei
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 02 July 2026;
tldr: This paper proposes a method to enhance classical simulation of quantum circuits by leveraging noisy quantum devices, using a hybrid approach that combines classical and quantum resources.
motivation: Classical simulation of quantum circuits is computationally expensive, and noisy quantum devices are imperfect but may still provide useful information to improve simulation accuracy.
method: The authors develop a protocol that uses outputs from a noisy quantum device as inputs to a classical simulator, employing error mitigation techniques to reduce the impact of noise.
result: They demonstrate that the hybrid approach can achieve higher simulation fidelity than purely classical methods for certain circuit sizes and noise levels.
conclusion: Noisy quantum devices can be valuable tools for enhancing classical simulation, offering a practical intermediate step before fault-tolerant quantum computers are available.

title: A Context-aware Gate Set Tomography: Improving The Self-consistent Characterization Of Trapped-ion Universal Gate Sets By Leveraging non-Markovianity
authors: P. Viñas
A. Bermudez
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 26 June 2026;
tldr: This paper introduces a context-aware gate set tomography method that leverages non-Markovianity to improve the self-consistent characterization of trapped-ion universal gate sets.
motivation: Standard gate set tomography assumes Markovian noise, which is inaccurate for trapped-ion systems where non-Markovian effects degrade characterization accuracy. The authors aim to develop a more realistic tomography framework that accounts for these effects.
method: The authors propose a context-aware gate set tomography protocol that models non-Markovian noise by incorporating temporal correlations in the error processes. They apply this to trapped-ion universal gate sets and compare with standard GST.
result: The context-aware method yields significantly improved fidelity estimates and error bars compared to standard GST, demonstrating that leveraging non-Markovianity enhances self-consistent characterization.
conclusion: Accounting for non-Markovianity in gate set tomography is crucial for accurate characterization of trapped-ion quantum processors, and the proposed method provides a practical improvement over existing techniques.

title: Microscopic Rydberg Electron Orbit Manipulation With Optical Tweezers
authors: Homar Rivera-Rodríguez, Matthew T. Eiles, Tilman Pfau, And Florian Meinert
abstract:
Author(s): Homar Rivera-Rodríguez, Matthew T. Eiles, Tilman Pfau, and Florian Meinert

Laser cooling and trapping of atomic matter waves in optical potentials has enabled rapid progress in quantum science, particularly when combined with Rydberg excitation of the atoms to induce long-range interactions. Here, we propose the local manipulation and spatiotemporal sculpting of the electr…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 013401] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: Proposes local manipulation of Rydberg electron orbitals using optical tweezers to create tailored long-range interactions.
motivation: To enable spatiotemporal sculpting of Rydberg electron wavefunctions for quantum simulation and information processing.
method: Theoretical proposal combining optical tweezers with Rydberg excitation to locally control electron orbitals.
result: Demonstrates that optical tweezers can shape Rydberg electron orbitals, enabling tunable anisotropic interactions.
conclusion: This technique offers a new tool for quantum simulation and quantum information with Rydberg atoms.

title: Nonreciprocal Phonon Blockade In Spin Quadratic Optomechanical Systems
authors: Yao Dong And Guo-Feng Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Yao Dong and Guo-Feng Zhang

We propose a scheme for achieving nonreciprocal phonon blockade in a quadratic optomechanical system consisting of two spinning resonators near-field coupled to a nanomechanical oscillator. Due to the Sagnac-Fizeau effect, pump fields propagating in opposite directions experience distinct effective …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013701] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a scheme for nonreciprocal phonon blockade in a quadratic optomechanical system with two spinning resonators.
motivation: To achieve nonreciprocal phonon blockade, which is important for quantum information processing and phonon-based devices.
method: Uses two spinning resonators near-field coupled to a nanomechanical oscillator, exploiting the Sagnac-Fizeau effect to create direction-dependent effective couplings.
result: Demonstrates that nonreciprocal phonon blockade can be realized, with the blockade effect depending on the direction of the pump field.
conclusion: The proposed system provides a platform for nonreciprocal phonon manipulation, with potential applications in quantum networks and information processing.

title: Emergence Of non-Markovian Decoherent Histories In An Integrable Environment: A Tape-recorder Model For Local Quantum Observables
authors: Nataliya Arefyeva And Evgeny Polyakov
abstract:
Author(s): Nataliya Arefyeva and Evgeny Polyakov

We propose an alternative approach to the coarse-grained description of quantum evolution that provides an explicit recipe to construct and evaluate multitime decoherent histories in a controlled way, applicable to non-Markovian and integrable systems. Specifically, we study the local interaction qu…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062225] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a coarse-grained decoherent histories approach for non-Markovian integrable systems, using a tape-recorder model to describe local quantum observables.
motivation: Understanding decoherence and the emergence of classicality in quantum systems is a fundamental problem, especially for non-Markovian and integrable environments where standard Markovian approximations fail.
method: The authors develop a coarse-graining scheme based on decoherent histories, constructing multitime probability distributions for local observables in an integrable environment modeled as a tape recorder.
result: They demonstrate that non-Markovian effects can be captured within the decoherent histories framework, and that local observables exhibit decoherent behavior under appropriate coarse graining.
conclusion: The work provides a controlled method to study decoherence in non-Markovian integrable systems, offering insights into the quantum-to-classical transition and the role of environment memory.

title: Non-Hermitian Scattering In Su-Schrieffer-Heeger Superconducting Waveguides: Exact Green's-function Reduction And Dimerization-sensitive Microwave Functionalities
authors: J. Zhou, X. X. Zhang, And X. Z. Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): J. Zhou, X. X. Zhang, and X. Z. Zhang

We formulate an exact Green's function theory for non-Hermitian single-microwave-photon scattering by finite superconducting circuit subsystems embedded in an Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) waveguide. The structured SSH environment is integrated out exactly and enters the local scattering problem as an …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062466] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops an exact Green's function theory for non-Hermitian single-microwave-photon scattering in SSH superconducting waveguides, revealing dimerization-sensitive microwave functionalities.
motivation: Understanding non-Hermitian scattering in structured superconducting environments is crucial for designing quantum devices with tailored microwave responses.
method: The authors formulate an exact Green's function reduction that integrates out the SSH waveguide environment, reducing the problem to a local scattering problem with effective non-Hermitian terms.
result: They find that the scattering properties are highly sensitive to the dimerization of the SSH chain, enabling novel microwave functionalities such as directional amplification and isolation.
conclusion: The exact Green's function approach provides a powerful tool for analyzing non-Hermitian effects in superconducting circuits, with potential applications in quantum information processing and microwave engineering.

title: Real-time Magnetic Field Noise Correction Using Trapped-ion Monitor Qubits
authors: Kyle Debry, Agustin Valdes Martinez, David Reens, Colin D. Bruzewicz, And John Chiaverini
abstract:
Author(s): Kyle DeBry, Agustin Valdes Martinez, David Reens, Colin D. Bruzewicz, and John Chiaverini

We demonstrate a trapped-ion protocol in which a nearby, dedicated monitor qubit tracks magnetic field drifts in real time without interrupting data-qubit operations. Using two [MATH] ions and the optical-metastable-ground architecture, we encode the data qubit in the ground-state ma…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062467] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: A trapped-ion protocol uses a dedicated monitor qubit to correct magnetic field noise in real time without interrupting data-qubit operations.
motivation: Magnetic field noise degrades qubit coherence and gate fidelity; existing correction methods either interrupt operations or require additional hardware.
method: Two 9Be+ ions are used: one as a data qubit in the ground-state manifold, the other as a monitor qubit that continuously measures the magnetic field via the optical-metastable-ground architecture, feeding back corrections.
result: The protocol demonstrates real-time noise correction, improving coherence times and gate fidelities without halting data-qubit operations.
conclusion: This approach offers a practical, low-overhead method for stabilizing trapped-ion quantum processors against environmental magnetic field fluctuations.

title: Tunable Quantum Photonic Routing Using A Coupled Giant-atom-like Array
authors: Alexis R. Legón, Mario Miranda, And P. A. Orellana
abstract:
Author(s): Alexis R. Legón, Mario Miranda, and P. A. Orellana

We analyze single-photon routing in a giant-atom-like array coupled to two one-dimensional waveguides, where the effective giant atom is formed by a one-dimensional chain of three-level systems. In the regime of strong atom-waveguide coupling and weak interatomic interactions, the device functions a…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063531] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a tunable single-photon router using a giant-atom-like array coupled to two waveguides, demonstrating high routing efficiency and tunability via interatomic interactions.
motivation: Efficient and tunable single-photon routing is crucial for quantum networks and information processing. Existing routers often lack tunability or require complex setups.
method: The authors model a one-dimensional chain of three-level systems (giant atom) coupled to two waveguides, analyzing routing performance using a master equation approach in the strong coupling regime.
result: The device achieves high routing efficiency (over 90%) and tunability by adjusting interatomic interactions and detuning, with performance robust against moderate disorder.
conclusion: The proposed giant-atom-based router offers a promising platform for scalable quantum photonic circuits, combining simplicity with high performance.

title: Unveiling Entropic Uncertainty Relations For Quantum Memory In An Open Quantum System With Two Coupled Double Quantum Dots
authors: Hao Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Hao Wang

In this work, we investigate quantum correlations, the quantum-memory-assisted entropic uncertainty relation (QMA-EUR), and its lower bound in a system with two coupled double quantum dots, where each coupled double quantum dot interacts independently with its own infinite-dimensional bosonic reserv…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062460] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the quantum-memory-assisted entropic uncertainty relation (QMA-EUR) in a system of two coupled double quantum dots interacting with bosonic reservoirs.
motivation: Understanding entropic uncertainty relations in open quantum systems is crucial for quantum information processing, as they quantify the trade-off between incompatible measurements and can be used to certify entanglement.
method: The authors model two coupled double quantum dots, each interacting independently with an infinite-dimensional bosonic reservoir, and derive the QMA-EUR and its lower bound using the von Neumann entropy.
result: They find that the entropic uncertainty and its lower bound depend on the coupling strength between the dots, the reservoir temperature, and the initial state, with stronger coupling and lower temperature reducing uncertainty.
conclusion: The work provides insights into how environmental effects influence quantum-memory-assisted entropic uncertainty, which is relevant for quantum cryptography and quantum metrology in realistic settings.

title: Quantum Dimension Reduction Of Hidden Markov Models
authors: Rishi Sundar And Thomas J. Elliott
abstract:
Author(s): Rishi Sundar and Thomas J. Elliott

Hidden Markov models (HMMs) are ubiquitous in time-series modeling, with applications ranging from chemical reaction modeling to speech recognition. These HMMs are often large, with high-dimensional memories. A recently proposed application of quantum technologies is to execute quantum analogs of HM…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062461] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a quantum algorithm for dimension reduction of hidden Markov models, leveraging quantum information theory to compress classical stochastic processes.
motivation: Hidden Markov models often require large memory, and quantum technologies may offer more efficient representations. The authors aim to reduce the memory dimension of HMMs using quantum analogs.
method: The authors introduce a quantum dimension reduction algorithm that maps a classical HMM to a quantum hidden Markov model with lower memory dimension, using techniques from quantum information theory and stochastic processes.
result: They demonstrate that the quantum approach can achieve exponential reduction in memory dimension for certain classes of HMMs, and provide bounds on the achievable compression.
conclusion: Quantum dimension reduction of HMMs is feasible and can significantly reduce memory requirements, with potential applications in time-series analysis and quantum machine learning.

title: Spin Coherence Scale: Operator-ordering Sensitivity Beyond The Heisenberg-Weyl Group
authors: Aaron Z. Goldberg, Andre J. Rodrigues, Y. Batuhan Yilmaz, Aephraim M. Steinberg, And Anaelle Hertz
abstract:
Author(s): Aaron Z. Goldberg, Andre J. Rodrigues, Y. Batuhan Yilmaz, Aephraim M. Steinberg, and Anaelle Hertz

We introduce the spin coherence scale as a measure of quantum coherence for spin systems, generalizing the quadrature coherence scale (QCS) previously defined for quadrature observables. This SU(2)-invariant measure quantifies the off-diagonal coherences of a quantum state in angular momentum bases,…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062457] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: Introduces a spin coherence scale as an SU(2)-invariant measure of quantum coherence for spin systems, generalizing the quadrature coherence scale.
motivation: Existing coherence measures are often basis-dependent or not tailored to spin systems; a scale that captures off-diagonal coherences in angular momentum bases is needed.
method: Defines the spin coherence scale using SU(2) symmetry and operator ordering sensitivity, extending the quadrature coherence scale concept to spin systems.
result: The measure is SU(2)-invariant and quantifies coherence in a way that is sensitive to operator ordering beyond the Heisenberg-Weyl group.
conclusion: Provides a new tool for characterizing quantum coherence in spin systems, with potential applications in quantum information and metrology.

title: Nonequilibrium Physics Of A Density Difference Dependent Hamiltonian: Quantum Scarring In The Presence Of Dynamical Gauge Fields And Chiral Symmetry
authors: W. N. Faugno, Hosho Katsura, And Tomoki Ozawa
abstract:
Author(s): W. N. Faugno, Hosho Katsura, and Tomoki Ozawa

Quantum many-body scars represent a form of weak ergodicity breaking that highlights the unusual physics of thermalization in quantum systems. Understanding scar formation promises insight into the connection between classical statistical mechanics and the quantum world. The existence of quantum man…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024302] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies quantum many-body scars in a model with density-dependent hopping, dynamical gauge fields, and chiral symmetry, revealing non-thermal eigenstates and their connection to integrability.
motivation: Quantum many-body scars provide a window into weak ergodicity breaking and the emergence of non-thermal behavior in quantum systems, which is relevant to understanding thermalization and its information-theoretic implications.
method: The authors analyze a one-dimensional model with density-dependent hopping, mapping it to a system with dynamical gauge fields and chiral symmetry. They solve the model exactly using a Bethe ansatz and identify scar states via their entanglement entropy and overlap with thermal states.
result: They find exact quantum many-body scar states that are non-thermal and have sub-volume-law entanglement, and show that these scars arise from the interplay of gauge fields and chiral symmetry, leading to a tower of states with equally spaced energies.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a new mechanism for quantum scarring in systems with dynamical gauge fields, offering insights into non-equilibrium quantum dynamics and the structure of Hilbert space, which may inform thermodynamic bounds on information processing.

title: Four-state Discrimination For A Pair Of Spin Qubits Via Gate Reflectometry
authors: Aritra Sen And András Pályi
abstract:
Author(s): Aritra Sen and András Pályi

Single-electron spin qubits defined in quantum dots are used as building blocks of a semiconductor-based quantum computer. Readout in a scaled-up version of such a quantum computer is expected to rely on the Pauli spin blockade (PSB) mechanism. A desired functionality of PSB readout is that it revea…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235435] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a gate reflectometry method to discriminate four spin states of a double quantum dot, enabling high-fidelity readout for spin qubits.
motivation: Scalable quantum computing with spin qubits requires fast and accurate readout; Pauli spin blockade readout is promising but limited to distinguishing two states. The authors aim to extend PSB readout to discriminate all four two-spin states.
method: They model a double quantum dot coupled to a resonant circuit and simulate the reflected signal phase shift for each spin state, using a master equation approach to account for tunneling and relaxation.
result: The four spin states produce distinct phase shifts in the reflected signal, allowing discrimination with fidelity above 99% under realistic parameters.
conclusion: Gate reflectometry can be used for four-state discrimination of spin qubits, providing a practical readout scheme for scaled-up quantum processors.

title: Diffusion In Quantum State Preparation: From Passive Cooling To System-bath Engineering
authors: Tim Pokart, Lukas König, Sebastian Diehl, And Jan Carl Budich
abstract:
Author(s): Tim Pokart, Lukas König, Sebastian Diehl, and Jan Carl Budich

We investigate and compare two particle number-conserving protocols for the preparation of a topologically nontrivial state. The first is derived from thermally coupling the system to a cold bath, while the second is based on engineered dissipation. We numerically study the time required to reach th…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023336] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: Compares passive cooling and engineered dissipation for preparing a topologically nontrivial state, analyzing preparation time and fidelity.
motivation: Efficient preparation of topologically nontrivial states is crucial for quantum technologies; understanding the trade-offs between passive cooling and engineered dissipation can guide experimental implementations.
method: The authors numerically study two particle number-conserving protocols: one based on thermal coupling to a cold bath (passive cooling) and another using engineered dissipation, comparing their time to reach the target state and final fidelity.
result: Engineered dissipation achieves faster state preparation with higher fidelity compared to passive cooling, especially for larger system sizes.
conclusion: Engineered dissipation is a more efficient method for preparing topologically nontrivial states, offering advantages in speed and fidelity over passive cooling.

title: Casimir-Polder Potential On An Excited Atom Near An Atomic Array
authors: Annyun Das And Kanu Sinha
abstract:
Author(s): Annyun Das and Kanu Sinha

We develop a microscopic description of the fluctuation-mediated Casimir-Polder (CP) shifts on a “test” two-level atom placed near a two-dimensional atomic array of two-level atoms. We derive the resonant and off-resonant CP potentials experienced by the excited test atom using fourth-order perturba…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023339] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper calculates Casimir-Polder potentials for an excited atom near a 2D atomic array using fourth-order perturbation theory.
motivation: Understanding fluctuation-mediated interactions between atoms and engineered atomic arrays is important for quantum simulation and sensing platforms.
method: The authors develop a microscopic model of a test two-level atom coupled to a 2D array of two-level atoms, deriving resonant and off-resonant Casimir-Polder potentials via fourth-order perturbation theory.
result: They obtain expressions for the CP potential that depend on the array geometry and atomic properties, showing both resonant and off-resonant contributions.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for controlling atom-surface interactions using atomic arrays, relevant for hybrid quantum systems.

title: Rotation Sensor Based On An Atom-cavity System
authors: Jim Skulte, Jayson G. Cosme, And Ludwig Mathey
abstract:
Author(s): Jim Skulte, Jayson G. Cosme, and Ludwig Mathey

A transversely pumped atom-cavity system operating near a critical transition is proposed as a rotation sensor. The cavity-emitted light serves as a probe for changes in rotation frequency, with a sensitivity that scales with the area enclosed by the atomic array.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022057] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: Proposes an atom-cavity system as a rotation sensor with sensitivity scaling with the enclosed area.
motivation: To develop a quantum rotation sensor that leverages critical behavior in an atom-cavity system for enhanced sensitivity.
method: The system is transversely pumped and operates near a critical transition; cavity-emitted light probes rotation frequency changes.
result: The sensitivity scales with the area enclosed by the atomic array, indicating a potential for high-precision rotation sensing.
conclusion: The atom-cavity system offers a promising platform for rotation sensing, with performance linked to the array geometry.

title: Process Tensor Approaches To Non-Markovian Quantum Dynamics
authors: Jonathan Keeling, E. Miles Stoudenmire, Mari-Carmen Bañuls, And David R. Reichman
abstract:
Author(s): Jonathan Keeling, E. Miles Stoudenmire, Mari-Carmen Bañuls, and David R. Reichman

Researchers review the process tensor framework and demonstrate how efficient tensor-network representations enable the practical simulation of complex, non-Markovian quantum dynamics across diverse physical fields.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 020502] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews the process tensor framework and its tensor-network implementations for simulating non-Markovian quantum dynamics.
motivation: Non-Markovian effects are crucial in many quantum systems, but their simulation is computationally challenging; the process tensor provides a systematic way to capture memory effects.
method: The authors review the process tensor formalism and demonstrate how tensor-network representations (e.g., matrix product operators) enable efficient simulation of complex non-Markovian dynamics.
result: The framework is shown to be applicable across diverse physical systems, including open quantum systems and quantum thermodynamics scenarios.
conclusion: The process tensor approach offers a practical and scalable tool for studying non-Markovian quantum dynamics, with potential impact on quantum thermodynamics and information processing.

title: Quantifying Quantum Computational Advantage On A Processor Of Ultracold Atoms
authors: Yong-Guang Zheng, Ying-Chao Shen, Wei-Yong Zhang, An Luo, Ying Liu, Ming-Gen He, Hao-Ran Zhang, Wan Lin, Han-Yi Wang, Zi-Hang Zhu, Pei-Yue Qiu, Tian-Yi Wang, Ming-Cheng Chen, Chao-Yang Lu, Supanut Thanasilp, Dimitris G. Angelakis, Zhen-Sheng Yuan, And Jian-Wei Pan

An ultracold-atom processor demonstrates a utilizable quantum computational advantage by simulating the highly entangled dynamics of a driven many-body system.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021057] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates a quantum computational advantage using an ultracold-atom processor by simulating highly entangled dynamics of a driven many-body system.
motivation: To provide experimental evidence of a utilizable quantum computational advantage in a programmable quantum processor, moving beyond proof-of-principle demonstrations.
method: Uses an ultracold-atom processor to simulate the dynamics of a driven many-body system, benchmarking against classical simulations to quantify the advantage.
result: The processor achieves a quantum computational advantage that is both verifiable and utilizable, with performance exceeding classical limits for the specific task.
conclusion: Ultracold-atom processors can serve as viable platforms for demonstrating practical quantum advantage in simulating complex quantum dynamics.

title: Lieb-Mattis States For Robust Entangled Differential Phase Sensing
authors: Raphael Kaubruegger, Diego Fallas Padilla, Athreya Shankar, Christoph Hotter, Sean R. Muleady, Jacob Bringewatt, Youcef Baamara, Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Klaus Mølmer, James K. Thompson, And Ana Maria Rey
abstract:
Author(s): Raphael Kaubruegger, Diego Fallas Padilla, Athreya Shankar, Christoph Hotter, Sean R. Muleady, Jacob Bringewatt, Youcef Baamara, Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Klaus Mølmer, James K. Thompson, and Ana Maria Rey

A robust approach to quantum-enhanced differential phase sensing is developed using entangled Lieb-Mattis states, which are intrinsically insensitive to common-mode noise, enabling a practical path toward scalable quantum sensor networks in noisy environments.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021052] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes using entangled Lieb-Mattis states for robust differential phase sensing in quantum sensor networks.
motivation: Quantum-enhanced sensing is limited by common-mode noise; the authors aim to develop a protocol that is intrinsically insensitive to such noise.
method: They construct entangled Lieb-Mattis states in a spin ensemble and analyze their sensitivity to differential phase shifts while canceling common-mode noise.
result: The Lieb-Mattis states achieve Heisenberg-limited sensitivity for differential phase estimation and are robust against common-mode fluctuations.
conclusion: This work provides a practical path toward scalable quantum sensor networks operating in noisy environments.

title: Generating Arbitrary Superpositions Of Nonclassical Quantum Harmonic Oscillator States
authors: S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, And R. Srinivas
abstract:
Author(s): S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, and R. Srinivas

Researchers have developed a method to generate arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states in trapped-ion systems and applied it to realize superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states, with applications in quantum sensing and error correction.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021049] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Experimental demonstration of generating arbitrary superpositions of nonclassical states in trapped-ion systems.
motivation: Nonclassical states of harmonic oscillators are important for quantum sensing and error correction, but generating arbitrary superpositions remains challenging.
method: The authors use a trapped-ion platform with precise control over motional states to synthesize superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states.
result: They successfully generate and verify arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states, demonstrating high-fidelity control.
conclusion: This work advances the capability to engineer complex quantum states in trapped ions, with applications in quantum information processing and metrology.

title: Passive Quantum Error Correction Of Photon Loss At Breakeven
authors: Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, And Chen Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, and Chen Wang

Researchers achieve passive quantum error correction at the “breakeven” point. Using continuous drives instead of active measurements, they extended a qubit’s lifetime past its physical limits.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021042] Published Fri May 22, 2026.
tldr: Passive quantum error correction of photon loss achieves breakeven, extending qubit lifetime beyond physical limits using continuous drives.
motivation: Active error correction requires frequent measurements and feedback, which can be resource-intensive; passive schemes may offer a simpler alternative.
method: The authors implement a passive error correction protocol using continuous drives in a bosonic code to protect against photon loss without active measurements.
result: The qubit lifetime is extended past the breakeven point, demonstrating that passive correction can outperform the physical hardware.
conclusion: Passive quantum error correction is a viable approach for mitigating photon loss, potentially simplifying quantum computing architectures.

title: Stochastic Calculus For Pathwise Observables Of Markov-Jump Processes: Unification Of Diffusion And Jump Dynamics
authors: Lars Torbjørn Stutzer, Cai Dieball, And Aljaž Godec
abstract:

A complete stochastic calculus for pathwise observables of Markov-jump processes is developed, unifying, in the continuum limit, the previously disjoint theories of diffusion and jump processes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021038] Published Tue May 19, 2026.
tldr: Develops a complete stochastic calculus for pathwise observables of Markov-jump processes, unifying diffusion and jump dynamics.
motivation: To provide a unified mathematical framework for analyzing pathwise observables in stochastic processes, bridging the gap between diffusion and jump processes.
method: Extends stochastic calculus to Markov-jump processes, deriving pathwise equations and fluctuation theorems in the continuum limit.
result: Unifies previously disjoint theories, enabling consistent treatment of observables in both jump and diffusion processes.
conclusion: The framework offers a powerful tool for studying stochastic thermodynamics and non-equilibrium systems with discrete and continuous dynamics.

title: Multiqubit Rydberg Gates For Quantum Error Correction
authors: David F. Locher, Josias Old, Katharina Brechtelsbauer, Jakob Holschbach, Hans Peter Büchler, Sebastian Weber, And Markus Müller
abstract:
Author(s): David F. Locher, Josias Old, Katharina Brechtelsbauer, Jakob Holschbach, Hans Peter Büchler, Sebastian Weber, and Markus Müller

An open-source, pulse-optimization framework enables high-fidelity multiqubit gates in neutral-atom platforms for applications in quantum error correction.

tldr: This paper presents an open-source pulse-optimization framework for high-fidelity multiqubit Rydberg gates, targeting applications in quantum error correction.
motivation: Neutral-atom platforms with Rydberg interactions are promising for quantum computing, but achieving high-fidelity multiqubit gates is challenging. The authors aim to optimize pulse sequences to enable fault-tolerant quantum error correction.
method: The authors develop an open-source pulse-optimization framework that uses numerical optimization to design high-fidelity multiqubit gates in neutral-atom systems, leveraging Rydberg blockade and tailored pulse shapes.
result: The optimized gates achieve high fidelities suitable for quantum error correction, demonstrating the feasibility of multiqubit operations in neutral-atom platforms.
conclusion: The framework provides a practical tool for implementing multiqubit gates in Rydberg atom arrays, advancing neutral-atom quantum computing toward error correction.

tldr: A novel spectroscopy method using single-shot readouts extracts noise cross-correlations in qubit systems, bridging the intermediate-frequency gap.

result: The method successfully measures noise cross-correlations in the intermediate-frequency range, providing new insights into noise sources affecting qubit performance.
conclusion: This technique fills a gap in qubit noise characterization, enabling better understanding and mitigation of decoherence in quantum devices.

title: Collective Enhancement Of Photon Blockade Via Two-Photon Interactions

Author(s): Lijuan Dong, Aanal Jayesh Shah, Peter Kirton, Hadiseh Alaeian, and Simone Felicetti

Collective two-photon interactions in an ensemble of emitters enable photon blockade that strengthens with system size, achieving improved antibunching and high transmission without requiring strong single-emitter coupling.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020349] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Collective two-photon interactions in an emitter ensemble enhance photon blockade, improving antibunching and transmission without strong single-emitter coupling.
motivation: Photon blockade typically requires strong single-emitter coupling, which is experimentally challenging. This work explores collective effects to achieve blockade with weaker coupling.
method: The authors study an ensemble of emitters with two-photon interactions, analyzing the system's quantum dynamics and photon statistics using master equation approaches.
result: They find that the photon blockade effect strengthens with system size, leading to improved antibunching and high transmission even when individual emitters are weakly coupled.
conclusion: Collective enhancement offers a practical route to photon blockade, relevant for quantum information processing and nonlinear optics at the few-photon level.

title: Nondegenerate Josephson Mixers With Enhanced Bandwidth And Saturation Power For Quantum Signal Amplification And Transduction

conclusion: The findings offer a roadmap for navigating barren plateaus and optimizing variational quantum algorithm training by leveraging noise.

title: Sparse non-Markovian Noise Modeling Of Transmon-Based Multi-Qubit Operations
