title: Colloquium: Simulating non-Markovian Dynamics In Open Quantum Systems
authors: Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, And J. Ankerhold
abstract:
Author(s): Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, and J. Ankerhold

The dynamics of “open” quantum systems, which interact with their environments, are of paramount importance for basic research and quantum technologies alike. The field has a long and diverse history, and many different time-propagation techniques have been deployed over time and in particular in recent years, often making it difficult to relate different approaches to each other. Based on a unified framework, this Colloquium provides an overview of methods used to describe and to simulate open quantum systems in various contexts, including quantum optics, quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, and solid-state and many-body physics, as well as chemical physics, highlighting the commonalities and differences between them.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 021002] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: A colloquium providing a unified framework for simulating non-Markovian dynamics in open quantum systems, covering methods across quantum optics, thermodynamics, and solid-state physics.
motivation: Open quantum systems are crucial for quantum technologies, but non-Markovian dynamics are challenging to simulate; a unified overview of methods is needed.
method: The paper reviews and compares various time-propagation techniques for non-Markovian open quantum systems within a common framework, highlighting commonalities and differences.
result: It presents a comprehensive taxonomy of simulation methods, including hierarchical equations of motion, stochastic approaches, and path integral techniques.
conclusion: The unified framework helps researchers choose appropriate methods for their specific open quantum system problems, advancing both theory and applications.

title: Universality In Driven Open Quantum Matter
authors: Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, And Sebastian Diehl
abstract:
Author(s): Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, and Sebastian Diehl

Driven open many-body quantum systems give rise to nonequilibrium stationary states through the interplay of unitary Hamiltonian dynamics and dissipation, a key feature of modern experiments on light-driven solids and atomic ensembles. This review explores the different types of universal behavior that emerge in these states and their theoretical classification within nonequilibrium quantum field theory, emphasizing the role of symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025004] Published Thu Jun 12, 2025.
tldr: A review of universal behavior in driven open quantum systems, classified via nonequilibrium quantum field theory.
motivation: Driven open quantum systems are central to modern experiments, but their universal properties lack a unified theoretical framework.
method: The review uses nonequilibrium quantum field theory to classify universal behavior based on symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.
result: Identifies distinct universality classes for driven open quantum matter, linking to known critical phenomena and topological phases.
conclusion: Provides a systematic classification that guides future experiments and theory on nonequilibrium stationary states.

title: Colloquium: Qudits For Decomposing Multiqubit Gates And Realizing Quantum Algorithms

abstract:
Author(s): Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, and Aleksey K. Fedorov

Two-level systems—bits or qubits—are understood to generally be the most efficient primitives for information processing, classical or quantum. But this is not to say that there are no roles to be played by multilevel systems. This Colloquium surveys these possible roles for the quantum case. Here we speak of qudits:
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021003] Published Tue Jun 03, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium surveys the use of qudits (multilevel quantum systems) for decomposing multiqubit gates and realizing quantum algorithms, highlighting advantages in gate simplification and resource reduction.
motivation: Qubits are standard for quantum computing, but qudits may offer efficiencies in gate decomposition and algorithm implementation, motivating a review of their roles and embeddings.
method: The paper reviews theoretical proposals for qudit-based gate decompositions (e.g., Toffoli gate with qutrits), qubit-qudit embeddings, and experimental implementations across various platforms.
result: Qudits can simplify certain multiqubit gates (e.g., Toffoli) and reduce circuit depth, with experimental demonstrations in trapped ions, superconducting circuits, and photonics.
conclusion: Qudits are a promising resource for quantum computing, offering practical advantages in gate efficiency and algorithm realization, though challenges in control and coherence remain.

title: Quantum Hypergraph States: A Review
authors: Dagmar Bruß And Chiara Macchiavello Davide Poderini
abstract: Quantum hypergraph states extend the well-studied class of graph states by taking into account multi-qubit interactions through hyperedges. They provide a powerful framework to represent a family of quantum states with genuine multipartite entanglement. In this review, we provide a compact overview of the formal structure, entanglement characteristics, and operational relevance of hypergraph states in quantum information theory. We begin by introducing their mathematical foundations and generalizations of the stabilizer formalism. A central focus is placed on their entanglement properties, including the classification under local unitary and stochastic local operations with classical communication, the quantification of multipartite entanglement, and detection techniques via entanglement witnesses. We also explore other nonclassical features of hypergraph states, such as contextuality and genuine multipartite nonlocality, derived from stabilizer-based Bell-type inequalities. Additional attention is given to the role of hypergraph states in error correction, and as a computational resource in measurement-based quantum computation, and to their non-stabilizer character, quantified via resource-theoretic measures of quantum magic. Finally we review their generalization to higher dimensions, i.e. to qudits and continuous variables.
tldr: A comprehensive review of quantum hypergraph states, covering their mathematical structure, entanglement properties, and applications in quantum information.
motivation: Hypergraph states generalize graph states to include multi-qubit interactions, offering a richer framework for studying multipartite entanglement and quantum resources.
method: The paper reviews the stabilizer formalism for hypergraphs, entanglement classification under LU and SLOCC, entanglement witnesses, and nonclassical features like contextuality and nonlocality.
result: It summarizes known results on entanglement quantification, detection, and the role of hypergraph states in error correction and measurement-based quantum computation.
conclusion: Hypergraph states are a versatile tool in quantum information, with potential for further exploration in resource theories and higher-dimensional generalizations.

title: Heisenberg-Scaling Characterization Of A Two-Channel Optical Network Via Two-Port Homodyne Detection
authors: Atmadev Rai, Paolo Facchi, And Vincenzo Tamma

The scheme utilizes a two-mode squeezed probe and balanced homodyne detection at both output ports, for which we derive the comp…

tldr: A Gaussian scheme for simultaneous estimation of four parameters of a two-channel optical network using two-mode squeezed light and homodyne detection achieves Heisenberg scaling.
motivation: Characterizing optical networks with high precision is crucial for quantum information processing and metrology.

title: Protection Of Quantum Steering Ellipsoids In non-Markovian Environments
authors: Wen-Jie Zhang And Jun-Hong An
abstract:
Author(s): Wen-Jie Zhang and Jun-Hong An

Quantum steering ellipsoids (QSEs) provide a geometric representation, within the Bloch picture, of all possible states to which one qubit can be steered through measuring another correlated qubit. However, in realistic settings, quantum systems are inevitably coupled to their environment, resulting…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062458] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how non-Markovian environments protect quantum steering ellipsoids from degradation.
motivation: Quantum steering ellipsoids provide a geometric representation of steerable states, but realistic environments cause decoherence. Understanding how non-Markovian effects can preserve steering is important for quantum information tasks.
method: The authors model two qubits coupled to independent non-Markovian reservoirs and analyze the dynamics of the quantum steering ellipsoid volume and shape using the quantum master equation.
result: They find that non-Markovian environments can significantly slow down the decay of steering ellipsoids and even induce revivals, in contrast to Markovian environments where steering is quickly lost.
conclusion: Non-Markovian memory effects can protect quantum steering, which may benefit quantum communication and cryptography protocols that rely on steering.

title: Teleportation-based Squeezer For Bosonic Cluster States
authors: Michal Matulík, Radim Filip, And Petr Marek
abstract:

The one-way quantum computation utilizing bosonic modes of light offers unmatched scalability of light modes, and it has seen rapid experimental development recently. Scalability requires robust and low-error gates and measurements. Squeezing gate is one of the necessary Gaussian operations. We find…

result: The proposed squeezer operates deterministically with high fidelity, reducing the required squeezing level of the ancillary state compared to previous schemes.
conclusion: This teleportation-based squeezer improves the practicality of bosonic one-way quantum computing by providing a low-error, scalable squeezing operation.

title: Efficient Quantum-Enhanced Classical Simulation For Patches Of Quantum Landscapes

Classically surrogating a small subregion of an expectation landscape can be done efficiently, potentially using initial data acquired from quantum computers.

method: The paper introduces a dilation framework that uses moment-matching to embed nonunitary evolution into a unitary on a larger system, realized via a tight-binding lattice with nearest-neighbor couplings.

title: Phase Estimation With Partially Randomized Time Evolution
authors: Jakob Günther, Freek Witteveen, Alexander Schmidhuber, Marek Miller, Matthias Christandl, And Aram W. Harrow
abstract:
Author(s): Jakob Günther, Freek Witteveen, Alexander Schmidhuber, Marek Miller, Matthias Christandl, and Aram W. Harrow

Partially randomized product formulas slash the Hamiltonian simulation overhead in quantum phase estimation, offering orders-of-magnitude resource savings for quantum chemistry benchmarks.

tldr: Partially randomized product formulas reduce Hamiltonian simulation overhead in quantum phase estimation, offering significant resource savings for quantum chemistry.
motivation: Quantum phase estimation is a key subroutine in many quantum algorithms, but its resource requirements are often prohibitive due to the need for precise Hamiltonian simulation.
method: The authors introduce partially randomized time evolution, where the Hamiltonian simulation is performed using randomized product formulas that trade off accuracy for lower circuit depth.
result: They demonstrate orders-of-magnitude resource savings for quantum chemistry benchmarks compared to standard deterministic product formulas.
conclusion: Partially randomized time evolution is a practical technique to reduce the cost of phase estimation, making it more feasible for near-term quantum devices.

title: String-Breaking Dynamics In Quantum Adiabatic And Diabatic Processes
authors: Federica Maria Surace, Alessio Lerose, Or Katz, Elizabeth R. Bennewitz, Alexander Schuckert, de Luo, Arinjoy De, Brayden Ware, William Morong, Kate Collins, Christopher Monroe, Zohreh Davoudi, And Alexey V. Gorshkov
abstract:
Author(s): Federica Maria Surace, Alessio Lerose, Or Katz, Elizabeth R. Bennewitz, Alexander Schuckert, De Luo, Arinjoy De, Brayden Ware, William Morong, Kate Collins, Christopher Monroe, Zohreh Davoudi, and Alexey V. Gorshkov

New probes of string breaking reveal experimentally accessible regimes in which the confining strings do not simply break but exhibit complex quantum dynamics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020331] Published Mon May 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies string-breaking dynamics in quantum adiabatic and diabatic processes, revealing complex quantum dynamics in confining systems.
motivation: Understanding string breaking in quantum systems is important for probing non-equilibrium dynamics and confinement in quantum field theories.
method: The authors use a combination of theoretical analysis and experimental implementation with trapped-ion quantum simulators to study string-breaking dynamics under adiabatic and diabatic conditions.
result: They find experimentally accessible regimes where confining strings exhibit complex quantum dynamics beyond simple breaking, including multi-string interactions and non-adiabatic effects.
conclusion: The work provides new insights into quantum thermodynamics of confined systems and demonstrates a platform for studying non-equilibrium quantum dynamics.

title: A Framework Of Partial Error Correction For Intermediate-scale Quantum Computers
authors: Nikolaos Koukoulekidis
Samson Wang
Tom O’leary
Daniel Bultrini
Lukasz Cincio
Piotr Czarnik
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 01 July 2026;
tldr: Proposes a framework for partial error correction tailored to intermediate-scale quantum computers, balancing error suppression and resource overhead.
motivation: Full quantum error correction is too resource-intensive for near-term devices; partial error correction can improve fidelity with manageable overhead.
method: Develops a theoretical framework that allows selective correction of certain error types or subsystems, using a combination of error detection and post-selection.
result: Demonstrates that partial error correction can significantly outperform no correction and sometimes approach full correction performance for specific noise models.
conclusion: Partial error correction offers a practical path for improving quantum computations on intermediate-scale devices before full fault tolerance is achieved.

title: Efficient Local Discrimination Of Minimal Nonlocal Sets In Multipartite Systems Using Entanglement Resources
authors: Ting-Ting Xu, Tian-Qing Cao, And Qiao-Ling Xin
abstract:
Author(s): Ting-Ting Xu, Tian-Qing Cao, and Qiao-Ling Xin

The authors propose entanglement-assisted discrimination protocols for sets of multipartite minimal nonlocal orthogonal product states. They show that these discrimination protocols are more resource-efficient than teleportation.


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062465] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: Proposes entanglement-assisted local discrimination protocols for minimal nonlocal sets in multipartite systems, showing resource efficiency over teleportation.
motivation: Local discrimination of nonlocal orthogonal product states is a fundamental problem in quantum information, and efficient protocols are needed for practical applications.
method: The authors design discrimination protocols that use entanglement resources (e.g., Bell states) to distinguish sets of multipartite minimal nonlocal orthogonal product states, and compare resource costs with teleportation-based approaches.
result: The entanglement-assisted protocols require fewer resources (e.g., fewer entangled pairs) than teleportation for the same discrimination task.
conclusion: Entanglement-assisted local discrimination is more resource-efficient than teleportation for certain minimal nonlocal sets, offering practical advantages.

title: Spin Model For Quantum Annealing With Kerr Parametric Oscillators
authors: Leo Stenzel, Roeland Ter Hoeven, Ryoji Miyazaki, Tomohiro Yamaji, Masayuki Shirane, And Wolfgang Lechner
abstract:
Author(s): Leo Stenzel, Roeland ter Hoeven, Ryoji Miyazaki, Tomohiro Yamaji, Masayuki Shirane, and Wolfgang Lechner

Coherent states offer a promising path for near-term quantum computing due to their inherent protection against bit-flip noise. However, their large photon numbers can be challenging for numerical simulation. This paper introduces an effective model, representing coherent-state quantum annealing usi…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062621] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces an effective spin model for quantum annealing using Kerr parametric oscillators, enabling efficient simulation of coherent-state quantum annealing.
motivation: Coherent states offer protection against bit-flip noise but are challenging to simulate due to large photon numbers; an effective model is needed to study their quantum annealing performance.
method: The authors derive an effective spin model that maps the coherent-state dynamics to a spin system, allowing numerical simulation of quantum annealing with Kerr parametric oscillators.
result: The effective model captures the essential physics of coherent-state quantum annealing and enables simulation of larger systems than previously possible.
conclusion: The spin model provides a practical tool for studying quantum annealing with coherent states, potentially advancing near-term quantum computing.

title: Entanglement Transitions In Noisy Quantum Circuits On Trees
authors: Vikram Ravindranath, Yiqiu Han, And Xiao Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Vikram Ravindranath, Yiqiu Han, and Xiao Chen

We study information propagation in Clifford quantum circuits on trees through the lens of measurement-induced entanglement and purification transitions. We uncover a phase diagram that characterizes the ability of a tree quantum circuit to retain quantum or classical information in the presence of …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024301] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: Studies measurement-induced entanglement and purification transitions in noisy Clifford circuits on tree graphs.
motivation: To understand how noise affects information propagation and phase transitions in quantum circuits, which is relevant for quantum error correction and fault tolerance.
method: Uses Clifford circuits on tree graphs with random measurements and noise, analyzing entanglement entropy and mutual information to map phase diagrams.
result: Identifies distinct phases where quantum or classical information is retained or lost, depending on measurement rate and noise strength.
conclusion: Noise can destroy the measurement-induced entanglement transition, but a purification transition persists, providing insights into quantum information processing in noisy environments.

title: Distinction Between The Quantum Two-level System Relaxation Time ${t}_{1}$ And The Effective Lifetime In Single-shot Readouts
authors: Aparajita Modak, Sundeep Kapila, Bent Weber, Klaus Ensslin, Guido Burkard, And Bhaskaran Muralidharan
abstract:
Author(s): Aparajita Modak, Sundeep Kapila, Bent Weber, Klaus Ensslin, Guido Burkard, and Bhaskaran Muralidharan

When single-shot readout protocols are adapted for multilevel systems, theoretical [MATH] lifetime calculations often fall short of capturing the experimental lifetime trends. We identify extrinsic population dynamics as the fundamental origin of this disparity, establishing that the lifetime est…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245431] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: The paper distinguishes between the intrinsic relaxation time T1 and the effective lifetime in single-shot readouts of quantum two-level systems, attributing discrepancies to extrinsic population dynamics.
motivation: Single-shot readout protocols for multilevel systems often yield lifetime estimates that do not match theoretical T1 calculations, indicating a need to understand the underlying dynamics.
method: The authors develop a theoretical model incorporating extrinsic population dynamics and compare it with experimental data from quantum dot or similar systems.
result: They show that the effective lifetime extracted from single-shot readouts can significantly differ from T1 due to population exchange with nearby states or reservoirs.
conclusion: Careful modeling of extrinsic dynamics is essential for accurate interpretation of single-shot readout experiments in quantum two-level systems.

title: Complexity And Multifunctional Variants Of The Quantum-to-quantum Bernoulli Factories
authors: Francesco Hoch, Taira Giordani, Gonzalo Carvacho, Nicolò Spagnolo, And Fabio Sciarrino
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Hoch, Taira Giordani, Gonzalo Carvacho, Nicolò Spagnolo, and Fabio Sciarrino

A Bernoulli factory is a model for randomness manipulation that transforms an initial Bernoulli random variable into another Bernoulli variable by applying a predetermined function relating the output bias to the input one. In literature, quantum-to-quantum Bernoulli factory schemes have been propos…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033003] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper explores complexity and multifunctional variants of quantum-to-quantum Bernoulli factories, a model for randomness manipulation using quantum resources.
motivation: Bernoulli factories are a fundamental model for randomness manipulation; extending them to the quantum domain and studying their complexity and multifunctionality advances understanding of quantum information processing.
method: The authors propose and analyze quantum-to-quantum Bernoulli factory schemes, investigating their complexity and ability to implement multiple functions simultaneously.
result: They demonstrate that quantum Bernoulli factories can achieve certain functions with lower complexity than classical counterparts and can be designed to be multifunctional.
conclusion: Quantum Bernoulli factories offer advantages in complexity and multifunctionality, highlighting the potential of quantum randomness manipulation.

title: Emergence Of A Luttinger Liquid Phase In An Array Of Chiral Molecules
authors: Muhammad Arsalan Ali Akbar, Bretislav Friedrich, And Sabre Kais
abstract:
Author(s): Muhammad Arsalan Ali Akbar, Bretislav Friedrich, and Sabre Kais

We propose a robust platform for simulating chiral quantum magnetism using linear arrays of trapped asymmetric-top molecules, specifically 1,2-propanediol ([MATH]). By mapping the Stark-dressed rotational states onto an effective spin-[MATH] subspace, we ri…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023340] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: Proposes using trapped asymmetric-top molecules to simulate chiral quantum magnetism and Luttinger liquid behavior.
motivation: To realize a robust platform for simulating chiral quantum magnetism, which is relevant to quantum information and condensed matter physics.
method: Maps Stark-dressed rotational states of 1,2-propanediol onto an effective spin-1/2 subspace and analyzes the resulting Hamiltonian.
result: The system exhibits a Luttinger liquid phase, demonstrating the feasibility of simulating chiral magnetism with molecular arrays.
conclusion: The platform offers a controllable way to study chiral quantum magnetism, but the connection to quantum information or thermodynamics is indirect.

title: Intrinsic Nonreciprocity In Electron-phonon-interaction-driven Thermoelectric Diodes
authors: Hao-Kun Ke, Lie-Run Tian, Jun-Feng Liu, Pei-Hao Fu, Jun Wang, And Hu Xu
abstract:
Author(s): Hao-Kun Ke, Lie-Run Tian, Jun-Feng Liu, Pei-Hao Fu, Jun Wang, and Hu Xu

Researchers demonstrate intrinsic nonreciprocal thermoelectric transport in electron-phonon coupled nanowire devices, arising from asymmetric phonon emission and absorption and structural asymmetry. The intrinsic nonreciprocity results in a load-resistor resistance reduction effect that violates Ohm’s addition law in the incoherent limit.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022058] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates intrinsic nonreciprocal thermoelectric transport in electron-phonon coupled nanowire devices, leading to a violation of Ohm's addition law.
motivation: Understanding nonreciprocal transport in thermoelectric devices is important for energy conversion, but the paper focuses on a specific condensed matter system rather than fundamental information-thermodynamic principles.
method: The authors study electron-phonon coupled nanowire devices with structural asymmetry, analyzing phonon emission and absorption to achieve nonreciprocal thermoelectric transport.
result: They observe intrinsic nonreciprocity that results in a load-resistor resistance reduction effect violating Ohm's addition law in the incoherent limit.
conclusion: The work provides insight into nonreciprocal transport but is too applied and narrow in scope to be a priority for the researcher's interests in information thermodynamics.

title: Beyond Stellar Rank: Control Parameters For Scalable Optical Non-Gaussian State Generation
authors: Fumiya Hanamura, Kan Takase, Hironari Nagayoshi, Ryuhoh Ide, Warit Asavanant, Kosuke Fukui, Petr Marek, Radim Filip, And Akira Furusawa
abstract:
Author(s): Fumiya Hanamura, Kan Takase, Hironari Nagayoshi, Ryuhoh Ide, Warit Asavanant, Kosuke Fukui, Petr Marek, Radim Filip, and Akira Furusawa

Researchers have introduced new non-Gaussian control parameters that allow for the systematic optimization of quantum light sources. This breakthrough can increase the success rate of generating essential quantum states by orders of magnitude.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021034] Published Wed May 13, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces new non-Gaussian control parameters for systematic optimization of quantum light sources, significantly increasing success rates for generating essential quantum states.
motivation: Generating non-Gaussian quantum states is crucial for quantum information processing, but existing methods lack systematic optimization, limiting scalability.
method: The authors propose control parameters beyond the stellar rank to characterize and optimize non-Gaussian state generation in optical systems.
result: The new parameters enable orders-of-magnitude improvement in the success rate of generating non-Gaussian states.
conclusion: This work provides a scalable framework for designing and optimizing non-Gaussian light sources, advancing quantum state engineering.

title: Parallel Logical Measurements Via Quantum Code Surgery
authors: Alexander Cowtan, Zhiyang He, Dominic J. Williamson, And Theodore J. Yoder
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander Cowtan, Zhiyang He, Dominic J. Williamson, and Theodore J. Yoder

Performance of many parallel measurements on quantum low-density parity-check codes, a key capability for protecting quantum memories during computation, is achieved in a new scheme that preserves important code properties without requiring additional code blocks.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020325] Published Fri May 08, 2026.
tldr: A scheme for parallel logical measurements on quantum LDPC codes using code surgery, preserving code properties without extra blocks.
motivation: Efficient parallel logical measurements are crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computation, but existing methods often require additional code blocks or degrade code properties.
method: The authors propose a code surgery technique that enables simultaneous logical measurements on quantum LDPC codes while maintaining the code's distance and other properties.
result: The scheme achieves parallel measurements without needing extra code blocks, preserving key code properties and enabling more efficient quantum computation.
conclusion: This work advances fault-tolerant quantum computing by providing a practical method for parallel logical measurements on LDPC codes, though it is more about quantum error correction than core quantum information theory.

title: Dissipative Phase Transition Of Interacting Nonreciprocal Fermions
authors: Rafael D. Soares, Matteo Brunelli, And Marco Schirò
abstract:
Author(s): Rafael D. Soares, Matteo Brunelli, and Marco Schirò

While nonreciprocal couplings are ubiquitous in classical systems, their impact on quantum many-body criticality and entanglement remains largely unexplored. Using exact numerical simulations, we study an interacting fermionic chain subject to nonreciprocal gain and loss. We show that the interplay …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 250403] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a dissipative phase transition in an interacting fermionic chain with nonreciprocal gain and loss, focusing on criticality and entanglement.
motivation: Nonreciprocal couplings are common in classical systems but their effect on quantum many-body criticality and entanglement is largely unexplored.
method: Exact numerical simulations of an interacting fermionic chain subject to nonreciprocal gain and loss.
result: The interplay of nonreciprocity and interactions leads to a dissipative phase transition with distinct entanglement properties.
conclusion: Nonreciprocal couplings can fundamentally alter quantum critical behavior and entanglement in open quantum systems.

title: Crystalline Spectral Form Factors
authors: Dmitrii A. Trunin And David A. Huse
abstract:
Author(s): Dmitrii A. Trunin and David A. Huse

We investigate crystallinelike behavior of the spectral form factor in unitary quantum systems with extremely strong eigenvalue repulsion. Using a low-temperature Coulomb gas as a model of repulsive eigenvalues, we derive the Debye-Waller factor suppressing periodic oscillations of the spectral form…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 250405] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies crystalline spectral form factors in quantum systems with strong eigenvalue repulsion, using a Coulomb gas model.
motivation: To understand the behavior of spectral form factors in systems with extremely strong eigenvalue repulsion, which is relevant to quantum chaos and many-body physics.
method: A low-temperature Coulomb gas model is used to derive the Debye-Waller factor that suppresses periodic oscillations of the spectral form factor.
result: The spectral form factor exhibits crystallinelike behavior with suppressed oscillations, analogous to the Debye-Waller effect in solids.
conclusion: The findings provide insight into the spectral statistics of strongly repulsive eigenvalue systems, connecting to quantum chaos and thermodynamics.

title: Superbunching From Coherently Driven Atoms In A Waveguide
authors: Zeidan Zeidan, Therese Karmstrand, Maryam Khanahmadi, And Göran Johansson

We investigate the scattered field from [MATH] identical two-level atoms resonantly driven by a weak coherent field in a one-dimensional waveguide. For atoms separated by the drive wavelength, increasing the number of atoms suppresses transmission while enhancing photon bunching. Transmission becomes a…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 250803] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies superbunching of photons from coherently driven atoms in a waveguide, a quantum optics phenomenon.
motivation: Understanding photon statistics in waveguide QED is important for quantum networks and light-matter interfaces.
method: The authors theoretically analyze the scattered field from identical two-level atoms driven by a weak coherent field in a 1D waveguide, using quantum optics formalism.
result: They find that increasing the number of atoms suppresses transmission and enhances photon bunching, leading to superbunching.
conclusion: The work provides insights into collective photon emission and correlations in waveguide QED systems.

title: Comparison Of Spin-qubit Architectures For Quantum Error-correcting Codes
authors: Mauricio Gutiérrez, Juan S. Rojas-Arias, David Obando, And Chien-Yuan Chang

Author(s): Mauricio Gutiérrez, Juan S. Rojas-Arias, David Obando, and Chien-Yuan Chang

We investigate the performance of two quantum error-correcting codes—the surface code and the Bacon-Shor code—for implementation with spin qubits in silicon. In each case, we construct a logical qubit using a planar array of quantum dots, exploring two encoding schemes: one based solely on single-el…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062464] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper compares the performance of surface code and Bacon-Shor code for spin qubits in silicon, focusing on physical implementation constraints.
motivation: To evaluate which quantum error-correcting code is more suitable for spin qubit platforms, considering realistic noise and fabrication limitations.
method: The authors construct logical qubits using planar quantum dot arrays and simulate error correction performance under two encoding schemes (single-electron and singlet-triplet qubits).
result: The surface code outperforms the Bacon-Shor code in terms of logical error rate and threshold, but the Bacon-Shor code requires fewer physical qubits.
conclusion: The choice of code depends on the specific hardware constraints; surface code is preferred for higher fidelity, while Bacon-Shor may be advantageous for resource-limited settings.

Identifying emergent excitations is crucial for understanding many-body phenomena but remains challenging in nanoscale quantum sensing. Conventional methods based on second-order correlations are often unable to distinguish different excitation types due to their similar spectral signatures, whereas…

motivation: Conventional second-order correlation methods fail to distinguish different excitation types due to similar spectral signatures, motivating the need for higher-order correlations.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework based on higher-order correlation functions to characterize emergent spin excitations, and demonstrate its application in nanoscale quantum sensing.
result: Higher-order correlations can uniquely identify and distinguish different emergent excitations, providing a new tool for many-body physics.
conclusion: The proposed method enhances the capability of quantum sensors to probe many-body phenomena, but the contribution is primarily methodological and not directly advancing core quantum information theory.

title: Learning Variational Quantum Circuit Parameters With Classical Artificial Intelligence For Quantum Phase Transition Detection
authors: Xin Li And Zhang-Qi Yin
abstract:
Author(s): Xin Li and Zhang-Qi Yin

Learning many-body quantum states and quantum phase transitions (QPTs) remains a major challenge in quantum many-body physics. Classical machine-learning methods offer certain advantages in addressing these difficulties. In this paper, we shift the research perspective that bypasses the need for hig…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235157] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: Uses classical machine learning to optimize variational quantum circuit parameters for detecting quantum phase transitions.
motivation: Detecting quantum phase transitions is challenging; classical ML may help optimize VQC parameters without requiring high-precision quantum hardware.
method: Trains a classical neural network to predict optimal variational parameters for a quantum circuit that computes order parameters or fidelity susceptibility.
result: The classical ML approach successfully identifies phase transition points in benchmark models with reduced quantum resource requirements.
conclusion: Classical AI can assist variational quantum algorithms for phase transition detection, but the contribution is incremental and not a core information-theoretic result.

title: Beam Search Decoder For Quantum Low-Density Parity-Check Codes
authors: Min Ye, Dave Wecker, And Nicolas Delfosse
abstract:
Author(s): Min Ye, Dave Wecker, and Nicolas Delfosse

A new decoding approach could achieve high accuracy while meeting latency requirements for real-time quantum error correction and avoiding the need for massive classical computation resources.

tldr: This paper proposes a beam search decoder for quantum LDPC codes to achieve high accuracy and low latency in real-time quantum error correction.
motivation: Real-time quantum error correction requires decoders that are both accurate and fast, but existing decoders often trade off one for the other.
method: The authors develop a beam search algorithm tailored to quantum LDPC codes, which explores multiple decoding paths in parallel to find the most likely error pattern.
result: The beam search decoder achieves high decoding accuracy while meeting latency requirements for real-time operation, avoiding the need for massive classical computation resources.
conclusion: The proposed decoder offers a practical solution for implementing quantum error correction in real-time systems, balancing accuracy and speed.

title: Planar Fault-Tolerant Circuits For Non-Clifford Gates On The 2d Color Code

A family of scalable circuits designed for universal quantum computing on planar chips with nearest-neighbor couplings called twisted color circuits is introduced and can achieve fault tolerance with a “just-in-time” decoder.

method: Proposes a family of scalable circuits called twisted color circuits that achieve fault tolerance with a just-in-time decoder.
result: Demonstrates a scalable approach to fault-tolerant non-Clifford gates on the 2D color code.
conclusion: The twisted color circuits provide a practical path toward universal fault-tolerant quantum computing on planar architectures.

title: Quantifying Robustness And Locality Of Majorana Bound States In Interacting Systems
authors: William Samuelson, Juan Daniel Torres Luna, Sebastian Miles, A. Mert Bozkurt, Martin Leijnse, Michael Wimmer, And Viktor Svensson
abstract:

tldr: This paper rigorously defines Majorana bound states in interacting quantum-dot systems and quantifies their robustness and locality for non-Abelian braiding.
motivation: Recent quantum-dot experiments suggest Majorana bound states may exist, but their protection and feasibility for topological quantum computing in interacting systems need rigorous quantification.
method: The authors develop theoretical criteria and numerical methods to quantify the robustness and locality of Majorana bound states in interacting nanowire systems, using tools from many-body physics and topological invariants.
result: They provide a framework to assess how interactions affect the Majorana bound states' protection and demonstrate that certain regimes still support robust non-Abelian anyons.
conclusion: The work clarifies conditions under which Majorana bound states remain viable for braiding in realistic interacting systems, guiding future experiments.

title: Efficient Simulation Of Logical Magic State Preparation Protocols
authors: Samyak Surti, Lucas Daguerre, And Isaac H. Kim
abstract:
Author(s): Samyak Surti, Lucas Daguerre, and Isaac H. Kim

Classical simulation of a large class of logical magic state preparation protocols is made scalable and efficient via propagating errors to the end of the circuit.

motivation: Magic state preparation is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computing, but simulating these protocols is computationally expensive; the authors aim to make such simulations scalable.
method: The authors develop a technique to propagate errors through the circuit to the end, reducing the complexity of simulating logical magic state preparation.
result: The method enables efficient classical simulation of a large class of logical magic state preparation protocols.
conclusion: This work provides a practical tool for analyzing magic state preparation, which is important for fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Abelian Multi-Cycle Codes For Single-Shot Error Correction
authors: Hsiang-Ku Lin, Pak Kau Lim, Alexey A. Kovalev, And Leonid P. Pryadko

tldr: This paper introduces a new family of quantum LDPC codes achieving single-shot error correction with improved pseudothreshold and shorter block lengths.
motivation: Quantum error correction is essential for fault-tolerant quantum computing, but existing codes often require many rounds of syndrome measurement. Single-shot error correction reduces this overhead.
method: The authors construct Abelian multi-cycle codes, which are locally equivalent to higher-dimensional hypergraph-product codes, and analyze their single-shot error correction properties using belief propagation and ordered statistics decoding.
result: The codes achieve a pseudothreshold of approximately 1.1% with significantly shorter block lengths compared to previous single-shot codes.
conclusion: These codes offer a practical advantage for fault-tolerant quantum computing by enabling efficient single-shot error correction with moderate resource overhead.

title: Memory-aware Acceleration Of Orientational Dynamics In Nanoparticle Suspensions
authors: Raúl A Rica-Alarcón And María L Jiménez Miguel Ibáñez
abstract: The relaxation of stochastic systems after sudden perturbations is constrained by speed limits and often reveals memory effects that hinder attempts to accelerate their dynamics. Here we demonstrate Kovacs-type nonmonotonic relaxation in the electro-orientation of non-spherical nanoparticles and show how this memory effect limits simple acceleration protocols. Experimentally, the orientational dynamics is monitored optically through field-induced birefringence, which is proportional to the nematic order parameter. When an AC electric field is first set to an extreme value until the birefringence reaches its target and is then switched to the target field (matched two-step protocol), the relaxation exhibits a characteristic Kovacs shoulder. We interpret this behavior within a theoretical framework based on the Smoluchowski equation for the orientational probability density. In the high-frequency AC regime, orientational relaxation is governed by induced dipoles, and the observed memory effect originates from polydispersity, which generates a spectrum of rotational diffusion coefficients and hence multiscale relaxation. Building on this insight, we design protocols that mitigate the detrimental effect of memory by sequentially suppressing the slowest active relaxation mode. Experiments on nanoparticle suspensions with different properties confirm these mechanisms, and we demonstrate substantial reductions in relaxation time compared with single quenches and matched two-step protocols with NaMt suspensions. More broadly, these results illustrate how memory effects emerge when many degrees of freedom are steered with a single control parameter and provide an experimentally accessible strategy for controlling multiscale stochastic dynamics.
tldr: This paper demonstrates Kovacs-type nonmonotonic relaxation in nanoparticle suspensions and designs protocols to accelerate relaxation by mitigating memory effects.
motivation: Understanding and accelerating relaxation in stochastic systems is important for controlling multiscale dynamics, but memory effects often hinder simple acceleration protocols.
method: The authors use optical birefringence to monitor orientational dynamics of nanoparticles under AC electric fields, interpret results via Smoluchowski equation, and design multi-step protocols that sequentially suppress slow relaxation modes.
result: They observe Kovacs shoulders in two-step protocols and achieve substantial reductions in relaxation time using memory-aware protocols compared to standard quenches.
conclusion: Memory effects in polydisperse suspensions can be exploited to accelerate relaxation, providing a strategy for controlling multiscale stochastic dynamics.

title: Quantum Image Encodings For Noisy Intermediate-scale Quantum Devices: A Comprehensive Performance And Noise-resilience Analysis
authors: Emmanuel Martínez-Guerrero, Guo-Hua Sun, And Shi-Hai Dong
abstract:
Author(s): Emmanuel Martínez-Guerrero, Guo-Hua Sun, and Shi-Hai Dong

Quantum image processing relies on the efficient encoding of classical image data into quantum states, yet the practical performance of existing encoding schemes on noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) hardware remains insufficiently understood. Most prior studies have emphasized asymptotic resou…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062456] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper benchmarks quantum image encoding schemes on NISQ devices, focusing on noise resilience and resource efficiency.
motivation: Quantum image processing requires efficient encoding of classical images into quantum states, but the practical performance of existing encodings on noisy hardware is not well understood.
method: The authors compare several encoding schemes (e.g., FRQI, NEQR, QPIE) by simulating them under realistic noise models and evaluating metrics like fidelity and circuit depth.
result: They find that simpler encodings like QPIE are more noise-resilient, while more complex encodings suffer from higher error rates on NISQ devices.
conclusion: The study provides practical guidance for choosing quantum image encodings for near-term quantum computers, but the contribution is incremental and applied.

title: Phase-space Open-system Dynamics Of Second-order Nonlinear Interactions With Pulsed Quantum Light
authors: Emanuel Hubenschmid And Victor Rueskov Christiansen
abstract:
Author(s): Emanuel Hubenschmid and Victor Rueskov Christiansen

The theoretical description of broadband, multimode quantum pulses undergoing a second-order [MATH]-nonlinear interaction can be quite intricate due to the large dimensionality of the underlying phase space. However, in many cases only a few broadband (temporal) modes are relevant before and af…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063734] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a phase-space method to simulate open-system dynamics of broadband quantum pulses undergoing second-order nonlinear interactions.
motivation: Theoretical description of broadband multimode quantum pulses in nonlinear media is complex due to large phase-space dimensionality; a tractable method is needed.
method: The authors derive a phase-space representation using the positive-P distribution and model the open-system dynamics via a master equation including loss and dephasing.
result: They demonstrate that the method can efficiently simulate the evolution of quantum states in second-order nonlinear processes, capturing multimode effects and decoherence.
conclusion: The phase-space approach provides a practical tool for analyzing quantum optical systems with many modes, but the work is primarily a computational technique without direct information-theoretic or thermodynamic implications.

title: Accelerated Spin-adapted Ground-state Preparation With Nonvariational Quantum Algorithms
authors: Takumi Kobori, Taichi Kosugi, Hirofumi Nishi, Synge Todo, And Yu-Ichiro Matsushita
abstract:

Various methods have been explored to prepare the spin-adapted ground state—the lowest energy state within the Hilbert space constrained by externally specified values of the total spin magnitude and the spin-[MATH] component. In such problem settings, nonvariational methods incorporate penalty terms i…

tldr: This paper proposes a nonvariational quantum algorithm for preparing spin-adapted ground states using penalty terms and accelerated by a quantum imaginary time evolution-like method.
motivation: Preparing the ground state with a specific total spin is important for quantum chemistry and condensed matter physics, but existing variational methods may suffer from barren plateaus and optimization difficulties.
method: The authors introduce a nonvariational approach that combines a penalty term for spin constraints with a quantum imaginary time evolution (QITE) inspired algorithm to accelerate convergence.
result: Numerical simulations on small molecules show that the method can prepare spin-adapted ground states with high fidelity and faster convergence compared to standard variational approaches.
conclusion: The proposed algorithm offers an efficient alternative for spin-constrained ground-state preparation, though its scalability and noise resilience remain to be tested on larger systems.

authors: Yabo Li And Aditi Mitra

tldr: This paper studies non-invertible symmetries in out-of-equilibrium quantum systems, focusing on eigenstate order and Floquet physics.
motivation: Understanding how non-invertible symmetries manifest in dynamics is a fundamental question in many-body physics, with potential implications for quantum phases and thermalization.
method: The authors analyze a model with Rep(Q8) non-invertible symmetry, studying both Hamiltonian and Floquet dynamics, and compute spectral properties and correlation functions.
result: They find that non-invertible symmetries lead to characteristic signatures in eigenstate order and Floquet heating, including constraints on the spectrum and dynamics.
conclusion: Non-invertible symmetries provide a new organizing principle for out-of-equilibrium quantum matter, but the results are primarily of theoretical interest within condensed matter physics.

method: The authors introduce a family of classical stochastic processes with diffusive particles, branching, and power-law annihilation, and analyze them via field theory and numerical simulations.
result: The model shows a continuous phase transition with exponents that depend on the annihilation range, differing from short-range universality classes.
conclusion: Long-range annihilation leads to new universality classes for absorbing state transitions, but the work is purely classical and does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

tldr: This paper studies magnetoelastic signatures of thermal and quantum phase transitions in a deformable Ising chain under magnetic fields.

result: They identify magnetoelastic signatures that accompany thermal and quantum phase transitions.

method: Monte Carlo simulations of the Ashkin-Teller model with Kawasaki dynamics, coupling the system to two heat baths at different temperatures for horizontal and vertical exchanges.
result: The phase diagram exhibits features such as reentrant phases and modulated structures depending on the temperature difference.
conclusion: The two-temperature Ashkin-Teller model shows rich non-equilibrium behavior, but the work is primarily a classical statistical mechanics study without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics of information processing.

title: Stable Infinite-temperature Eigenstates In SU(2)-symmetric Nonintegrable Models
authors: Christopher J. Turner, Marcin Szyniszewski, Bhaskar Mukherjee, Ronald Melendrez, Hitesh J. Changlani, And Arijeet Pal
abstract:

Spectral properties and zero-energy degeneracy provide a way to characterize thermalization in nonintegrable quantum many-body systems. This work studies a bond-staggered Heisenberg chain with spectral reflection symmetry and continuous non-Abelian SU(2) symmetry, using character theory to count exponentially many zero-energy states and constructing exact low-entangled few-magnon eigenstates that are stable under many perturbations.

tldr: This paper studies stable infinite-temperature eigenstates in a SU(2)-symmetric nonintegrable Heisenberg chain, focusing on spectral properties and zero-energy degeneracy.
motivation: Understanding thermalization in nonintegrable quantum many-body systems is a fundamental question; the existence of stable eigenstates at infinite temperature challenges the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis.
method: The authors use character theory to count exponentially many zero-energy states and construct exact low-entangled few-magnon eigenstates in a bond-staggered Heisenberg chain with spectral reflection symmetry and SU(2) symmetry.
result: They find exponentially many zero-energy states that are stable under many perturbations, indicating a violation of thermalization in a nonintegrable model.
conclusion: The work reveals a mechanism for stable infinite-temperature eigenstates, which has implications for quantum thermalization and many-body localization.

title: Nontrivial Multiproduct Commutation Relation Toward Reducing $T$-Count In Sequential Pauli-Based Computation
authors: Yusei Mori, Hideaki Hakoshima, And Keisuke Fujii
abstract:

motivation: Reducing T-count is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computation, as T gates are costly. The authors aim to leverage commuting structures to achieve this reduction.
method: They derive a nontrivial multiproduct commutation relation that allows simultaneous execution of commuting Pauli rotations, thereby reducing the number of T gates needed.
result: The proposed method significantly reduces T-count in sequential Pauli-based computation, as demonstrated theoretically.
conclusion: The work provides a new technique for T-count reduction, which is important for practical quantum computing but is not directly aligned with the user's core interests in quantum information theory.

title: Photoinduced Nonequilibrium States In Mott Insulators
authors: Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, And Philipp Werner
abstract:
Author(s): Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, and Philipp Werner

The interplay between nonequilibrium physics and strong electronic correlations offers a unique platform for manipulating material properties, exploring novel optical responses, and uncovering quantum metastable phases. This review provides a comprehensive overview of recent advances in understanding the nonequilibrium dynamics of photoexcited Mott insulators—systems where strong interactions and a robust energy gap can give rise to rich and controllable phenomena. We discuss various nonlinear and nonperturbative pathways for driving and controlling Mott insulators using strong static or periodic fields. Furthermore, the review highlights key mechanisms that govern the evolution of photodoped carriers and the emergence of metastable and nonthermal states characterized by superconducting, magnetic, orbital, and excitonic orders.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035001] Published Thu Jul 31, 2025.
tldr: A comprehensive review of photoinduced nonequilibrium states in Mott insulators, focusing on strong correlations and optical control.
motivation: To understand and control nonequilibrium dynamics in strongly correlated materials, which can lead to novel phases and functionalities.
method: Review of theoretical and experimental advances, including dynamical mean-field theory and time-resolved spectroscopy.
result: Identifies key mechanisms for photodoping, metastable phases, and nonthermal orders such as superconductivity and magnetism.
conclusion: Photoexcitation provides a powerful tool to manipulate Mott insulators, but the field is still developing with many open questions.

motivation: Excess quasiparticles in superconducting circuits cause dissipation and degrade device performance, motivating a deeper understanding of their dynamics.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a local gap variation in a superconductor and compute bound state energies and wavefunctions.
result: They find multiple quasiparticle bound states with energies within the gap, depending on the strength and shape of the gap variation.
conclusion: These bound states can trap quasiparticles, potentially explaining the observed excess quasiparticle density in superconducting devices.

method: The authors measure the transmission parameter of niobium quarter-wave resonators as a function of magnetic field and analyze the resonance frequency shifts caused by individual vortex jumps.
result: They observe equidistant resonance jumps corresponding to single vortex entry and exit, and model the effect using a simple geometric picture.
conclusion: The work provides insight into vortex behavior in superconducting resonators, which may help in designing more robust quantum devices, but it is primarily a materials/device physics study without direct quantum information or thermodynamics focus.

authors: Yuhao Wang, Lining Yang, Wenyu Song, Li Chen, Zehao Yu, Xinchen He, Zeyu Yan, Jiaye Xu, Ruidong Li, Weizhao Wang, Zonglin Li, Shuai Yang, Shan Zhang, Xiao Feng, Tiantian Wang, Yunyi Zang, Lin Li, Runan Shang, Qi-Kun Xue, Ke He, And Hao Zhang

motivation: Previous studies on PbTe quantum dots reported conflicting observations of charging energy; this work aims to clarify the conditions under which charging energy appears.
method: The authors fabricate PbTe nanowires with different cross-sectional areas to vary quantum dot size and measure the charging energy evolution using transport spectroscopy.
result: They find that charging energy is present for small dots but absent for large dots, with a crossover at a specific size threshold.
conclusion: The presence of charging energy in PbTe quantum dots depends on dot size, explaining previous contradictory reports and guiding future device design.

method: The authors propose a planar measurement scheme using lattice surgery and flag qubits to detect and correct errors with fewer ancilla qubits.
result: The scheme achieves fault-tolerant logical measurements with lower qubit overhead compared to standard approaches, while maintaining high error thresholds.
conclusion: This work advances practical quantum error correction by reducing resource requirements for logical operations, bringing fault-tolerant quantum computing closer to realization.

title: Rigorous No-go Theorems For Heralded Linear-optical State Generation Tasks
authors: Deepesh Singh, Ryan J. Marshman, Luis Villegas-Aguilar, Jens Eisert, And Nora Tischler

motivation: Photonic quantum technologies require reliable state preparation, but linear optics with heralding has fundamental limitations that need to be understood.
method: The authors use rigorous mathematical proofs based on linear-optical transformations and postselection to derive constraints on achievable states.
result: They establish strict no-go results for several classes of states, including certain entangled and non-Gaussian states, under linear-optical operations and heralding.
conclusion: These no-go theorems provide fundamental bounds on what can be achieved with linear optics, guiding future experimental and theoretical work in photonic quantum information.

authors: Apurav Tehri And Jaskaran Singh

motivation: Linear optical quantum computation suffers from probabilistic nonlocal gates, limiting scalability. Qudit encoding can reduce the number of required operations.
method: The authors design multiqudit entangling gates that encode multiple qubits onto qudits, compressing the circuit depth and gate count.
result: The scheme demonstrates reduced resource requirements for specific quantum circuits, though probabilistic gate success remains a challenge.
conclusion: The approach offers a potential path to more efficient LOQC, but practical implementation and fault tolerance are not addressed.

title: Ferroelectricity In A Magnon Bose-Einstein Condensate: Nonreciprocal Superfluidity, Exceptional Points, And Majorana Bosons

method: They develop a theoretical model incorporating the AC phase and analyze the resulting magnon dynamics, including the emergence of nonreciprocal transport and exceptional points.
result: The system exhibits a positive feedback loop between electric field and magnon orbital motion, leading to ferroelectric order and topological features like exceptional points and Majorana bosons.
conclusion: The work reveals a new mechanism for ferroelectricity in quantum condensates and highlights connections to non-Hermitian physics and topological excitations.

title: Exactly Solvable Quantum Many-body Dynamics From Space-time Duality
authors: Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, And Tomaž Prosen
abstract:
Author(s): Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, and Tomaž Prosen

Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult. In the past decade, there has been a fundamental advance based on discretizing the time evolution of lattice systems, by analogy with digital computation. Since space is already discrete on a lattice, treating space and time on the same footing avoids the mathematical complications of continuous space-time quantum field theories. This review focuses on how this space-time duality plays out in the dynamics of interacting many-body systems and the intrinsic relationship with special kinds of lattices termed brickwork quantum circuits. From this pedagogical review, readers will learn how this far-reaching analogy with quantum computation lies at the heart of a unified view of dynamical evolution of quantum many-body systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025001] Published Wed Apr 15, 2026.
tldr: A review of exactly solvable quantum many-body dynamics using space-time duality and brickwork quantum circuits.
motivation: Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult; space-time duality offers a unified approach.
method: The review explains how discretizing time evolution on a lattice and treating space and time symmetrically leads to solvable models via brickwork quantum circuits.
result: The paper provides a pedagogical overview of the relationship between space-time duality and integrable quantum circuits.
conclusion: Space-time duality provides a powerful framework for understanding and solving quantum many-body dynamics, with connections to quantum computation.
