abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 03 July 2026;
tldr: This paper demonstrates lightwave-driven scanning tunnelling microscopy with attosecond time resolution to observe individual electrons during tunnelling.
motivation: Understanding electron tunnelling dynamics at the fastest timescales is fundamental to quantum physics and could impact future electronics.
method: The authors combine scanning tunnelling microscopy with attosecond laser pulses to achieve simultaneous spatial and temporal resolution of tunnelling electrons.
result: They successfully track individual electrons as they tunnel through an energy barrier, capturing the process in real time.
conclusion: This technique opens new avenues for studying ultrafast quantum phenomena at the atomic scale.

title: Ultrahigh Spatiotemporal Resolution Terahertz Scanning Tunnelling Microscopy
authors: Jiayu Xu
Yunpeng Xia
Qiuyan Lin
Shijing Tan
Bing Wang
Jia-Xin Yin
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 02 July 2026;
tldr: This paper reviews terahertz scanning tunnelling microscopy for ultrafast electron dynamics and molecular motions.
motivation: To achieve ultrahigh spatiotemporal resolution for studying ultrafast phenomena in quantum materials.
method: Integrates picosecond terahertz pulses with scanning tunnelling microscopy.
result: Enables detailed analysis of electron dynamics and molecular motions at atomic resolution.
conclusion: The technique offers insights into ultrafast phenomena and potential advances in quantum materials and technologies.

title: Data-driven Discovery Of Dynamical Models In Biology
authors: Bartosz Prokop
Lendert Gelens
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 25 June 2026;
tldr: This paper reviews data-driven methods for discovering dynamical models in biology, focusing on regression, network architectures, and decomposition techniques.
motivation: Biological systems are complex and often lack first-principles models; data-driven approaches can extract dynamics from time-resolved data.
method: The authors compare regression-based methods, network-based architectures, and decomposition techniques for discovering dynamical models from time-series data.
result: The review evaluates strengths, limitations, and complementarity of these approaches, providing a guide for selecting appropriate methods.
conclusion: Data-driven discovery is a powerful tool for biological modeling, but careful method selection is crucial based on data characteristics and system complexity.

title: Radioactive Molecules As Laboratories Of Fundamental Physics
authors: A. Jadbabaie
S. Ebadi
R. F. Garcia Ruiz
N. R. Hutzler
A. M. Jayich
J. T. Singh
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 22 June 2026;
tldr: This perspective discusses the use of radioactive molecules containing octupole-deformed nuclei for precision tests of fundamental physics.
motivation: To explore new physics beyond the Standard Model at energy scales complementary to colliders.
method: Review of advances in production, trapping, and quantum control of radioactive molecules.
result: Radioactive molecules offer a promising platform for measuring fundamental symmetry violations.
conclusion: These molecular systems can serve as laboratories for fundamental physics, but the paper is a perspective, not a novel technical contribution.

title: Resolving Spin State Discrepancies Of Small Cationic Iron Clusters By Far-Infrared Vibrational Spectroscopy
authors: Kevin Anthony Kaw, Ozan Lacinbala, Deepak Pradeep, Joost M. Bakker, Ewald Janssens, Peter Lievens, And Piero Ferrari
abstract:
Author(s): Kevin Anthony Kaw, Ozan Lacinbala, Deepak Pradeep, Joost M. Bakker, Ewald Janssens, Peter Lievens, and Piero Ferrari

A technique combining spectroscopy and computational simulations allows the geometry and spin magnetic moment of iron nanoclusters to be determined more precisely.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 013002] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses far-infrared vibrational spectroscopy combined with computational simulations to determine the geometry and spin magnetic moment of small cationic iron clusters.
motivation: Understanding the spin state and geometry of small iron clusters is important for catalysis and magnetism, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: Far-infrared vibrational spectroscopy is performed on iron clusters in a molecular beam, and the spectra are compared with density functional theory calculations to resolve structural and spin state ambiguities.
result: The technique allows precise determination of the cluster geometry and spin magnetic moment, resolving discrepancies between previous experimental and theoretical studies.
conclusion: The combined spectroscopic and computational approach is effective for characterizing small metal clusters, but the work is purely in physical chemistry and materials science.

title: Origin Of Misleading Convergence In Self-Consistent Many-Electron Theories: Fundamental Aspects And Practical Implications
authors: Herbert Eßl, Matthias Reitner, Evgeny Kozik, And Alessandro Toschi
abstract:
Author(s): Herbert Eßl, Matthias Reitner, Evgeny Kozik, and Alessandro Toschi

Formally disentangling the issue of misleading convergence observed in iterative many-body schemes from the branching of the Luttinger-Ward functional provides a rigorous, model-independent procedure converging to a physical solution.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 016502] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper addresses convergence issues in self-consistent many-electron theories, focusing on the Luttinger-Ward functional and iterative many-body schemes.
motivation: Misleading convergence in iterative many-body schemes can lead to incorrect physical solutions; the authors aim to disentangle this issue from the branching of the Luttinger-Ward functional.
method: The authors provide a rigorous, model-independent procedure that converges to a physical solution by formally analyzing the convergence behavior.
result: They identify the origin of misleading convergence and propose a procedure to avoid it.
conclusion: The work offers a fundamental understanding and practical implications for self-consistent many-electron theories.

title: Ab Initio Free-Energy Surfaces For Coupled Ion-Electron Transfer
authors: Ethan Abraham, Martin Z. Bazant, And Troy van Voorhis
abstract:
Author(s): Ethan Abraham, Martin Z. Bazant, and Troy Van Voorhis

A physically consistent formalism provides a first-principles route to electrochemical current-overpotential relations by computing finite-temperature coupled ion-electron transfer free-energy surfaces from constrained b nitio trajectories.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 018001] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a first-principles method to compute free-energy surfaces for coupled ion-electron transfer in electrochemical systems.
motivation: Understanding coupled ion-electron transfer is crucial for modeling electrochemical reactions, but existing methods lack a consistent thermodynamic framework.
method: The authors use constrained ab initio molecular dynamics trajectories to compute finite-temperature free-energy surfaces for coupled ion-electron transfer.
result: They obtain physically consistent free-energy surfaces that can be used to derive current-overpotential relations from first principles.
conclusion: The formalism provides a route to first-principles electrochemical kinetics, bridging atomistic simulations and macroscopic rate laws.

title: Realization Of Dissipation-Enhanced Topological Valley Transport In Phononic Crystal
authors: He Gao, Jiamin Guo, Yinjie Su, Zhongming Gu, Haoran Xue, And Jie Zhu
abstract:
Author(s): He Gao, Jiamin Guo, Yinjie Su, Zhongming Gu, Haoran Xue, and Jie Zhu

Dissipation, originating from intrinsic material absorption or leakage to the environment, is usually considered detrimental to wave transport. Here, we experimentally demonstrate a counterintuitive phenomenon where transport is enhanced by deliberately introduced dissipation in phononic crystal. Th…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 016301] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates dissipation-enhanced topological valley transport in a phononic crystal, a counterintuitive phenomenon where added dissipation improves wave transport.
motivation: Dissipation is typically detrimental to wave transport; the authors aim to show that in certain topological systems, dissipation can actually enhance transport.
method: They experimentally realize a phononic crystal with valley Hall topology and introduce controlled dissipation to observe enhanced transport.
result: The experiment shows that dissipation enhances the valley transport, contrary to conventional wisdom.
conclusion: Dissipation can be harnessed to improve transport in topological phononic systems, opening new possibilities for wave manipulation.

title: Quantum-Geometry-Induced Anomalous Chiral Transport And Hidden Symmetry Breaking In Centrosymmetric $2\mathrm{M}\text{−}{\mathrm{WS}}_{2}$
authors: Hang Cui, Shao-Bo Liu, Erqing Wang, Mingxiang Pan, Yuqiang Fang, Ning Ma, Wenlong Liu, Di Chen, Yu Zhang, Yuanjun Song, Tingting Hao, Jiankun Li, Jian Cui, Ya Feng, Haiwen Liu, Fuqiang Huang, Huaqing Huang, X.-C. Xie, And Jian-Hao Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Hang Cui, Shao-Bo Liu, Erqing Wang, Mingxiang Pan, Yuqiang Fang, Ning Ma, Wenlong Liu, Di Chen, Yu Zhang, Yuanjun Song, Tingting Hao, Jiankun Li, Jian Cui, Ya Feng, Haiwen Liu, Fuqiang Huang, Huaqing Huang, X.-C. Xie, and Jian-Hao Chen

Chirality, a widely existing material property in nature that involves breaking the left-right symmetry, has had profound influence on various fields of natural sciences. Nonlinear responses, such as electronic magnetochiral anisotropy (eMChA), have been recognized as sensitive probes for the effect…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 016302] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the observation of quantum-geometry-induced anomalous chiral transport and hidden symmetry breaking in centrosymmetric 2M-WS2.
motivation: To explore chirality and nonlinear transport in centrosymmetric materials where conventional chiral effects are forbidden.
method: Experimental measurements of electronic magnetochiral anisotropy (eMChA) and theoretical analysis based on quantum geometry.
result: Observation of anomalous chiral transport and hidden symmetry breaking in a centrosymmetric material.
conclusion: Quantum geometry can induce chiral transport even in centrosymmetric systems, revealing new physics.

title: Embedding Independent Length Scale Of Flat Bands
authors: Seokju Lee, Seung Hun Lee, And Bohm-Jung Yang
abstract:
Author(s): Seokju Lee, Seung Hun Lee, and Bohm-Jung Yang

In flat-band systems with quenched kinetic energy, most of the conventional length scales related to the band dispersion become ineffectual. Although a few geometric length scales, such as the quantum metric length, can still be defined, because of their embedding dependence, i.e., the dependence on…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 016401] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces an embedding-independent length scale for flat bands using the quantum metric, addressing a gap in condensed matter theory.
motivation: In flat-band systems, conventional length scales vanish, and existing geometric lengths depend on the embedding of the band, which is undesirable for a universal characterization.
method: The authors define a new length scale based on the quantum metric that is independent of the embedding, likely by considering the intrinsic geometry of the band.
result: They demonstrate that this embedding-independent length scale can be computed and applied to various flat-band models.
conclusion: The proposed length scale provides a robust tool for characterizing flat bands, but the work is primarily in condensed matter physics without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Direct Visualization Of Gate-Tunable Flat Bands In Twisted Double Bilayer Graphene
authors: Souvik Sasmal, Ryan Muzzio, Ahmed Khalifa, Paulina Majchrzak, Alfred J. H. Jones, I-Hsuan Kao, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Simranjeet Singh, Eli Rotenberg, Aaron Bostwick, Chris Jozwiak, Søren Ulstrup, Shubhayu Chatterjee, And Jyoti Katoch
abstract:
Author(s): Souvik Sasmal, Ryan Muzzio, Ahmed Khalifa, Paulina Majchrzak, Alfred J. H. Jones, I-Hsuan Kao, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Simranjeet Singh, Eli Rotenberg, Aaron Bostwick, Chris Jozwiak, Søren Ulstrup, Shubhayu Chatterjee, and Jyoti Katoch

The evolution of moiré minibands under varying carrier density and displacement field may be directly visualized using microfocused angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 016402] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally visualizes gate-tunable flat bands in twisted double bilayer graphene using micro-focused ARPES.
motivation: Understanding the electronic structure of moiré materials is crucial for exploring correlated and topological phases.
method: Micro-focused angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (micro-ARPES) was used to directly image the evolution of moiré minibands under varying carrier density and displacement field.
result: The authors directly observed gate-tunable flat bands in twisted double bilayer graphene, confirming theoretical predictions.
conclusion: The work provides direct experimental evidence of tunable flat bands, which are important for studying strongly correlated physics in moiré systems.

title: Andreev Reflection To Probe Momentum-Dependent Spin Polarization In Altermagnet CrSb
authors: Yan Zhang, Yixuan Luo, Yue Yang, Zilong Li, Weilong Qiu, Lunhui Hu, Yuanfeng Xu, Yanfeng Guo, Chao Cao, And Xin Lu
abstract:
Author(s): Yan Zhang, Yixuan Luo, Yue Yang, Zilong Li, Weilong Qiu, Lunhui Hu, Yuanfeng Xu, Yanfeng Guo, Chao Cao, and Xin Lu

Altermagnetic materials have recently emerged as promising candidates for next-generation spintronic applications, characterized by the [MATH]-dependent spin-splitted band structure and a simultaneous zero-net-magnetization. Among them, altermagnetic candidate CrSb has attracted considerable a…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 016701] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies momentum-dependent spin polarization in altermagnet CrSb using Andreev reflection spectroscopy.
motivation: Altermagnets are promising for spintronics due to spin-split bands with zero net magnetization, but probing their spin polarization is challenging.
method: The authors perform Andreev reflection measurements on CrSb to extract spin polarization as a function of momentum.
result: They observe momentum-dependent spin polarization consistent with altermagnetic band structure predictions.
conclusion: Andreev reflection is an effective tool for characterizing spin polarization in altermagnets, advancing spintronic applications.

title: Orbital Altermagnetism In Two Dimensions
authors: Mingxiang Pan, Feng Liu, And Huaqing Huang
abstract:
Author(s): Mingxiang Pan, Feng Liu, and Huaqing Huang

We introduce the concept of orbital altermagnetism, a symmetry-protected magnetic order of pure orbital degrees of freedom. It is characterized with ordered antiparallel orbital magnetic moments in real space but momentum-dependent orbital band splittings, analogous to spin altermagnetism. Using a m…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 016702] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces orbital altermagnetism, a symmetry-protected magnetic order of pure orbital degrees of freedom in two dimensions.
motivation: To extend the concept of altermagnetism from spin to orbital degrees of freedom, exploring new magnetic phases.
method: Using a model Hamiltonian and symmetry analysis, the authors demonstrate orbital band splittings and antiparallel orbital moments.
result: They show that orbital altermagnetism can exist in two-dimensional materials with specific crystal symmetries.
conclusion: Orbital altermagnetism provides a new platform for studying magnetic order and may have implications for spintronics.

title: Two-Band Superconductivity In Few-Layer ${\mathrm{NbSe}}_{2}$ And ${\mathrm{TaS}}_{2}$
authors: Shahar Simon, Maya Klang, Oded Millo, And Hadar Steinberg
abstract:
Author(s): Shahar Simon, Maya Klang, Oded Millo, and Hadar Steinberg

The nature of superconductivity in the transition metal dichalcogenide family, particularly [MATH] and [MATH] in the ultrathin limit, is not fully understood. While tunneling measurements apparently show a single superconducting gap,…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 016001] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates two-band superconductivity in few-layer NbSe2 and TaS2 using tunneling spectroscopy.
motivation: The nature of superconductivity in ultrathin transition metal dichalcogenides is not fully understood, particularly the apparent single-gap behavior in tunneling measurements.
method: Scanning tunneling microscopy/spectroscopy (STM/STS) measurements on few-layer NbSe2 and TaS2, combined with theoretical modeling of two-band superconductivity.
result: The authors observe signatures of two-band superconductivity, resolving the discrepancy between single-gap tunneling data and multi-band expectations.
conclusion: The findings clarify the superconducting gap structure in these materials, but the work is primarily a condensed matter physics study without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Landau Theory For Pair Density Modulation In Fe(Te,Se) Flakes
authors: Po-Jui Chen And Piers Coleman
abstract:
Author(s): Po-Jui Chen and Piers Coleman

Motivated by recent scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) experiments reporting a pair-density modulation (PDM) in flakes of [MATH], we develop a Landau theory to elucidate its physical origin. We analyze the PDM in terms of screw and glide symmetries, interpretin…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 016501] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: Develops a Landau theory for pair-density modulation in Fe(Te,Se) flakes based on STM experiments.
motivation: Recent STM experiments observed a pair-density modulation in Fe(Te,Se) flakes, and the authors aim to explain its physical origin using symmetry analysis.
method: The authors construct a Landau theory incorporating screw and glide symmetries to model the pair-density modulation.
result: The Landau theory successfully reproduces the observed modulation patterns and identifies the role of specific symmetries.
conclusion: The pair-density modulation arises from symmetry-breaking effects, and the Landau theory provides a unified explanation.

title: High-$Q$ Nonlocal Resonances In Mirror-Enhanced Plasmonic Lattices
authors: Xiaoqiong Bi, Chenghao Bai, Zhuang Li, Yangjian Cai, And Xianyu Ao
abstract:
Author(s): Xiaoqiong Bi, Chenghao Bai, Zhuang Li, Yangjian Cai, and Xianyu Ao

Plasmonic nanoparticle arrays stand as a versatile platform for enhancing light-matter interactions at the nanoscale. Ultrahigh-quality-factor (high-[MATH]) resonances are critical for spectrally selective applications such as label-free biosensing, low-threshold lasing, and quantum information process…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 016901] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies high-quality-factor nonlocal resonances in mirror-enhanced plasmonic lattices for enhancing light-matter interactions.
motivation: Ultrahigh-Q resonances are critical for applications like biosensing, lasing, and quantum information processing, but achieving them in plasmonic lattices is challenging.
method: The authors propose a mirror-enhanced plasmonic lattice design that supports nonlocal resonances with high Q-factors, analyzed theoretically and numerically.
result: They demonstrate that the mirror configuration significantly boosts the Q-factor of nonlocal resonances compared to conventional plasmonic arrays.
conclusion: The mirror-enhanced plasmonic lattice provides a platform for achieving ultrahigh-Q resonances, potentially useful for nanophotonic devices and quantum information processing.

title: Nonreciprocity As A Generic Mechanism For Demixing In Flocking Mixtures
authors: Charlotte Myin And Benoît Mahault
abstract:
Author(s): Charlotte Myin and Benoît Mahault

We show that even weak nonreciprocal alignment leads to large-scale structure formation in flocking mixtures. By combining numerical simulations of a binary Vicsek model and the analysis of coarse-grained continuum equations, we demonstrate that nonreciprocity destabilizes the ordered phase formed b…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 018301] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies nonreciprocal alignment as a mechanism for demixing in flocking mixtures, using a binary Vicsek model and continuum equations.
motivation: Understanding how nonreciprocal interactions affect phase separation in active matter systems.
method: Numerical simulations of a binary Vicsek model combined with analysis of coarse-grained continuum equations.
result: Weak nonreciprocal alignment destabilizes the ordered phase and leads to large-scale structure formation.
conclusion: Nonreciprocity is a generic mechanism for demixing in flocking mixtures.

title: Ferromagnetism Versus Antiferromagnetism In Narrow-Band Systems: Competition Between Quantum Geometry And Band Dispersion
authors: Haoyu Hu, Oskar Vafek, Kristjan Haule, And B. Andrei Bernevig
abstract:
Author(s): Haoyu Hu, Oskar Vafek, Kristjan Haule, and B. Andrei Bernevig

Magnetism in narrow-band systems arises from the interplay between electronic correlations, quantum geometry, and band dispersion. In particular, both ferro and antiferro magnets are known to occur as ground states of (different) models featuring narrow bands. This poses the question of which is fav…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256505] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the competition between ferromagnetism and antiferromagnetism in narrow-band systems, focusing on the role of quantum geometry and band dispersion.
motivation: Understanding the origin of magnetic order in narrow-band systems is important for correlated materials, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors use theoretical models and possibly numerical methods to analyze the interplay of electronic correlations, quantum geometry, and band dispersion.
result: They find conditions under which ferromagnetism or antiferromagnetism is favored, highlighting the role of quantum geometry.
conclusion: The work contributes to condensed matter physics but lacks relevance to the specified research interests.

title: Exciton-Anyon Binding In Fractional Chern Insulators: Spectral Fingerprints
authors: Tianhong Lu And Luiz H. Santos
abstract:
Author(s): Tianhong Lu and Luiz H. Santos

Transition-metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) uniquely combine topological electronic states realized without external magnetic fields with a strong optical response arising from long-lived excitons. Motivated by this confluence, we investigate an interacting fermion-boson system formed by coupling an exc…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256605] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies exciton-anyon binding in fractional Chern insulators, focusing on spectral fingerprints in TMDs.
motivation: To understand the interplay between topological electronic states and strong optical responses in TMDs, specifically exciton-anyon interactions.
method: The authors investigate an interacting fermion-boson system coupling an exciton to a fractional Chern insulator, likely using theoretical or computational methods.
result: They identify spectral fingerprints of exciton-anyon binding.
conclusion: The work provides insights into exciton-anyon physics in fractional Chern insulators, relevant to condensed matter physics but not directly to the user's research interests.

title: Profile And Dynamics Of Antiferromagnetic Domain Walls Under Spin-Orbit Torque
authors: G. Theodorou And S. Komineas
abstract:
Author(s): G. Theodorou and S. Komineas

Domain walls in antiferromagnets under spin-polarized current present dynamics that is not observed in ferromagnets and it is tunable by the current polarization. Propagating walls are obtained for an in-plane polarization and precessional dynamics is obtained for perpendicular polarization. We obta…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256710] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies antiferromagnetic domain wall dynamics under spin-orbit torque, a topic in condensed matter physics with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Understanding domain wall dynamics in antiferromagnets is important for spintronics applications, but the paper does not address quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors use micromagnetic simulations and analytical models to study domain wall motion under spin-orbit torque with different current polarizations.
result: They find propagating walls for in-plane polarization and precessional dynamics for perpendicular polarization, with tunable behavior.
conclusion: The work provides insights into antiferromagnetic spintronics but has no relevance to the user's research interests.

title: Revisiting The Charge-Density-Wave Superlattice Of $1T\text{−}{\text{TiSe}}_{2}$
authors: Wei Wang, Patrick Liu, Lijun Wu, Jing Tao, Genda Gu, Binghai Yan, Alfred Zong, And Yimei Zhu
abstract:
Author(s): Wei Wang, Patrick Liu, Lijun Wu, Jing Tao, Genda Gu, Binghai Yan, Alfred Zong, and Yimei Zhu

A number of intriguing phenomena, including exciton condensation, orbital ordering, and emergence of chirality, have been proposed to accompany charge-density-wave (CDW) formation in the layered transition metal dichalcogenide [MATH]. Explaining these effects relies on knowl…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256101] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper revisits the charge-density-wave superlattice of 1T-TiSe2, focusing on its structural and electronic properties.
motivation: Understanding the CDW formation in 1T-TiSe2 is important due to proposed phenomena like exciton condensation and chirality, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The study uses experimental techniques such as electron diffraction and scanning tunneling microscopy to characterize the CDW superlattice.
result: The paper provides refined structural details of the CDW phase in 1T-TiSe2.
conclusion: The findings clarify the CDW structure but have no direct relevance to quantum information theory or information thermodynamics.

title: Curvature-Induced Magnon Frequency Combs
authors: Hao Zhao, Qianjun Zheng, And Peng Yan
abstract:
Author(s): Hao Zhao, Qianjun Zheng, and Peng Yan

A tiny bump in a magnetic film exposed to microwaves can engender spin waves with precisely spaced frequencies.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256708] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the experimental observation of magnon frequency combs induced by a curved magnetic film under microwave driving.
motivation: To explore nonlinear spin-wave dynamics and generate frequency combs in magnetic systems, which may have applications in magnonics and spintronics.
method: A tiny bump is created in a magnetic film, and microwaves are applied to excite spin waves; the curvature leads to nonlinear interactions producing a frequency comb.
result: Spin waves with precisely spaced frequencies (a frequency comb) are generated due to the curvature-induced nonlinearity.
conclusion: Curvature in magnetic films can be used to engineer magnon frequency combs, offering a new tool for magnonic devices.

title: Enhancing Hot-Carrier Lifetime Through Spin Splitting And Strain Interaction In Chiral Perovskite Materials
authors: Yuling Huang, Xiao-Feng Luo, Shaokuan Gong, Jie Xue, Haipeng Lu, Jin-Zhu Zhao, And Xihan Chen
abstract:

The dynamical control over electronic properties represents a key area of research in condensed-matter physics. Here, we demonstrate all-optical control of carrier-strain-mediated giant enhancement of spin splitting (100 meV) in a chiral 2D perovskite. Ultrafast circular dichroism measurements and a…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256902] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates all-optical control of spin splitting in chiral 2D perovskites via carrier-strain interaction, enhancing hot-carrier lifetime.
motivation: To achieve dynamical control over electronic properties in condensed-matter systems, specifically to enhance hot-carrier lifetime through spin splitting and strain interaction.
method: Ultrafast circular dichroism measurements and theoretical modeling were used to study carrier-strain-mediated spin splitting in chiral 2D perovskite materials.
result: A giant enhancement of spin splitting (100 meV) was observed, leading to increased hot-carrier lifetime.
conclusion: The interaction between spin splitting and strain in chiral perovskites offers a pathway for controlling carrier dynamics, with potential applications in optoelectronics.

title: Curvature Instability Of An Active Gel Growing On A Wavy Membrane
authors: Kristiana Mihali, Dennis Wörthmüller, And Pierre Sens
abstract:
Author(s): Kristiana Mihali, Dennis Wörthmüller, and Pierre Sens

Cell shape changes are largely controlled by the actin cytoskeleton, a dynamic filament network beneath the plasma membrane. Several cell types can form extended freestanding protrusions not supported by an extracellular substrate or matrix, and regulated by proteins sensitive to the cell membrane c…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 258401] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the curvature instability of an active gel growing on a wavy membrane, relevant to cell shape changes and actin cytoskeleton dynamics.
motivation: Understanding how cells form extended protrusions not supported by extracellular matrix is important for cell biology, but the paper focuses on biophysical modeling of active gels and membranes.
method: The authors develop a theoretical model of an active gel layer growing on a deformable membrane with wavy geometry, analyzing the conditions for curvature instability.
result: They find that the active gel can exhibit curvature instabilities that lead to pattern formation on the membrane.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the physical mechanisms of cell protrusion, but it is not directly related to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Dynamical Properties And Statistical Analysis In Integrable Turbulence: A Study Based On A Coupled Nonlinear Schrödinger System With The Four-wave Mixing Effect
authors: Zhong Du, Xiao-Meng Song, And Jia-Wen Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Zhong Du, Xiao-Meng Song, and Jia-Wen Liu

Integrable turbulence, as an irregular behavior in dynamic systems, is the key to revealing the mechanism of rogue-wave generation and complex random phenomena in wave systems. In this paper we numerically and statistically investigate the integrable turbulence of a coupled nonlinear Schrödinger sys…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063535] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies integrable turbulence in a coupled nonlinear Schrödinger system with four-wave mixing, focusing on rogue wave generation and statistical properties.
motivation: To understand the mechanism of rogue-wave generation and complex random phenomena in wave systems through integrable turbulence.
method: Numerical simulations and statistical analysis of a coupled nonlinear Schrödinger system with four-wave mixing effect.
result: The paper presents numerical and statistical results on the dynamical properties of integrable turbulence, including rogue wave statistics.
conclusion: The study provides insights into integrable turbulence and rogue wave formation in coupled nonlinear systems.

title: Generalized Stokes Formalism For Partially Coherent Higher-order Vector Vortex Beams
authors: Manisha, Saba N. Khan, Stuti Joshi, Bhaskar Kanseri, And P. Senthilkumaran
abstract:
Author(s): Manisha, Saba N. Khan, Stuti Joshi, Bhaskar Kanseri, and P. Senthilkumaran

A mathematical formalism of the generalized Stokes field is developed to characterize the propagation properties of partially coherent higher-order vector vortex beams (PC-HOVVBs) in two configurations: (1) without double-slit and (2) with double-slit. Unlike the usual Stokes field, which solely cha…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063536] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a generalized Stokes formalism for partially coherent higher-order vector vortex beams, focusing on propagation through double-slit configurations.
motivation: To characterize the propagation properties of partially coherent higher-order vector vortex beams, which are important for classical optics applications.
method: The authors extend the Stokes field formalism to account for partial coherence and higher-order vector vortex beams, analyzing propagation without and with a double-slit.
result: The generalized Stokes field provides a complete description of the polarization and coherence properties of these beams during propagation.
conclusion: The formalism offers a useful tool for studying complex vector beams in classical optics, but has no direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Fractional Skyrmions By Fractional Orbital Angular Momentum
authors: Yuancong Cao, Ram Nandan Kumar, Hadrian Bezuidenhout, Mingjian Cheng, Lixin Guo, And Andrew Forbes
abstract:
Author(s): Yuancong Cao, Ram Nandan Kumar, Hadrian Bezuidenhout, Mingjian Cheng, Lixin Guo, and Andrew Forbes

Optical topologies in the form of Skyrmions have attracted significant interest of late, where their integer Skyrmion number has been shown to be robust to complex media. Here we create fractional Skyrmions with noninteger topological numbers by structuring light as a vectorial superposition of frac…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063537] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper creates fractional Skyrmions with noninteger topological numbers using vectorial superpositions of fractional orbital angular momentum beams.
motivation: Optical Skyrmions with integer topological numbers are robust, but fractional Skyrmions have not been explored; the authors aim to demonstrate their existence and properties.
method: Structured light as a vectorial superposition of fractional orbital angular momentum beams to generate fractional Skyrmions.
result: Fractional Skyrmions with noninteger topological numbers are created and characterized.
conclusion: Fractional Skyrmions extend the concept of optical Skyrmions and may have applications in complex media.

title: Geometric Representation Of Higher-order Optical Modes
authors: Claire Cisowski
abstract:
Author(s): Claire Cisowski

The author presents an octant geometric framework that maps higher-order, three-state optical modes onto the positive surface of a sphere spanned by a torus. In contrast to standard Poincaré sphere analogs that are restricted to subspaces, this parametrization covers the entire state space of structured light modes except for isolated coordinate singularities where a mode amplitude vanishes.


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063530] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents a geometric framework for representing higher-order optical modes on a sphere, extending the Poincaré sphere concept.
motivation: Standard Poincaré sphere analogs are restricted to subspaces and cannot represent the full state space of higher-order optical modes.
method: The author develops an octant geometric framework that maps three-state optical modes onto the positive surface of a sphere spanned by a torus, covering the entire state space except for isolated singularities.
result: The parametrization covers all higher-order optical modes except where a mode amplitude vanishes, providing a complete geometric representation.
conclusion: This geometric representation offers a unified way to visualize and analyze higher-order optical modes, with potential applications in structured light and classical optics.

title: Pseudo-Hermitian Symmetry Breaking And Re-entrant Localization In A One-dimensional non-Hermitian Chain
authors: Pei-Lin Wang, Ai-Bo Xia, Jun-Bo Zhao, Hong-Tao Fan, And Y. P. Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Pei-Lin Wang, Ai-Bo Xia, Jun-Bo Zhao, Hong-Tao Fan, and Y. P. Wang

Non-Hermitian systems have attracted considerable research interest due to their capacity to host unconventional physical phenomena. However, research on pseudo-Hermitian symmetry and re-entrant localization in one-dimensional non-Hermitian settings remain relatively limited. Here, we propose a one-…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063736] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies pseudo-Hermitian symmetry breaking and re-entrant localization in a one-dimensional non-Hermitian chain.
motivation: Non-Hermitian systems exhibit unconventional phenomena, but pseudo-Hermitian symmetry and re-entrant localization in 1D are underexplored.
method: The authors propose a one-dimensional non-Hermitian tight-binding model and analyze its spectral properties and localization transitions.
result: They observe pseudo-Hermitian symmetry breaking and re-entrant localization as system parameters vary.
conclusion: The work reveals new localization physics in non-Hermitian systems, but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Quantum Simulation Of Fermionic non-Abelian Lattice Gauge Theories In $(2+1)$ Dimensions With Built-in Gauge Protection
authors: Gaia de Paciani, Lukas Homeier, Jad C. Halimeh, Monika Aidelsburger, And Fabian Grusdt
abstract:
Author(s): Gaia De Paciani, Lukas Homeier, Jad C. Halimeh, Monika Aidelsburger, and Fabian Grusdt

Recent advancements in the field of quantum simulation have significantly expanded the potential for applications, particularly in the context of lattice gauge theories (LGTs). Maintaining gauge invariance throughout a simulation remains a central challenge, especially for large-scale non-Abelian LG…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063327] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a quantum simulation scheme for non-Abelian lattice gauge theories in (2+1) dimensions with built-in gauge protection.
motivation: Simulating non-Abelian lattice gauge theories on quantum devices is challenging due to gauge violations; the authors aim to design a scheme that inherently preserves gauge invariance.
method: They introduce a digital quantum simulation approach using ultracold atoms in optical lattices, incorporating a gauge protection term that suppresses gauge errors without active feedback.
result: Numerical simulations show that the scheme maintains gauge invariance with high fidelity for accessible system sizes, and the resource requirements are within reach of near-term quantum simulators.
conclusion: The proposed method offers a practical route to simulating non-Abelian gauge theories on current quantum platforms, enabling studies of confinement and other non-perturbative phenomena.

title: Optimal Displacement Detection Of Arbitrarily Shaped Levitated Dielectric Objects Using Optical Radiation
authors: Shaun Laing, Shelby Klomp, George Winstone, Alexey Grinin, Andrew Dana, Zhiyuan Wang, Kevin Seca Widyatmodjo, James Bateman, And Andrew A. Geraci
abstract:
Author(s): Shaun Laing, Shelby Klomp, George Winstone, Alexey Grinin, Andrew Dana, Zhiyuan Wang, Kevin Seca Widyatmodjo, James Bateman, and Andrew A. Geraci

Optically levitated dielectric objects are promising for precision force, acceleration, torque, and rotation sensing due to their extreme environmental decoupling. While many levitated optomechanics experiments employ spherical objects, for some applications nonspherical geometries offer advantages.…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063529] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a theoretical framework for optimal displacement detection of arbitrarily shaped levitated dielectric objects using optical radiation.
motivation: Optically levitated objects are promising for precision sensing, but existing detection methods are optimized for spherical objects; nonspherical geometries offer advantages but require generalized detection theory.
method: The authors develop a general theory for optical displacement detection of arbitrarily shaped dielectric objects in a focused laser beam, using the dipole approximation and scattering theory to compute the scattered field and detection signal.
result: They derive optimal detection strategies and show that the signal-to-noise ratio depends on the object's shape and orientation, with nonspherical objects potentially offering enhanced sensitivity.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical foundation for designing optimal detection schemes for levitated nonspherical particles, which could improve force and torque sensing.

title: Geometric Theory Of Constrained Schrödinger Dynamics With Application To Time-dependent Density-functional Theory On A Finite Lattice
authors: Éric Cancès, Théo Duez, Jari van Gog, Asbjørn Bækgaard Lauritsen, Mathieu Lewin, And Julien Toulouse
abstract:

In this work, we revisit the foundations of TDDFT within a finite-dimensional sett…

tldr: This paper develops a geometric theory of constrained Schrödinger dynamics and applies it to time-dependent density-functional theory on a finite lattice.
motivation: The mathematical foundations of TDDFT are not fully understood, especially for finite lattice systems.
method: The authors formulate the dynamics as a constrained evolution on a manifold of Slater determinants, using geometric tools to derive equations of motion.
result: They obtain a rigorous geometric framework for TDDFT on finite lattices, clarifying the role of the Runge-Gross theorem and the adiabatic connection.
conclusion: The work provides a solid mathematical foundation for TDDFT on lattices, but does not directly address quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Systematic Errors From Inhomogeneous Alkali-spin Polarization In Nmr Gyroscopes And Comagnetometers
authors: Xiangdong Zhang, Jinbo Hu, Juhao Luo, Chaohong Lee, And Nan Zhao

Isotope shift, a systematic error arising from the alkali polarization field generated by the spin-exchange collisions between the Xe and alkali-metal atoms, has been observed in many [MATH] comagnetometer studies. This isotope shift constitutes a major source of syste…

tldr: This paper analyzes systematic errors from inhomogeneous alkali-spin polarization in NMR gyroscopes and comagnetometers.
motivation: Isotope shift due to alkali polarization field is a major systematic error in comagnetometer studies, and understanding its origin is crucial for improving measurement accuracy.
method: The authors theoretically model the spin-exchange collisions between Xe and alkali-metal atoms and derive the effect of inhomogeneous alkali-spin polarization on the NMR signals.
result: They quantify the isotope shift and show how it depends on experimental parameters such as alkali density and magnetic field gradients.
conclusion: The findings provide a framework to correct for this systematic error, enhancing the precision of NMR gyroscopes and comagnetometers.

title: Ultrafast Three-dimensional Steering Of Electronic Ring Currents In Benzene: Coherent Control Of Angular Momentum
authors: Dongming Jia, Yuteng Zhou, Chunmei Liu, And Yonggang Yang
abstract:
Author(s): Dongming Jia, Yuteng Zhou, Chunmei Liu, and Yonggang Yang

Coherent control of electronic ring currents enables the steering of optomagnetic responses on femtosecond timescales. However, most existing schemes confine these currents to the molecular plane, effectively constraining the electronic angular momentum (EAM) vector to a fixed direction. Here, we de…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063115] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates coherent control of electronic ring currents in benzene to steer the electronic angular momentum vector in three dimensions on femtosecond timescales.
motivation: Existing schemes confine ring currents to the molecular plane, limiting the direction of electronic angular momentum. The authors aim to achieve full three-dimensional control.
method: Using tailored laser pulses with specific polarization and timing, they simulate the dynamics of electronic ring currents in benzene via time-dependent quantum mechanics.
result: They show that the electronic angular momentum vector can be steered in three dimensions, enabling ultrafast control of optomagnetic responses.
conclusion: This work provides a method for three-dimensional coherent control of electronic currents, with potential applications in ultrafast optomagnetism and molecular electronics.

title: Interacting Many-body non-Hermitian Systems As Markov Chains
authors: Zichang Hao, Wei Jie Chan, And Ching Hua Lee
abstract:

Rich phenomenology emerges at the intersection of non-Hermiticity and many-body dynamics, yet physically realizable implementations remain challenging. [Phys. Rev. B 114, 014301] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: Maps non-Hermitian many-body Hamiltonians to Markov chain Laplacians, revealing non-equilibrium steady states and topological properties.
motivation: Non-Hermitian many-body systems are difficult to realize physically; a mapping to Markov chains could simplify analysis and connect to stochastic processes.
method: Proposes a general formalism that maps non-Hermitian Hamiltonians to Laplacians of Markov chains, using wave-function redefinition and analyzing the resulting stochastic matrix.
result: The mapping yields non-equilibrium steady states and reveals topological features such as non-Hermitian skin effect and exceptional points in many-body systems.
conclusion: The Markov chain formalism provides a new perspective on non-Hermitian many-body physics, potentially enabling experimental realizations via classical stochastic systems.

title: Itinerant Magnetism In Hubbard Models With Long-range Interactions
authors: Johannes Dieplinger, Rhine Samajdar, And R. N. Bhatt

Motivated by these developments, here, we investigate a generalization of the Hubbard mode…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 014402] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies itinerant magnetism in Hubbard models with long-range interactions, motivated by quantum simulators.
motivation: To understand magnetic phases in generalized Hubbard models relevant to experimental platforms like quantum-dot arrays and moiré materials.
method: The authors investigate a Hubbard model with long-range interactions using analytical and numerical techniques.
result: They characterize magnetic phase diagrams and identify regimes of itinerant magnetism.

conclusion: The work contributes to understanding frustrated magnetism and electronic correlations, but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

result: They show that altermagnets can generate DC spin currents via the nonlinear spin Hall effect.
conclusion: Altermagnets provide a promising platform for light-driven spintronics.

result: The paper finds that the spiral can be distorted into a commensurate phase under certain field strengths, and provides analytical expressions for the transition.
conclusion: The work contributes to the theory of magnetic phase transitions in helical antiferromagnets, but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Rashba-driven Insights Into Molecular Excitons
authors: Hao Li, Sergei Tretiak, And Vladimir Chernyak
abstract:
Author(s): Hao Li, Sergei Tretiak, and Vladimir Chernyak

Emmanuel Rashba’s enduring influence on molecular exciton physics is reflected in several foundational concepts: excitons in the narrow-band limit, impurity-induced spectral anomalies, the giant oscillator strength of shallow impurity-bound excitons, and isotopic editing as a quantitative spectroscopic tool. Together, these insights bridge theory and experiment, guiding research in organic semiconductors, molecular aggregates, and nanoscale materials. Rashba’s vision continues to inspire modern multiscale modeling and the design of excitonic functionality in current quantum and optoelectronic materials.

tldr: This paper reviews Rashba's contributions to molecular exciton physics, focusing on narrow-band excitons, impurity-induced spectral anomalies, and isotopic editing.
motivation: To highlight Rashba's enduring influence on molecular exciton physics and its applications in organic semiconductors and nanoscale materials.
method: The paper is a review that synthesizes Rashba's foundational concepts and their impact on modern multiscale modeling and excitonic functionality design.
result: Rashba's insights bridge theory and experiment, guiding research in organic semiconductors, molecular aggregates, and nanoscale materials.
conclusion: Rashba's vision continues to inspire modern multiscale modeling and the design of excitonic functionality in quantum and optoelectronic materials.

title: Phonons And The Lattice Dynamics In Crystals With Atomic Diffusion: Concept And Application To Superionic Ices
authors: Hairui Ding, Artem R. Oganov, Haixu Cui, Jiachang Zhang, And Xiao Dong

tldr: This paper studies phonons and lattice dynamics in crystals with atomic diffusion, focusing on superionic ices.
motivation: Understanding lattice vibrations in systems with both ordered and disordered components is challenging but important for describing thermal and transport properties.

result: They demonstrate that phonon-like excitations can be defined even in the presence of diffusion, and calculate the phonon dispersion for superionic ice phases.
conclusion: The work extends phonon theory to partially disordered systems, providing insights into the lattice dynamics of superionic materials.

title: Non-self-averaging Topological Anderson Insulator
authors: Zheng-Wei Zuo And Jun-Chong Liu
abstract:

Current research on the disordered topological quantum phases primarily focuses on the uncorrelated and short-range correlated disorder regimes. These topological Anderson insulators are typically self-averaging. However, topological quantum systems with long-range correlated disorder have received …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024201] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies non-self-averaging topological Anderson insulators with long-range correlated disorder.
motivation: To understand the effects of long-range correlated disorder on topological quantum phases, which are less explored compared to uncorrelated or short-range correlated disorder.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a disordered topological system with long-range correlations, using numerical simulations to study the non-self-averaging behavior.
result: They find that the topological Anderson insulator exhibits non-self-averaging properties, meaning the conductance does not converge to a fixed value as system size increases.
conclusion: Long-range correlated disorder leads to novel non-self-averaging effects in topological Anderson insulators, which may have implications for understanding disorder in topological systems.

title: Non-Hermitian Comb Effect In Coupled Clean And Quasiperiodic Chains

motivation: Understanding localization in non-Hermitian systems with quasiperiodic potentials is of fundamental interest in condensed matter physics.
method: The authors analyze a system of non-Hermitian quasiperiodic chains coupled to a clean chain via interchain hopping, studying localization properties as a function of non-Hermiticity and coupling strength.
result: They find transitions from delocalized to intermediate phases with increasing non-Hermiticity in the weak interchain coupling limit.
conclusion: The work reveals a non-Hermitian comb effect that modifies localization behavior, contributing to the theory of non-Hermitian localization.

title: Impact Of Stealthy Hyperuniform Magnetic Impurity Configurations On Bulk Magnetism In A Two-dimensional Heisenberg Model

We investigate an antiferromagnetic quantum Heisenberg model on a square lattice with high-spin magnetic impurities to clarify how random and stealthy hyperuniform impurity configurations influence the bulk magnetic properties. [Phys. Rev. B 114, 024403] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the effect of stealthy hyperuniform magnetic impurity configurations on bulk magnetism in a 2D Heisenberg model.
motivation: To understand how different spatial arrangements of magnetic impurities influence the magnetic properties of quantum antiferromagnets.
method: The authors generate stealthy hyperuniform impurity configurations using generalized cos... and perform numerical simulations on the Heisenberg model.
result: They find that stealthy hyperuniform configurations lead to distinct bulk magnetic behavior compared to random configurations.
conclusion: The spatial distribution of impurities significantly affects the magnetic properties, with stealthy hyperuniformity offering a way to control magnetism.

motivation: Understanding collective modes in multicomponent superconductors is important for characterizing their properties, but the paper focuses on condensed matter physics without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors start from a Bogoliubov–de Gennes Hamiltonian with separable pairing interaction and derive a gauge-invariant expression for the Raman susceptibility.
result: They obtain the Raman response of collective modes, including the amplitude and phase modes, in multicomponent superconductors.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for interpreting Raman experiments on multicomponent superconductors, but does not address quantum information or thermodynamic aspects.

title: Continuum Fractons: Quantization And The Few-body Problem
authors: Ylias Sadki, Abhishodh Prakash, And S. L. Sondhi

method: The authors impose symmetries and locality to formulate a nonrelativistic quantum mechanics for dipole-conserving fractons, analyzing the few-body problem.
result: A single fracton has a vanishing Hamiltonian, leading to a spectrum of zero modes; few-body systems show unusual dynamics.
conclusion: Continuum fractons exhibit fundamentally different quantum behavior from ordinary particles, opening new directions in condensed matter physics.

title: Competitive Orders In Altermagnetic Chiral Magnons

authors: Xiaozheng Fan, Panshi Jing, Chuanguang Zhang, Junshuai Wang, Chunlan Ma, Shijing Gong, Chuanxi Zhao, Tianxing Wang, And Yipeng An

title: Reexamining The Strange Metal Charge Response With Transmission Inelastic Electron Scattering

motivation: To evaluate the accuracy and applicability of truncated Wigner and positive-P representations for modeling light-matter interactions beyond the perturbative regime.
method: Uses the Jordan-Schwinger transformation to map atomic degrees of freedom and compares the two phase-space methods under unitary and dissipative dynamics.
result: The positive-P method remains accurate for longer times and stronger nonlinearities, while the truncated Wigner approximation fails in those regimes.
conclusion: Positive-P is a reliable tool for simulating near-resonant light propagation, whereas truncated Wigner has limited applicability.

method: Numerical simulations of interaction quenches from repulsive to attractive couplings in a one-dimensional bosonic gas using many-body methods.
result: The formation and dynamics of the quantum Peregrine soliton exhibit strong correlations and deviations from mean-field predictions.
conclusion: Quantum correlations play a crucial role in the Peregrine soliton dynamics, highlighting the need for beyond-mean-field treatments.

motivation: To explore the interplay between periodic driving and quasiperiodic potentials in two dimensions, extending the Aubry-André model to a dynamical setting.
method: The authors superimpose two square-lattice potentials with a time-dependent twist angle and analyze the resulting Floquet Hamiltonian using numerical simulations.
result: They identify localization transitions and topological features, such as edge states and Chern numbers, that depend on the twist angle and driving frequency.
conclusion: Periodic twisting can induce novel localization and topological phenomena not present in static systems, offering a new platform for studying driven quantum matter.

method: The authors derive a relation between the spin splitting and multipole moments using symmetry analysis and density functional theory calculations.
result: They show that specific multipoles (e.g., octupoles) directly determine the magnitude and anisotropy of the spin splitting.
conclusion: Higher-order magnetic multipoles serve as quantitative order parameters for altermagnetic spin splitting, providing a unified framework.

method: The authors theoretically analyze a model of fractional quantum Hall systems with nonlocal confinement, examining the edge spectrum and identifying new gapless modes.
result: Conventional edge modes are replaced by gapless bulk excitations such as gravitons and quasielectrons at the boundary.
conclusion: Nonlocal confinement fundamentally alters edge physics, leading to novel gapless edge excitations.

conclusion: Time delay is a crucial factor in the aging of active matter systems, and the swarmalator model provides insights into the interplay between delay and collective behavior.

method: The author analyzes sources of uncertainty in simulation codes for strong-field QED, such as discretization and truncation errors.
result: The paper provides a framework for estimating and propagating uncertainties in predictions of strong-field QED processes.
conclusion: Quantifying theory uncertainties is essential for meaningful comparison between experiment and theory in strong-field QED.

result: They find that collisions can lead to hybrid spatiotemporal patterns and that redirection depends on swarm parameters.
conclusion: The work provides insights into controlling multiswarm systems through collision-induced redirection.

result: The method yields a variety of quasiperiodic tilings, including those with 12-fold and 8-fold rotational symmetry.
conclusion: The near-coincidence method offers a simple geometric approach to generate quasiperiodic tilings, relevant to moiré materials.

result: They show that BosonSampling with a linear number of modes remains classically hard, extending the theoretical foundation to the regime relevant for near-term experiments.
conclusion: The results validate the quantum advantage claims of photonic experiments operating in the saturated regime.

conclusion: The fuzzy sphere is a powerful tool for studying strongly coupled CFTs, and emergent supersymmetry may be a general feature of such systems.
